verseTranslations: But the Great Souls, O Arjuna! Filled with My Divine Spirit, they worship Me, they fix their minds on Me and on Me alone, for they know that I am the imperishable Source of being.
Always extolling Me, strenuous, firm in their vows, prostrating themselves before Me, they worship Me continually with concentrated devotion.
Others worship Me with full consciousness as the One, the Manifold, the Omnipresent, the Universal.
snippets.commentary:
Yoga of Supreme *Knowledge* and Supreme Secret. So far we have seen the Bhagavan has revealed the supreme secret that I pervade everything in this Jagat.

And this Jagat is supported by my Maya, my association with Prakruti. Prakruti produces all that is moving and unmoving. But I am not in the *Prakriti*.

I am not in the beings in the *Prakriti*. Those beings are in me. I am not in the Jagat, but Jagat is in me.

In other words, my *self* supports the perception of the Jagat. So the Jagat exists as long as I perceive it. This world exists for me as long as I am conscious of it.

When I'm not conscious of this Jagat, then this Jagat does not exist for me. The same way from the Supreme *Consciousness*. As long as that Supreme *Consciousness* is aware of the Jagat, that Jagat exists.

And therefore Bhagavan says that I am not in the Jagat, Jagat is in me. But then he also said that they are also not in me. The beings and things in this Jagat are also not in me.

In other words, the Jagat and the things and beings which I see in the *Prakriti*, they are not in the consciousness. The *consciousness* is not affected by this perceptions of the world outside. So Bhagawan created contradictory statements for us to understand.

Relationless relationship with Bhagavan. We are related to Bhagavan, as close to him as we are to our own selves. Because this world is created out of Bhagavan's own *self*.

Therefore I cannot be further away from him than I am from my own *self*. And that's the secret which is the Supreme Secret. Even though I am as close to him as I am to my own *self*.

But I never feel his presence. So Bhagawan said, to feel my presence you have to identify with me. People who do not identify with me.

Bhagawan is explaining in last verse, 12 he says Moga Asa, Mogha Karmanaha, Moga *Gnana* Vicheta sah. This is the reason why we are not experiencing his presence. Because we are distracted by our vain desires.

Those desires prompt us to do vain actions. Because of our vain *knowledge* who we are, we consider this body, this mind, this intellect is to be me, this limited being to be me. I'm driven by my Rajasic and Tamasic tendencies.

As we have seen, this *Maya* is the root cause of the production of this Jagat. Jagat comes into existence out of Maya. Maya has three qualities.

Sattva, *Rajas* and Tamas. Therefore everything in this Prakriti. Prakriti is nothing but the representation of *Maya* to us.

So everything in this *Prakriti* has those three qualities, Satvarajas and Dhammas. Awareness, activity and inertia. To exist in space and time, it has to have activity and inertia.

And *Sattva* is the *awareness* part of it. So everything in this Jagat has these three qualities. The permutation combination of these three qualities makes this plurality that we see like in a three color printing.

There are only three colors, but they create myriads of shades of color. We can create all kinds of pictures from the combination of those three colors. The same way, this *Prakriti* produces a variety of things and beings by permutation and combination of these three *Gunas*.

Bhagavan said that up to the level of human beings, people are just living by their instincts. All animals, plants, and aquatic life survive in the lap of Mother Nature. They are aware of their own existence.

But they are not aware of any other higher entity. Human beings are the only ones who have intellect. To realize that there got to be somebody higher than me, somebody greater than me to have the control over this world.

Having that understanding, I still don't identify with him, because *Rajas* and *Tamas* dominate. When *Sattva* is subdued by *Rajas* and *Tamas*, all my actions will be driven by those Rajasic and Tamasic tendencies. The Rajasic and Tamasic tendencies tell me that my happiness lies in this world out there.

Therefore all my efforts to achieve that happiness which is my true nature. Just like water seeks its own nature, happiness is our true nature. So we constantly seek bliss and happiness.

And therefore we work in the world outside. We never complain about why I'm feeling good today. We always complain I'm not feeling good.

Today because being good is my nature, being not feeling good is not my nature. Bhagavan said, you are not recognizing your nature because of your wrong *knowledge* about yourself. Mogha *Gnana* -- because of wrong *knowledge*, Vichetasaha -- my thinking is wrong about where my happiness lies.

I'm working outside in a Rajasic manner to acquire things, to achieve things, to get happiness. Or I say, "If I don't do anything, then I'll be happy" -- that's the Tamasic tendency. Because of these two aspects of my nature, which are predominantly Rajasic and Tamasic, I'm not identifying with him.

Bhagavan said that when he takes the human form, people do not recognize him and they avoid him, ignore him. We know everything about our own *self* and other beings, but we don't know about the divinity which is common in all of us -- the *consciousness* which is the common factor, the one thread which ties everything together in this universe. So therefore Bhagavan says Rakshasim Asuram Chaiva Prakritim Mohinim Shritaha -- by the nature of this Rajasic and Tamasic *Prakriti*, they are confused about their own *self* and about the divinity in all human beings.

In contrast, Mahatmanastumam Partha Devim Prakritim Ashritaha. In this path of evolution, everything evolves from *Tamas* to *Sattva*. Even in the evolution of our planet, we can see that first there was nothing but just inert matter.

Then came the organic life. Then gradually it evolved into more complex life, more intelligent life. So everything evolves from inertia to *knowledge*, from Tamas to *Sattva*.

Some are in the path of evolution at Tamasic level, but they are on the path of their own evolution. So next step is Rajas to be Rajasic. So in our *self* unfoldment, when you introspect and see what you find, if you find Tamasic quality, then replace it by Rajasic quality.

If you find Rajasic tendencies, replace them by Sattvic tendencies. So this is a conscious effort. As a human being, we have our *freedom* to choose how to behave.

So Bhagavan said, those Mahatmas who have evolved to *Sattva*, even Mahatma has Rajasic and Tamasic tendencies. But they're subdued by Sattvic tendencies. In other cases, the Rajasic tendencies are subduing the Sattvic tendency.

Here the Sattvic tendencies are subduing the Rajasic and Tamasic tendencies. Devim Prakritim Ashritaha -- the Sattvic is considered the Devi, the divine quality, closer to reality. Bhajantim Ananya Manasaha -- knowing fully well that I am not this bundle of matter, not this mind, not this intellect.

Even though I'm pulled by the tendencies of body, mind, and intellect. I'm constantly reminding myself I'm part of this all pervading *consciousness*. My consciousness is same as *consciousness* in all other being.

Bhajanti Ananya Manasa not having any other thought. Even though I'm functioning in the world like everybody else. But that thought is constant in my mind that I am the divine being at the core of my being.

I am that supreme self, the all pervading *consciousness*. Knowing that Gnatva Bhuta dim avyam I am part of that immutable *self* which is all pervading. So we have discussed this example before.

The space in my car or my car is in this space. The car is in the space. Space is not in the car.

The space seems divided in different cars in different rooms. But it is not really divided. Otherwise the car cannot move in the space -- it would have Henrico space when it is in Henrico, Hanover space when it's in Hanover County.

Gnatva Bhutadim Avyayam -- the *self* in me and the *self* in you are not two divided selves. The *self* in all beings is one. The *consciousness* which makes the entire Jagat possible is undivided.

It's not that my consciousness is different than your *consciousness*. Your equipment, my equipment are different. And therefore our manifest representations are different.

So Bhagavan says Mahatma. One who has evolved to that level of understanding that the self is undivided and all beings are existing in that *consciousness*. Bhajanti Ananyamanah he devotes himself to me without any other thought, constantly with a single pointed *devotion*.

There is no other doubt. There is no other identification. Even though he realizes that he is an individual functioning as this body, mind, intellect.

But that is only possible because the *consciousness* functioning. We know this body is inert because we have seen dead bodies. Dead body cannot function when the *consciousness* is not there.

Therefore we come to the conclusion that the body is inert. Body is nothing but made up of food which I have eaten all my life. But I am a conscious being.

Therefore my real identity is the *consciousness* and not this body. This Mahatma has come to this level of understanding. Therefore he is constantly devoting himself to that true *self* which is the *consciousness*.

Satatam, Kirta, Yanthamam, Yatantaschadravrataha. He is constantly doing kirtan to me. He is constantly praising me.

So we obviously kirtan, bhajan, kirtan. We hear these words in our day to day conversation. In our culture, bhajan is when we are thinking about the Lord; kirtan is when we are praising the Lord.

But here, the praise and thinking about the Lord carry a very different connotation. When I am praising the Lord, I am devoted to the Lord. *Devotion* is love for the Divine. Our love for the Divine becomes *devotion*, and love is nothing but identification.

When I identify with something or someone, I love that thing or that person. I love my BMW because I identify with my BMW. When I identify with the Lord as my Lord, then I devote myself to Him.

This *devotion* is nothing but my identification with the Lord. And therefore that kirtan -- kirtan is not that one Sunday afternoon or Saturday evening we get together, and, the noisy kirtan we do with equally noisy equipment. Kirtan is a constant thought in my mind that I am not this limited being, and my Lord is not divided into separate beings.

We all exist in his own being. We are only existing because he exists. I am only alive because the *consciousness* is functioning through me.

When the *consciousness* will not be there, I will be purely as just a bundle of matter. They will call it dead body and get rid of it as quickly as possible. Satatam Yatantascha Dridavrataha.

They are constantly striving, because they will be pulled by this *Prakriti* to identify with it -- to identify with my body, to go out and get things, to fall in love with things and beings outside. I have to constantly remind myself; therefore it's Yatantaha. So once you get this *knowledge* from the books or from a guru, you're not done with it.

That's just the beginning. Now you have to constantly remember it with everything you do. Constant efforts are required for even Mahatmas.

Dridavrataha -- they are steadfastly established in this *knowledge*. There is never a doubt that this is not true. Some of us read this, then read another book, and start doubting whether this is right or that is right.

One says there is Ishvara; another says there is no Ishvara. One path says there is no life after death.
snippets.reflection:
The Mahatmas (great souls) are distinguished not by external achievements but by their inner orientation. They have taken refuge in the Daivi Prakriti - the divine nature of Sattva, truth, and awareness. While functioning in the world like everyone else, they maintain unwavering recognition that their true identity is not the body-mind but the all-pervading consciousness. Like the actor Amitabh Bachchan who never forgets he is Amitabh while playing a coolie, the Mahatma never loses awareness of the Self while playing worldly roles.

"Bhajanti ananya manasah" - they worship with single-pointed mind, with no other thought. This is not about excluding worldly duties, but about the constant background awareness that "I am the divine being at the core of my existence." Such devotion is identification - the more you identify with something, the more you love it. The Mahatma identifies with the imperishable Self (bhutadim avyayam) that is the same in all beings. Just as the space in your car is not separate from space everywhere, consciousness in you is not separate from universal consciousness.

Krishna describes three approaches to this truth: seeing the Divine as One (ekatvena - Advaita), as separate Creator and creation (prthaktvena - Dvaita), or as present everywhere with many faces (bahudha vishvatomukham). Whatever your philosophical approach, if your goal is alignment with the Supreme, you will reach it. Practice this week: Whatever draws you spiritually - prayer, meditation, service, study - pursue it with drdha-vrata (firm resolve). The path matters less than the steadfastness with which you walk it.
snippets.shortReflection: You already have one thing you pursue with absolute devotion—check your actions, not your words. Your bank account, your body, your career, your family? The question isn't whether to be devoted, but to what.

snippets.title: Day 121: Father, Mother, Seed
snippets.sanskrit:
अहं क्रतुरहं यज्ञः स्वधाऽहमहमौषधम् |
मंत्रोऽहमहमेवाज्यमहमग्निरहं हुतम् ||

पिताऽहमस्य जगतो माता धाता पितामहः |
वेद्यं पवित्रमोंकार ऋक् साम यजुरेव च ||

गतिर्भर्ता प्रभुः साक्षी निवासः शरणं सुहृत् |
प्रभवः प्रलयः स्थानं निधानं बीजमव्ययम् ||
snippets.transliteration:
ahaṁ kratur ahaṁ yajñaḥ svadhāham aham auṣhadham
mantro ’ham aham evājyam aham agnir ahaṁ hutam

pitāham asya jagato mātā dhātā pitāmahaḥ
vedyaṁ pavitram oṁkāra ṛik sāma yajur eva cha

gatir bhartā prabhuḥ sākṣhī nivāsaḥ śharaṇaṁ suhṛit
prabhavaḥ pralayaḥ sthānaṁ nidhānaṁ bījam avyayam
verseTranslations: I am the Oblation, the Sacrifice and the Worship; I am the Fuel and the Chant, I am the Butter offered to the fire, I am the Fire itself, and I am the Act of offering.
I am the Father of the universe and its Mother; I am its Nourisher and its Grandfather; I am the Knowable and the Pure; I am Om; and I am the Sacred Scriptures.
I am the Goal, the Sustainer, the Lord, the Witness, the Home, the Shelter, the Lover and the Origin; I am Life and Death; I am the Fountain and the Seed Imperishable.
snippets.commentary:
From chapters one through six we have seen who I am and how I should work in this world with the Spirit of Yajna. Because those actions are not binding.

All others are binding. Then we have looked in chapter seven, the lower nature of the supreme, that which is manifest all around me. And then in chapter eight we have seen his higher nature which is unmanifest, supporting all the beings.

The secret still is what is my relationship with him is the secret. Having known all that, I still cannot find how I can relate to Him. So now chapter nine gives us the indication of what is your relationship with the Supreme? The Bhagavan, the Almighty, my Creator.

So in the beginning he said that my relationship to this *prakriti* which you are part of it. I'm trying to find out my relationship with Him. I already learned in chapter 8 that I'm nothing but a part of this manifest world.

Therefore I'm nothing but a *prakriti*. See, my relationship to this manifest world, Bhagavan said, is that of a relationship less relation. So he said that this entire Jagat of moving and unmoving is pervaded by me and presided by me, Adiyakshaina.

I keep eye on it, but I don't take part in it. This Jagat is in me, but I'm not in them. They are also not in.

From my perspective, from the perspective of the supreme, this Jagat does not exist and therefore it is not in me. So therefore he says, this relationship of this Prakriti and the supreme is that of no relationship but a perceived relationship. Relationship which can be associated with each other but have no real association.

This entire Jagat is pervaded by me and Chara Nachar, moving and unmoving. I send them forth by my *yoga* Maya. At the beginning of the cycle I send those multitude of beings.

Same multitude of beings will merge into me at the end of the cycle. And again they will start all over again. Those who do not recognize this fact because of their limited understanding of the nature of the supreme, they try to find the perfection which truly belongs to the supreme through Mogasa, Moga Karma.

By the vain desires and vain actions. I'm trying to achieve something which can only be achieved at the level of perfection. I'm trying to achieve it with my little efforts here and there.

Bhagavan says, therefore they cannot achieve it. But then there are others who recognize this fact that if my goal is that high, then I have to align myself with that high of an entity. The one who truly have these qualities.

How do you do strategic planning? You align your capabilities with the opportunities. When you combine the two, that's your strategy. But if I don't have capabilities and I just keep looking at opportunities, that's not really a strategy.

My strategy in life is to get perfect happiness. I see opportunity there -- there's got to be somewhere, a state where I can be happy all the time. What I miss out on is: am I capable? So I am not really aligning these two.

I have two different entities -- one who is very limited in capability, trying to achieve something which is highly unachievable through limited means. Bhagavan said that those who recognize this align themselves with the supreme. They focus single-pointedly to identify themselves with that supreme who is pervading everywhere.

And to do that, they use different methods. Different people use different methods. Once they recognize the fact that the perfect happiness is not achievable by actions in this world of Prakriti -- the world of objects, emotions and thoughts as shown in 's BMI chart -- this world can never give you the perfect happiness, no matter how hard you try.

They align with the supreme, the work in this world. But their goal is aligned with the Mahatmas. Those great souls who realize that perfect happiness can only be found by aligning with one who is perfect.

They achieve that in many different ways. Some consider him to be only one -- the one that exists and nothing else can exist. And as we have seen in our three schools of thought, that's Advaita.

I and him are no different from each other. I am under the spell of Maya. That's the only difference.

Some see it as divided into many. So at least it's more than one -- Creator and creation. These two, some believe, will never be able to coincide with each other.

Creation will always remain creation, Creator will always remain Creator. From that perspective also people can reach Him. Or I say bahudha vishvatomukham.

He is everywhere, in everything I see. And every being I see is him alone. Every eye I see, every leg I see, every mouth I see -- it's all his expressions.

Others see it that way, as we have seen in Vishishtadvaita. He is the whole and what I see is just a part. I have a narrow perspective on life.

Therefore I cannot see him in his complete glory. But wherever I see, I see his glimpse. That's Visheshta Advaita.

So Bhagavan said, any which way you can approach me, it is all coming to me only. Because I am everything. If you pay money to Chinmaya Mission, whether at this center or any other center, eventually it all goes to Chinmaya Mission.

It really doesn't matter. Any efforts you put in aligning yourself with the supreme, in whatever manner -- whether it's Advaita, Dvaita, or Vishishtadvaita -- seeing him as father, mother, brother, supporter. And therefore they will be successful as long as they align with me in any which way.

Because that's all coming to me. Because I am the father of this entire Jagat -- Mata Dhata Pitamaha. As we have said, I am also mother, sustainer, grandfather.

Vedyam, Pavitram, Omkaram. I am that which is indicated in the Vedas as the supreme reality, as Om, which encompasses all four states of existence. Three which I am very aware which is my dream world, deep sleep and waking world.

In the fourth one which supports all these three, he said that's indicated by Om. Therefore whatever is indicated in the Rukh Saam and Yajuho in these books of knowledge about his nature. Any which way you approach me is acceptable.

You will reach me as long as your goal is to reach me. Gatihi Bharata Prabhuhu Sakshi Nivasah Bhagawan Vidyas uses the approach sometimes. I tell our young architects: it has to be idiot-proof.

Consider your contractor the greatest fool on this planet, and then do your documents. That way you will not make the mistake of him misunderstanding you. Make it so clear, so obvious that you hit the lowest denominator.

Bhagavan through Vedavyasa doesn't want to leave anything out. In case you missed it in Pitahamasya Jagato Mata Dhata -- now he adds Gatihi. I am the goal Bharata.

I am the supporter Prabhu. I am the Lord Saksihi. Anything that is happening in this world, I am the witness.

You may think that when you are doing something bad, nobody is seeing. But Bhagavan is watching that. Because Bhagavan is every including your own self.

It means you will know what you have done. Therefore I am always witness as you. I am the refuge when I am in trouble.

I'm actually invoking my own capacity to overcome my difficulties. We have talked about many times. Friend is a very special relationship.

In any other relationship, I have to be correct in my behavior and approach for that relationship to work. But friends? Any which way we meet after a long time, they curse each other and do all the funny things, hit each other. A friend is one who supports you no matter how wrong you are.

Anytime I want to do something and I tell my friend Deepak, "I'm trying to do this," he says, "That's not a good idea." I say, "No, but that will be fun in the end." He says, "Okay, then if you really want to do it, let's go and do it." Just before exams, we did this all the time. I'd say, "Deepak, let's go see a movie." He'd say, "But tomorrow you have an exam." I'd say, "I think I can make it up." And in the end he would say, "Okay, then let's go." A friend will support you even when you are wrong, even if he knows you are going down the wrong path and going to suffer through it. Bhagavan says, "I am that friend.

Anytime you do something wrong, I know." I am telling you as your conscience. Still you want to do it? I am the beginning and the end. Sthanam -- also the place where you exist, the support.

For anything to exist in space and time, you need inertia. Bhagavan says, I am the Sthanam, that space where you exist. I'm also the treasure house.

When I need knowledge -- O Bhagavan, O Saraswati Mata, Saraswati Puja. I want wealth -- Lakshmi Mata. I am afraid -- Hanuman Ji or Durga Mata.

Whatever you want. I am the treasure house of anything you want. We have discussed this concept before.

I am the source, the seed. But very different than any other source which we know. Every other source will be depleted once you exercise it.

That source will be depleted. That's why worried about this. Fossil fuel will be depleted or any seed.

Once you use that seed and the tree comes out, the seed is destroyed. Immutable seed, the tree will come out or whatever the product. I still remain intact.

Therefore any method which you apply is still coming to me. I am the one who bakes you as the sun. Aham Varsam, I rain down as rains.

Nigruhani Utsradami I also hold and I also throw you out. I send you back Amrutham Chaya. None of us will ever have any experience of not existing.

Not a single being has ever existed in this universe who has the experience of not existing. We assume we will not exist because Gandhiji is not here, my father is not here. So it's an assumed position that I will not exist.

However, you can't find one person in the entire history of the human race who can say, "Yeah, I know what it means to not exist." Because everyone is only there when they think they are existing. Amritam -- immortality. Cha Eva Mrityustra -- and also death.

The death which I see decaying every day. Death and decay which I see. I as a baby have died and become a toddler.

Toddler died and became a boy. And boy died, became a young man. A young man died into the old man.

And now I think my next stage is not existing. I'm constantly seeing death. Bhagawan says that's also me.

Sat, Asatya Aham Arjuna. O Arjuna in the head and Sat, that which is existing as real and also Asat that which is unreal. So Sat can be viewed in many different ways.

That which is temporary is Asat. That which is permanent is Sat. That which is cause is Sat.

That which we see as effect is Asat. Everything in this world is nothing but an effect of a cause. The cause remains intact throughout all the variations and modifications of the effect.

Standard examples we have seen are that of gold and gold bangles. I also use the example of space: space is Sat; all conditioned spaces -- room space, cathedral space, casino space -- are Asat.
snippets.reflection:
In these verses, Krishna declares: "I am the ritual, the sacrifice, the offering, the fire, and the act of offering" (aham kratur aham yajnah). He is not just one element of worship - He is every element. This reveals a profound truth: in any spiritual practice, the worshipper, the worshipped, and the act of worship are all expressions of the same reality. There is no separation between subject, object, and action. When you offer a prayer, who is praying to whom? The consciousness in you reaches toward... consciousness itself.

"I am the Father, Mother, Grandfather, Sustainer of the universe" (pitaham asya jagato mata dhata pitamahah). Whatever role you seek the Divine in, that role is fulfilled. "I am the Goal, the Supporter, the Lord, the Witness, the Abode, the Refuge, the Friend" (gatir bharta prabhuh sakshi nivasah saranam suhrt). Notice especially "suhrt" - the friend. A friend supports you even when you are wrong, unlike other relationships that demand correct behavior. The Divine is that friend who accompanies you through every mistake, never abandoning you.

Most remarkably, Krishna says: "I am the imperishable seed" (bijam avyayam). Unlike ordinary seeds that are destroyed when they sprout, the Divine remains unchanged though the entire universe emerges from it. This week, contemplate: What remains unchanged through all your life's transformations - childhood to adulthood, joy to sorrow, health to illness? That unchanging witness-awareness is the avyaya bija, the imperishable seed that is your true identity and the source of all.
snippets.shortReflection: When you pray, who is praying to whom? The consciousness in you is reaching toward itself. Notice how in any act of devotion, you are both the seeker and what you seek—there's no separation, only the illusion of it.

snippets.title: Day 122: The Cycle of Heaven
snippets.sanskrit:
तपाम्यहमहं वर्षं निगृह्णाम्युत्सृजामि च |
अमृतं चैव मृत्युश्च सदसच्चाहमर्जुन ||

त्रैविद्या मां सोमपाः पूतपापा यज्ञैरिष्ट्वा स्वर्गतिं प्रार्थयन्ते |
ते पुण्यमासाद्य सुरेन्द्रलोक मश्नन्ति दिव्यान्दिवि देवभोगान् ||

ते तं भुक्त्वा स्वर्गलोकं विशालं क्षीणे पुण्ये मर्त्यलोकं विशन्ति |
एव त्रयीधर्ममनुप्रपन्ना गतागतं कामकामा लभन्ते ||
snippets.transliteration:
tapāmyaham ahaṁ varṣhaṁ nigṛihṇāmyutsṛijāmi cha
amṛitaṁ chaiva mṛityuśh cha sad asach chāham arjuna

trai-vidyā māṁ soma-pāḥ pūta-pāpā
yajñair iṣhṭvā svar-gatiṁ prārthayante
te puṇyam āsādya surendra-lokam
aśhnanti divyān divi deva-bhogān

te taṁ bhuktvā swarga-lokaṁ viśhālaṁ
kṣhīṇe puṇye martya-lokaṁ viśhanti
evaṁ trayī-dharmam anuprapannā
gatāgataṁ kāma-kāmā labhante
verseTranslations: I am the Heat of the Sun, I release and hold back the Rains. I am Death and Immortality; I am Being and Not-Being.

Those who are versed in the scriptures, who drink the mystic Soma-juice and are purified from sin, but who while worshipping Me with sacrifices pray that I will lead them to heaven; they reach the holy world where lives the Controller of the Powers of Nature, and they enjoy the feasts of Paradise.

Yet although they enjoy the spacious glories of Paradise, nevertheless, when their merit is exhausted, they are born again into this world of mortals. They have followed the letter of the scriptures, yet because they have sought but to fulfill their own desires, they must depart and return again and again.
snippets.commentary:
Who is that that I'm seeking is that you are that. So that paradigm shift about the one I'm seeking is not away from me, but my own *self*. And then we obviously have seen that the one which I consider myself me is just an equipment which I use to transact with this world. What I consider myself with this body, this mind, this intellect.

In chapter two we have this paradigm shift that that's not you. That's actually a vehicle you use to transact with this world. But you are imperishable, immutable, unborn, never dying. That's a paradigm shift we have learned in the in the second chapter then we also learned about the *karma* *yoga* act. I must as an individual in this world. So I do not perpetuate this ignorance I have about myself.

So we all learned about *karma* *yoga*. Selfless actions will purify my mind and intellect, the internal instrument so that I'll be able to see the reality as is where myself then the universal self has no duality. It is something similar to my room space. Right now I see is completely separated from the outside. But from another developer who wants to build a big building, this space is part of the space outside. And then obviously we have seen how to get the Karma Sanyas renunciation in actions by knowledge.

By knowing that I am not the doer, I can renounce my actions. I right now take the doership and ownership of my actions. Except I am not really ready to face the consequences. And when the consequences come, I blame other people. World was unfair, society is unjust. People don't recognize my contribution.

All of that is simply because of my lack of understanding that I am not the doer. I have very little capacity to act on my own. I'm just a part of this whole fabric which is called this universe. And I'm just this minute part which only can function when other parts function in its own way. So there's a Gnana Karma Sanyas Yoga. Once the knowledge takes place that I am not by individual and island who is capable of acting that I give up my ownership of my actions and I start accepting my role as a part in this whole. And then we obviously see in meditation, Dhyana Yoga how to now reflect and contemplate on myself so I can wipe this ignorance out of myself.

Those are the first six chapters we learned about ourselves. We are not with who think we are. Bhagavan said, you are part of my own self. The next three chapters, 7, 8, and 9, are about "That" -- we learned about "Tat" first. "Tat" means "That" -- we learned about That. Then we said, who is That which I'm seeking as the Lord of this universe?

Therefore Lord of my own self. Bhagavan gave his identity in the last three chapters saying I am who pervades in this entire universe in my unmanifest form, I am the source of this universe. I'll be the resting place for this universe. Everything comes out of me, everything dissolves in me. But we can recognize that. So this chapter Chapter 9 says Raja Vidya Raja Guya Yoga opened with a profound statement by Bhagavan said I manifest in this entire Jagat in my unmanifest form.

But people fail to recognize it out of their own ignorance. The world is full of Mudhas. They fail to recognize because of their own different identifications, notions, desires -- Mogha Asha, Mogha Karmaha. Bhagavan said you need the right equipment to recognize something which is unmanifest. There are radio waves in this room. I'm not sure now that they've all gone digital.

But think about how analog radio waves work. Radio waves are wireless. What are the waves which make my wireless phone work? To make them manifest, I need equipment. And when that equipment is fine-tuned and pointed in the right direction, it will manifest. Yesterday I was listening to one of these Gujarati Kathas by Ramesh bhai Oza.

And I said this Samsar. We are completely surrounded by this Samsar that is constantly changing by this Maya. We are trying to find its end. Where does this Maya end? They say all over vernacular language said Sansar. You have to cross this Sansar, this ocean of Sansar.

And for that you need a boat. He said that boat, Ramesh bhai, is your body, this mind, and this intellect. It's not an ordinary boat -- it's like a luxury liner. It is fully equipped with all that you need to cross over this ocean in a very luxurious way. But we fail to recognize the goal of this boat and direct it towards other things.

So we go in circles. Our scripture says that the ultimate goal of human life is to recognize your own self, your own reality, who you really are. In this evolution from a single-cell amoeba to where we are now, we are fully equipped to realize who we are. But we fail to recognize that. Why? Traividya mam somapaha puta papa yajnaih ishtva svargantim prarthayante.

Te punya masadya surendra lokam asnanti divyan divi deva bhogan. How does this work? It works as simply as this: wherever you put your effort, whatever your goal is, that is what you will achieve. What do I want to become? We ask our little children all the time, "What do you want to become when you grow up?" "Well, I want to be a fireman."

We never let him try to become a fireman. The parents say, "Oh no, okay, that's a great idea. But no, no, you're not becoming a fireman. We are not going to let you do that." The point is: we don't always put our efforts into what we truly want to achieve. We achieve whatever we actually put our efforts into.

Now here we're not talking about people who are completely deluded and don't know what they are doing. Here are the people who we consider ourselves to be like -- people who say, "Look, I really don't need to do anything more. I'm a good man doing good things. So what else do I need to do?" And I constantly say doing good is not good enough.

The knowledge about yourself and what you're trying to achieve is very important before you start any action. So here it says traividya. Those who are expert in three Vedas, those who have learned three Vedas -- they are knowledgeable people. They have jnana in the Vedas. They are somapaha -- puta papa.

Somapaha means one who has drunk that soma drink. The soma drink was offered into the Agni, and then as prasad, you take it in a small quantity at the end of the Yajna. It indicates that the ritual is over and I'm taking whatever came out of this Yajna. Just like when you go to the temple, at the end of the Aarti, Panditji is standing there distributing the Charnamrit. It basically indicates that the performing of the Puja is over. That's the conclusion of my actions.

And I'm taking whatever will come out of the action. They are also purified of the sins. They don't have any evil qualities. They are not evil doers. They are the Veda knowers. They have done the rituals as indicated in the Vedas.

They are free from sins. Yajnaih Ishtva Svargantim Prarthayante. Having performed this sacrifice of the Yajna, what does their desire say? They want to achieve heaven. Anything good we do -- what is the ultimate goal? I am doing this Puja, I am doing these actions.

In the end what we want is heaven. I can have all the good things in life and no sorrows. So Swarganti Parthayanti, the Purnya Masadya, Surendra Loka, Asnanti Divyan Divideva Bhagaana. So having earned all this merits of the good deeds they are doing the knowledge they have gathered from the Vedas. Vedas means the books of knowledge. So our Vedas are now expanded to many, many, many sciences.

Knowing all this, I perform actions in a field of my chosen field and ask for Swarga. O Lord, give me a situation where there is no sorrow ever, always there is happiness. So they achieve the Surendra Loka. The Loka of the Devas. The place of Devalok. And we have talked about there are various Lokas.

You know, from Go Loka to Brahma Loka. After all they are all in my mind. When I am in a complete control and happiness, I feel I am in heaven. Things are going right. Kids are doing fine job. Nobody is bothering me.

People are respecting me. Everybody is saying Rajan, you are doing wonderful. Meena is not complaining. Surendra Loka Hatha Bhagawan says you reach that Surendra Loka. People achieve that state of Surendra Loka, Asnanti Divya Divideva Bhogan. They're enjoying all these divine pleasures which we learn in this Purana all the time.

These Apsaras are dancing. You know, somebody is doing this. Beautiful gardens, no drought anywhere. You enjoy all the Bhogas. But then I say tetam bhuktva swargalokam vishalam Enjoying these vast heavens and vast enjoyments in the heavens. Chine punya martha lo KE vishante.

But once those punyas are exhausted -- no matter how infinite you think they are -- consider Bill Gates, the wealthiest person in this world. You can still count his wealth, can't you? We can put a number to it. An expert CPA sits down, looks at his books, and comes up with "this is your wealth." It can be spent. It may take longer than my wealth, maybe a very long time, but it can be exhausted, and it will be exhausted at some point. Bill Gates' descendants, whoever they may be, will eventually not have anything.

I remember one Gujarati poem I heard is Sagaadi tami sa alamna bhik magda shariya sah alam who was the Mughal emperor. He said, I've seen his descendants begging in the street. Saga di tam es salam na bhik makta serhiye. So any wealth, no matter how infinite seem right now, will be exhausted in time. The same applies to you. Any amount of good deeds and good merits you have done to achieve these heavenly pleasures -- you will get them according to your efforts, according to your ability.

But once you reach there and enjoy those vast heavens, at some point they will exhaust, and you're back to square one. You're going to start from where you left off. Just like going on a vacation -- at the end of the vacation, you are back to square one, working for another 50 weeks to earn two weeks of vacation again. Evam Trayi Dharmam Anuprapanna Gatagatam Kama Kama Labhante. Thus, as described in the Vedas, they attain the state of going and coming.

I perform good actions, achieve heavens, come back, keep performing good actions, go back and coming back. Obviously we say well that's good enough for me. And Bhagawan says that's why we are stuck into it, no? Because we are so addicted to this heavens, addicted to the results of my good actions that we continue to go back and forth, go back and forth into it.
snippets.reflection:
Krishna describes people who are learned in the Vedas (traividya), who perform rituals correctly (yajnair ishtva), who are purified of sins (puta-papa) - yet they pray for heaven (svargati prarthayante). They achieve what they seek: divine pleasures in celestial realms. But here is the sobering truth - "kshine punye martya lokam vishanti" - when their merit is exhausted, they return to the mortal world. Even Bill Gates' wealth, though seemingly infinite, can be counted and eventually spent. So too, any accumulation of punya (merit), no matter how vast, will eventually deplete.

This is the cosmic trap: "gatagatam kama-kama labhante" - those driven by desires attain going and coming, an endless cycle of earning, enjoying, depleting, and returning. Like working 50 weeks for a 2-week vacation, then returning to work again, we strive for temporary heavens only to start over. We have a "luxury liner" of body-mind-intellect fully equipped to cross the ocean of samsara, yet we sail in circles, never reaching the far shore.

Honest self-assessment: What is the goal of your spiritual practice? Is it a better rebirth, a more comfortable life, heavenly rewards? These are legitimate desires, but Krishna invites you to something greater - liberation from the cycle itself. This week, examine your deepest motivations. Are you seeking temporary relief or permanent freedom? The practices may look similar externally, but the intention determines the destination. What would shift if your goal became not better experiences within the dream, but awakening from the dream altogether?
snippets.shortReflection: You've achieved what you set out to achieve, enjoyed what you wanted to enjoy. So why does satisfaction still feel temporary? What if the things you're working toward—even the good ones—are designed to run out?

snippets.transliteration:

verseTranslations: But if a man will meditate on Me and Me alone, and will worship Me always and everywhere, I will take upon Myself the fulfillment of his aspiration, and I will safeguard whatsoever he shall attain.
Even those who worship the lesser Powers, if they do so with faith, they thereby worship Me, though not in the right way.
I am the willing recipient of sacrifice, and I am its true Lord. But these do not know me in truth, and so they sink back.
snippets.commentary:
Who is that that I'm seeking is that you are that. So that paradigm shift about the one I'm seeking is not away from me, but my own *self*. And then we obviously have seen that the one which I consider myself me is just an equipment which I use to transact with this world. What I consider myself with this body, this mind, this intellect.

In chapter two we have this paradigm shift that that's not you. That's actually a vehicle you use to transact with this world. But you are imperishable, immutable, unborn, never dying. That's a paradigm shift we have learned in the in the second chapter then we also learned about the *karma* *yoga* act. I must as an individual in this world. So I do not perpetuate this ignorance I have about myself.

So we all learned about *karma* *yoga*. Selfless actions will purify my mind and intellect, the internal instrument so that I'll be able to see the reality as is where myself then the universal self has no duality. It is something similar to my room space. Right now I see is completely separated from the outside. But from another developer who wants to build a big building, this space is part of the space outside. And then obviously we have seen how to get the Karma Sanyas renunciation in actions by knowledge.

By knowing that I am not the doer, I can renounce my actions. I right now take the doership and ownership of my actions. Except I am not really ready to face the consequences. And when the consequences come, I blame other people. World was unfair, society is unjust. People don't recognize my contribution.

All of that is simply because of my lack of understanding that I am not the doer. I have very little capacity to act on my own. I'm just a part of this whole fabric which is called this universe. And I'm just this minute part which only can function when other parts function in its own way. So there's a Gnana Karma Sanyas Yoga. Once the knowledge takes place that I am not by individual and island who is capable of acting that I give up my ownership of my actions and I start accepting my role as a part in this whole. And then we obviously see in meditation, Dhyana Yoga how to now reflect and contemplate on myself so I can wipe this ignorance out of myself.

Those are the first six chapters we learned about ourselves. We are not with who think we are. Bhagavan said, you are part of my own self. The next three chapters, 7, 8, and 9, are about "That" -- we learned about "Tat" first. "Tat" means "That" -- we learned about That. Then we said, who is That which I'm seeking as the Lord of this universe?

Therefore Lord of my own self. Bhagavan gave his identity in the last three chapters saying I am who pervades in this entire universe in my unmanifest form, I am the source of this universe. I'll be the resting place for this universe. Everything comes out of me, everything dissolves in me. But we can recognize that. So this chapter Chapter 9 says Raja Vidya Raja Guya Yoga opened with a profound statement by Bhagavan said I manifest in this entire Jagat in my unmanifest form.

But people fail to recognize it out of their own ignorance. The world is full of Mudhas. They fail to recognize because of their own different identifications, notions, desires -- Mogha Asha, Mogha Karmaha. Bhagavan said you need the right equipment to recognize something which is unmanifest. There are radio waves in this room. I'm not sure now that they've all gone digital.

But think about how analog radio waves work. Radio waves are wireless. What are the waves which make my wireless phone work? To make them manifest, I need equipment. And when that equipment is fine-tuned and pointed in the right direction, it will manifest. Yesterday I was listening to one of these Gujarati Kathas by Ramesh bhai Oza.

And I said this Samsar. We are completely surrounded by this Samsar that is constantly changing by this Maya. We are trying to find its end. Where does this Maya end? They say all over vernacular language said Sansar. You have to cross this Sansar, this ocean of Sansar.

And for that you need a boat. He said that boat, Ramesh bhai, is your body, this mind, and this intellect. It's not an ordinary boat -- it's like a luxury liner. It is fully equipped with all that you need to cross over this ocean in a very luxurious way. But we fail to recognize the goal of this boat and direct it towards other things.

So we go in circles. Our scripture says that the ultimate goal of human life is to recognize your own self, your own reality, who you really are. In this evolution from a single-cell amoeba to where we are now, we are fully equipped to realize who we are. But we fail to recognize that. Why? Traividya Mam Somapaha Puta Papa Yajnaih Ishtva Svargantim Prarthayante.

Te Punya Masadya Surendra Lokam Asnanti Divyan Divi Deva Bhogan. How does this work? It works as simply as this: wherever you put your effort, whatever your goal is, that is what you will achieve. What do I want to become? We ask our little children all the time, "What do you want to become when you grow up?" "Well, I want to be a fireman."

We never let him try to become a fireman. The parents say, "Oh no, okay, that's a great idea. But no, no, you're not becoming a fireman. We are not going to let you do that." The point is: we don't always put our efforts into what we truly want to achieve. We achieve whatever we actually put our efforts into.

Now here we're not talking about people who are completely deluded and don't know what they are doing. Here are the people who we consider ourselves to be -- people who say, "Look, I really don't need to do anything more. I'm a good man doing good things. So what else do I need to do?" And I constantly say doing good is not good enough.

The knowledge about yourself and what you're trying to achieve is very important before you start any action. So here it says traividya. Those who are expert in three vedas, those who have learned three vedas, they are knowledgeable people. They have jnana of the Vedas. They are soma paha -- puta papa.

One who has drunk that soma drink. The soma drink was offered into the Agni, and then as prasad, you take it in a small quantity at the end of the Yajna. It indicates that the ritual is over and I'm taking whatever came out of this Yajna. Just like when you go to the temple, at the end of the Aarti, Panditji is standing there distributing the Charnamrit. It basically indicates that the performing of the Puja is over. That's the conclusion of my actions.

And I'm taking whatever will come out of the action. They are also purified of the sins. They don't have any evil qualities. They are not evil doers. They are the Veda knowers. They have done the rituals as indicated in the Vedas.

They are free from sins. Yajnaih Ishtva Svargantim Prarthayante. Having performed this sacrifice of the Yajna, what does their desire say? They want to achieve heaven. Anything good we do -- what is the ultimate goal? I am doing this Puja, I am doing these actions.

In the end what we want is heaven. I can have all the good things in life and no sorrows. So Swarganti Parthayanti, the Purnya Masadya, Surendra Loka, Asnanti Divyan Divideva Bhagaana. So having earned all this merits of the good deeds they are doing the knowledge they have gathered from the Vedas. Vedas means the books of knowledge. So our Vedas are now expanded to many, many, many sciences.

Knowing all this, I perform actions in a field of my chosen field and ask for Swarga. O Lord, give me a situation where there is no sorrow ever, always there is happiness. So they achieve the Surendra Loka. The Loka of the Devas. The place of Devalok. And we have talked about there are various Lokas.

You know, from Go Loka to Brahma Loka. After all they are all in my mind. When I am in a complete control and happiness, I feel I am in heaven. Things are going right. Kids are doing fine job. Nobody is bothering me.

People are respecting me. Everybody is saying Rajan, you are doing wonderful. Meena is not complaining. Surendra Loka Hatha Bhagawan says you reach that Surendra Loka. People achieve that state of Surendra Loka, Asnanti Divya Divideva Bhogan. They're enjoying all these divine pleasures which we learn in this Purana all the time.

These Apsaras are dancing. You know, somebody is doing this. Beautiful gardens, no drought anywhere. You enjoy all the Bhogas. But then I say tetam bhuktva swargalokam vishalam Enjoying these vast heavens and vast enjoyments in the heavens. Chine punya martha lo KE vishante.

But once those punyas are exhausted -- no matter how infinite you think they are -- consider Bill Gates, the wealthiest person in this world. You can still count his wealth, can't you? We can put a number to it. An expert CPA sits down, looks at his books, and comes up with "this is your wealth." It can be spent. It may take longer than my wealth, maybe a very long time, but it can be exhausted, and it will be exhausted at some point. Bill Gates' descendants, whoever they may be, will eventually not have anything.

I remember one Gujarati poem I heard is Sagaadi tami sa alamna bhik magda shariya sah alam who was the Mughal emperor. He said, I've seen his descendants begging in the street. Saga di tam es salam na bhik makta serhiye. So any wealth, no matter how infinite seem right now, will be exhausted in time. The same applies to you. Any amount of good deeds and good merits you have done to achieve these heavenly pleasures -- you will get them according to your efforts, according to your ability.

But once you reach there and enjoy those vast heavens, at some point they will exhaust, and you're back to square one. You're going to start from where you left off. Just like going on a vacation -- at the end of the vacation, you are back to square one, working for another 50 weeks to earn two weeks of vacation again. Evam Trayi Dharmam Anuprapanna Gatagatam Kama Kama Labhante. Thus, as described in the Vedas, they attain the state of going and coming.

I perform good actions, achieve heavens, come back, keep performing good actions, go back and coming back. Obviously we say well that's good enough for me. And Bhagawan says that's why we are stuck into it, no? Because we are so addicted to this heavens, addicted to the results of my good actions that we continue to go back and forth, go back and forth into it.
snippets.reflection:
Verse 22 contains one of the most reassuring promises in the Gita: "Tesham nityabhiyuktanam yoga-kshemam vahamy aham" - "For those who worship Me with single-pointed devotion, I personally carry their yoga (acquisition of what they lack) and kshema (preservation of what they have)." This is not about material prosperity but spiritual assurance: when you make the Divine your sole refuge, your spiritual welfare is guaranteed. You need not worry about whether you are progressing correctly - that responsibility shifts to the Lord.

Yet verse 23 adds nuance: even those who worship other deities with faith (shraddhayanvitah) are actually worshipping Krishna, though "avidhi-purvakam" - not in the proper manner. All sincere worship reaches the same destination, like tributaries flowing to the ocean. However, verse 24 warns: "na tu mam abhijananti tattvena" - they do not know Me in truth, and therefore "cyavanti te" - they fall back. The difference between temporary upliftment and permanent liberation lies in correct understanding, not just sincere feeling.

Practical inquiry: Examine where you place your deepest trust. Is it in your abilities, your relationships, your financial security? These are forms of worship too - whatever you depend upon most is your functional deity. Krishna invites you to shift that ultimate reliance to the imperishable Self. This week, when anxiety arises about outcomes, practice this surrender: "My part is to act with devotion; the yoga and kshema are not my burden to carry." Notice how this shifts your relationship with uncertainty from fear to trust.
snippets.shortReflection: Are you constantly checking if you're progressing, if you're doing it right, if you're good enough? What would change if you trusted that your growth is being taken care of—that the work is to show up, not to manage the outcome?

snippets.sanskrit:

snippets.transliteration:

bhūtāni yānti bhūtejyā yānti mad-yājino ’pi mām

verseTranslations: The votaries of the lesser Powers go to them; the devotees of spirits go to them; they who worship the Powers of Darkness, to such Powers shall they go; and so, too, those who worship Me shall come to Me.
Whatever a man offers to Me, whether it be a leaf, or a flower, or fruit, or water, I accept it, for it is offered with devotion and purity of mind.
Whatever thou doest, whatever thou dost eat, whatever thou dost sacrifice and give, whatever austerities thou practisest, do all as an offering to Me.
snippets.commentary:
Obviously we have seen, as Bhagavan said, a royal secret, a grand secret is something which is very close to us but we fail to recognize. Therefore it's a secret. So the first declaration in this chapter, Bhagawan says that even though I pervade this entire Jagat, the universe, this creation, in my unmanifest form, all the beings dwell in me, but I don't dwell in them.

They are in me, but I'm not in them. Which is obviously quite contrary to what we typically have learned all our life through all religions saying, Bhagwan, the Lord is within you. Here he said, even though I pervade the entire universe in my unmanifest form, I do not dwell in them, they dwell in Me.

Then he even further clarifies in saying, but in reality, they are also not in me. In other words, if we can take it on its face value, if we say we are in him, obviously we are influencing his being. All my qualities of limitedness and imperfection will affect Him.

And therefore he says, in reality, even they are not in Me. None of the qualities we see in this world, in the things and beings, Bhagavan Siddi does not exist in me. All the imperfections we see in this world, which we constantly wonder why Lord created this world like that.

And he says, it is not in Me. And then obviously we have continued to discuss this, the relationship of this creation and the Lord *self*. And he says, even though this world is created by my *maya*, I am the efficient cause for this world and I am also the material cause for this world.

And therefore everything comes out of me and everything goes back to me. Because there is no nothing other than him existed before this creation was created. Then nothing will exist after this creation will be dissolved.

All that was there was his own *self*. So Bhagavan said, the relationship, less relationship between the *prakriti*, the world, the manifest world as we know, and the unmanifest self which he says pervades entire Jagat, is that of a non existent relationship. But we have created this relationship.

So then we have understood that everything which we do is because of the Lord's presence. As long as I'm conscious, I can act in this world. So Bhagavan said that everything you do eventually comes to me.

I'm the only enjoyer. *consciousness* is the only enjoyer in any being. Because only time we enjoy or suffer is when we are conscious about it. So we have seen that relationship.

The Bhagavan says, everything comes out of me. Everything dissolves in me. Everything is possible because of me.

Everything can be done only with my presence. However, because of our desires and wrong identification with this limited self, we create our own world of actions and our own world of worship. Depending on my desires, I worship the Lord of my heart.

I put my efforts into the field where I want success. Bhagavan says, those who apply their efforts to fulfill their desires will be blessed to get their desires fulfilled by me. So then we have seen in detail that the worshipers of the Devas goes to the Devas.

Worshipper of the Bhutas goes to Bhutas. Worshipper of the Pitrus go to the Pitras. Deva, as we say Diva is to illumine which relates to our senses.

So whoever perceives the visual arts, excel in visual arts. Whoever perceives performing arts, excels in performing arts. So we know in this world we can prove from our own experience that wherever I put my efforts, wherever I identify myself, that's the field I'll excel.

That the success I will receive. Same way we see the Pitruloka, the cultural heritage of our ancestors. Those who value that and put efforts in that, they will achieve that.

Bhutas we have seen is the physical sciences. Science of this manifest world is Bhuta. Those who pursue that, they excel in that.

But see, all these successes are finite in nature, exist in time and space. And once you achieve that success, enjoy the fruits of it. You to come back to pursue the next desire which you have and the next success you want.

So this is the coming and going which Bhagavad Gita and Upanishad describe. We constantly achieve, things, enjoy it, come back, strive for something else, achieve that, come back, strive for something else. But Bhagavan said, the one who worships me -- and we have seen, worship is devotion, devotion is love for the Divine, love is identification -- one who starts identifying with that eternal self will achieve me.

That we have seen in the last three verses. Verse 26 actually says Patram Puspam falam toyam Yomi bhakta prayachati Tadaham bhakt Apurhat asnami prayatat Manaha. Whatsoever my devotee offer me with devotion, I accept that.

That's good enough for me. You really don't have to have elaborate resources to worship Lord. And as we discussed last time, it takes away any excuse that I may have.

Look, I'm not strong enough. I don't have enough strength or I don't have enough wealth. But once it is whatever you can offer from my own garden, whatever you can pluck and give it back to me, I'll be happy simply because I see your devotion.

What he's looking for is your intention, your devotion and your attitude. So the next verse 27 says, Yat karosi yatasnasi yat johosi dadasiyat. Now here comes the prescription.

We have seen in theory what is our relationship to the Lord? What can we do to remove this parallax between myself and his self? And then we may have an excuse saying, but I'm not capable of doing so. There is a very simple method. And you will not need anything more than what you already have.

All you have to do is change your attitude in what you do. Yat Karoshi -- whatever you do, no matter who you are: a cobbler, a weaver, a doctor, an engineer, a president -- whatever you are, whatever you are doing. Yat Ashnasi -- whatever you are receiving, eating.

View and says eating is not only what we eat through our mouth but anything we take in through our eyes, ears, and all the senses. Yat Juhoshi -- whatever you offer back to the world. Yat Dadasi -- whatever you give as charity.

Yat Tapasyasi -- whatever discipline you are following. We all follow some discipline -- I have to get up in the morning, do this, do that. We follow discipline to achieve anything.

Whatever discipline you are following to achieve what you are pursuing -- it is that simple: do not do it for yourself. Right now we are doing it for ourselves. It is very clear in my mind why I am doing this.

Rajan, why are you doing this? Well, because I want to do this. Rajan, why don't you do this? Because I don't want to do that. It's as simple as that.

So we know very clearly that all my actions are for me. For me to achieve what I want. Bhagavan says, just change that attitude and have that attitude that I'm offering.

All my actions, all my charities, all my disciplines, all that I'm receiving is to him. Because without his presence as the consciousness in me, none of these activities are possible in the first place. So who am I to take credit now when I say who am I? As I said I reside in my ego.

That "I" which resides in my ego -- if it gives up that "I" and says, "I'm only possible as long as this consciousness functions through me, and I do not know where this consciousness comes from; it must be my Lord's presence" -- then I offer all my actions to him. Bhagavan says, you will achieve myself. So that's a simple prescription.

Do not change anything that you are doing except change your attitude that you're not doing it for yourself, you're doing it for him. Therefore, when you enjoy something, he's the enjoyer. When you suffer, he's the sufferer.

You achieve something, he's the achiever. When you fail somewhere, he bears the failure. Shubha Ashubha Phalaih Evam Mokshyase -- thus you shall be freed from this bondage of Shubha and Ashubha, this bondage of labeling things as "good for me" or "not good for me." When something good for me happens, I'm very proud.

When something good doesn't happen for me, I blame everybody else other than me. He should have done this. Why didn't he tell me that? Why didn't he do that? We find everybody responsible except me.

Also it creates negative impression on my mind. Well, next time I never want to do that. I went to this organization for volunteer my services and they were not appreciative at all.

I will never do that again. So I lost a chance of doing something good in life. That bondage which is created by the impressions on my mind -- by perceiving "this is good for me" and "this is bad for me" -- you will be freed from.

You will then see clearly, without having a cataract in your vision. I went to the doctor a few weeks ago and he said, "Open your right eye." I could barely see anything, completely fuzzy. I said, "I'm fine." He said, that's because your left eye is taking over.

And he said, thank God you don't have cataract in both eyes. That's exactly what he told me. So you can imagine if you have a cataract in a vision in both your eyes, the world will be very fuzzy.

And Bhagavan said, that's where we are Right now. Because if one eye we see Subha, other we see a Subha and we have a very distorted view of this world. But once we are freed from that, you have 2020 vision of this world.

And then you will be doing exactly what is appropriate at an appropriate time. And when you do that, you know what you will achieve? So you'll be freed from by changing your attitude about everything you do. From doing it for myself to doing it for his self, I will be freed from the bondage of this is good and this is bad.

Whatever the results come from my actions, I'll say, lord, you gave me this Buddhi to do this and I did that. Now this is what you are giving me as a prasad. I'm sure you know what you're doing.

Then this must be good for me. I'm accepting it and I'm moving forward. Next step, Sannyasa, Yoga Yuktatma, Vimukto Mam Upeshasi.

You will become Sannyasa and Yoga Yuktatma. We have learned these terms in previous chapters that should I be a Sanyasi or should I be any yogi? He says sannyasi is the one who has given up the sense of agency. I am the doer that agency.

One who gives up, he is called Sannyasi., not the one who wears the saffron robe and has a long beard. One who has given up the sense of agency that I am the doer is a Sannyasi. The yogi is the one who has given up the desire for the results of the actions.

One who is given the Karma Phala is the yogi. You are established in Yoga if you have no particular desire for particular results. I will do my actions because I am not the Karma Faladatta.

I am never the actor is never in control of its results. It's always somebody else. You present a song, you present a performance.

It's not who you are going to applaud. Other people are going to applaud or other people are going to throw stones at you.
snippets.reflection:
"Yanti deva-vrata devan" - those devoted to the devas (sense pleasures, arts) go to the devas; those devoted to the pitrs (ancestors, cultural heritage) go to the pitrs; those devoted to the bhutas (physical sciences) excel there. Wherever you place your devoted attention and effort, that is what you become. This is both warning and promise: you have complete freedom to choose your destination through where you invest your identification. The question is not whether you will reach your goal, but whether your goal is worthy of your infinite potential.

Verse 26 removes all excuses: "Patram pushpam phalam toyam" - a leaf, a flower, fruit, water - the simplest offerings are accepted when given with devotion. You need not be wealthy, learned, or specially qualified. What Krishna seeks is "bhaktya prayacchati" - the devotion behind the offering, not its material value. This demolishes the ego's protest that "I'm not ready" or "I don't have enough." You have enough right now to begin.

Verse 27 provides the complete prescription: "Yat karoshi yad ashnasi yaj juhoshi dadasi yat" - whatever you do, eat, offer, give, or practice as austerity - "tat kurushva mad-arpanam" - do it as an offering to Me. This is not about adding spiritual activities to your life; it is about transforming your entire life into spiritual practice. The cobbler stitching shoes, the executive closing deals, the parent changing diapers - all becomes worship when the attitude shifts from "I do this for myself" to "I offer this to the Divine."

This week's practice: Choose one routine activity - eating, commuting, working - and consciously offer it before, during, and after. Notice: when you act as an offering rather than as the doer seeking results, how does your relationship with success and failure change?
snippets.shortReflection: Look at your calendar, your browser history, your bank statement. Where your attention and resources consistently go is what you're actually devoted to. Is that the destination you want?
