verseTranslations: So shall thy action be attended by no result, either good or bad; but through the spirit of renunciation thou shalt come to Me and be free.
I am the same to all beings. I favour none, and I hate none. But those who worship Me devotedly, they live in Me, and I in them.
Even the most sinful, if he worship Me with his whole heart, shalt be considered righteous, for he is treading the right path.
snippets.commentary:
Obviously we have seen, as Bhagavan said, a royal secret, a grand secret is something which is very close to us but we fail to recognize. Therefore it's a secret. So the first declaration in this chapter, Bhagawan says that even though I pervade this entire Jagat, the universe, this creation, in my unmanifest form, all the beings dwell in me, but I don't dwell in them.

They are in me, but I'm not in them. Which is obviously quite contrary to what we typically have learned all our life through all religions saying, Bhagwan, the Lord is within you. Here he said, even though I pervade the entire universe in my unmanifest form, I do not dwell in them, they dwell in Me.

Then he even further clarifies in saying, but in reality, they are also not in me. In other words, if we can take it on its face value, if we say we are in him, obviously we are influencing his being. All my qualities of limitedness and imperfection will affect Him.

And therefore he says, in reality, even they are not in Me. None of the qualities we see in this world, in the things and beings, Bhagavan Siddi does not exist in me. All the imperfections we see in this world, which we constantly wonder why Lord created this world like that.

And he says, it is not in Me. And then obviously we have continued to discuss this, the relationship of this creation and the Lord *self*. And he says, even though this world is created by my *maya*, I am the efficient cause for this world and I am also the material cause for this world.

And therefore everything comes out of me and everything goes back to me. Because there is no nothing other than him existed before this creation was created. Then nothing will exist after this creation will be dissolved.

All that was there was his own *self*. So Bhagavan said, the relationship, less relationship between the *prakriti*, the world, the manifest world as we know, and the unmanifest self which he says pervades entire Jagat, is that of a non existent relationship. But we have created this relationship.

So then we have understood that everything which we do is because of the Lord's presence. As long as I'm conscious, I can act in this world. So Bhagavan said that everything you do eventually comes to me.

I'm the only enjoyer. *consciousness* is the only enjoyer in any being. Because only time we enjoy or suffer is when we are conscious about it. So we have seen that relationship.

The Bhagavan says, everything comes out of me. Everything dissolves in me. Everything is possible because of me.

Everything can be done only with my presence. However, because of our desires and wrong identification with this limited self, we create our own world of actions and our own world of worship. Depending on my desires, I worship the Lord of my heart.

I put my efforts into the field where I want success. Bhagavan says, those who apply their efforts to fulfill their desires will be blessed to get their desires fulfilled by me. So then we have seen in detail that the worshipers of the Devas goes to the Devas.

Worshipper of the Bhutas goes to Bhutas. Worshipper of the Pitrus go to the Pitras. Deva, as we say Diva is to illumine which relates to our senses.

So whoever perceives the visual arts, excel in visual arts. Whoever perceives performing arts, excels in performing arts. So we know in this world we can prove from our own experience that wherever I put my efforts, wherever I identify myself, that's the field I'll excel.

That the success I will receive. Same way we see the Pitruloka, the cultural heritage of our ancestors. Those who value that and put efforts in that, they will achieve that.

Bhutas we have seen is the physical sciences. Science of this manifest world is Bhuta. Those who pursue that, they excel in that.

But see, all these successes are finite in nature, exist in time and space. And once you achieve that success, enjoy the fruits of it. You to come back to pursue the next desire which you have and the next success you want.

So this is the coming and going which Bhagavad Gita and Upanishad describe. We constantly achieve, things, enjoy it, come back, strive for something else, achieve that, come back, strive for something else. But Bhagavan said, the one who worships me -- and we have seen, worship is devotion, devotion is love for the Divine, love is identification -- one who starts identifying with that eternal self will achieve me.

That we have seen in the last three verses. Verse 26 actually says Patram Puspam falam toyam Yomi bhakta prayachati Tadaham bhakt Apurhat asnami prayatat Manaha. Whatsoever my devotee offer me with devotion, I accept that.

That's good enough for me. You really don't have to have elaborate resources to worship Lord. And as we discussed last time, it takes away any excuse that I may have.

Look, I'm not strong enough. I don't have enough strength or I don't have enough wealth. But once it is whatever you can offer from my own garden, whatever you can pluck and give it back to me, I'll be happy simply because I see your devotion.

What he's looking for is your intention, your devotion and your attitude. So the next verse 27 says, Yat karosi yatasnasi yat johosi dadasiyat. Now here comes the prescription.

We have seen in theory what is our relationship to the Lord? What can we do to remove this parallax between myself and his self? And then we may have an excuse saying, but I'm not capable of doing so. There is a very simple method. And you will not need anything more than what you already have.

All you have to do is change your attitude in what you do. Yat Karoshi -- whatever you do, no matter who you are: a cobbler, a weaver, a doctor, an engineer, a president -- whatever you are, whatever you are doing. Yat Ashnasi -- whatever you are receiving, eating.

View and says eating is not only what we eat through our mouth but anything we take in through our eyes, ears, and all the senses. Yat Juhoshi -- whatever you offer back to the world. Yat Dadasi -- whatever you give as charity.

Yat Tapasyasi -- whatever discipline you are following. We all follow some discipline -- I have to get up in the morning, do this, do that. We follow discipline to achieve anything.

Whatever discipline you are following to achieve what you are pursuing -- it is that simple: do not do it for yourself. Right now we are doing it for ourselves. It is very clear in my mind why I am doing this.

Rajan, why are you doing this? Well, because I want to do this. Rajan, why don't you do this? Because I don't want to do that. It's as simple as that.

So we know very clearly that all my actions are for me. For me to achieve what I want. Bhagavan says, just change that attitude and have that attitude that I'm offering.

All my actions, all my charities, all my disciplines, all that I'm receiving is to him. Because without his presence as the consciousness in me, none of these activities are possible in the first place. So who am I to take credit now when I say who am I? As I said I reside in my ego.

That "I" which resides in my ego -- if it gives up that "I" and says, "I'm only possible as long as this consciousness functions through me, and I do not know where this consciousness comes from; it must be my Lord's presence" -- then I offer all my actions to him. Bhagavan says, you will achieve myself. So that's a simple prescription.

Do not change anything that you are doing except change your attitude that you're not doing it for yourself, you're doing it for him. Therefore, when you enjoy something, he's the enjoyer. When you suffer, he's the sufferer.

You achieve something, he's the achiever. When you fail somewhere, he bears the failure. Shubha Ashubha Phalaih Evam Mokshyase -- thus you shall be freed from this bondage of Shubha and Ashubha, this bondage of labeling things as "good for me" or "not good for me." When something good for me happens, I'm very proud.

When something good doesn't happen for me, I blame everybody else other than me. He should have done this. Why didn't he tell me that? Why didn't he do that? We find everybody responsible except me.

Also it creates negative impression on my mind. Well, next time I never want to do that. I went to this organization for volunteer my services and they were not appreciative at all.

I will never do that again. So I lost a chance of doing something good in life. That bondage which is created by the impressions on my mind -- by perceiving "this is good for me" and "this is bad for me" -- you will be freed from.

You will then see clearly, without having a cataract in your vision. I went to the doctor a few weeks ago and he said, "Open your right eye." I could barely see anything, completely fuzzy. I said, "I'm fine." He said, that's because your left eye is taking over.

And he said, thank God you don't have cataract in both eyes. That's exactly what he told me. So you can imagine if you have a cataract in a vision in both your eyes, the world will be very fuzzy.

And Bhagavan said, that's where we are Right now. Because if one eye we see Subha, other we see a Subha and we have a very distorted view of this world. But once we are freed from that, you have 2020 vision of this world.

And then you will be doing exactly what is appropriate at an appropriate time. And when you do that, you know what you will achieve? So you'll be freed from by changing your attitude about everything you do. From doing it for myself to doing it for his self, I will be freed from the bondage of this is good and this is bad.

Whatever the results come from my actions, I'll say, lord, you gave me this Buddhi to do this and I did that. Now this is what you are giving me as a prasad. I'm sure you know what you're doing.

Then this must be good for me. I'm accepting it and I'm moving forward. Next step, Sannyasa, Yoga Yuktatma, Vimukto Mam Upeshasi.

You will become Sannyasa and Yoga Yuktatma. We have learned these terms in previous chapters that should I be a Sanyasi or should I be any yogi? He says sannyasi is the one who has given up the sense of agency. I am the doer that agency.

One who gives up, he is called Sannyasi., not the one who wears the saffron robe and has a long beard. One who has given up the sense of agency that I am the doer is a Sannyasi. The yogi is the one who has given up the desire for the results of the actions.

One who is given the Karma Phala is the yogi. You are established in Yoga if you have no particular desire for particular results. I will do my actions because I am not the Karma Faladatta.

I am never the actor is never in control of its results. It's always somebody else. You present a song, you present a performance.

It's not who you are going to applaud. Other people are going to applaud or other people are going to throw stones at you.
snippets.reflection:
Verse 28 promises liberation from "shubha-ashubha-phalaih" - the bondage created by labeling results as good or bad. Like having cataracts in both eyes, we see a fuzzy, distorted world when we constantly sort experiences into favorable and unfavorable. The sannyasa-yoga described here is not about external renunciation but internal freedom: sannyasi is one who gives up the sense of doership; yogi is one who gives up attachment to specific results. When both are achieved, you act with full engagement yet remain untouched by outcomes - not through suppression but through understanding.

"Samo'ham sarva-bhuteshu" (verse 29) - "I am the same to all beings." The Divine has no favorites. Like a parent whose love for all children is equal (even if one visits more often), Krishna's relationship with every being is identical. The difference we experience is not in His giving but in our receiving. "Ye bhajanti tu mam bhaktya, mayi te teshu chapy aham" - those who worship with devotion dwell in Him, and He in them. The intimacy is not one-sided; it is mutual. You are not reaching toward a distant God; you are recognizing the God who has never left.

Verse 30 offers radical hope: "Api chet su-duracharo" - even the worst sinner, if they worship with undivided devotion, should be considered righteous (sadhur eva). This is not endorsement of wrongdoing but acknowledgment that right resolve changes everything. Your past does not define your future; your present orientation does. Today, release any sense that you are disqualified from spiritual progress due to past mistakes. Ask: "Am I now, in this moment, rightly resolved toward truth?" That is the only question that matters.
snippets.shortReflection: You label every email as urgent or not urgent, every conversation as good or bad. What if this constant sorting is the real exhaustion? The event itself takes five minutes; the internal commentary runs for hours.

snippets.title: Day 126: Where Happiness Lies
snippets.sanskrit:

kṣhipraṁ bhavati dharmātmā śhaśhvach-chhāntiṁ nigachchhati
kaunteya pratijānīhi na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśhyati

verseTranslations: He shall attain spirituality ere long, and Eternal Peace shall be his. O Arjuna! Believe me, My devotee is never lost.
For even the children of sinful parents, and those miscalled the weaker sex, and merchants, and labourers, if only they will make Me their refuge, they shall attain the Highest.
What need then to mention the holy Ministers of God, the devotees and the saintly rulers? Do thou, therefore, born in this changing and miserable world, do thou too worship Me.
snippets.commentary:
Yoga of Royal *knowledge* and Royal Secret.

And obviously the question last time, what is this secret? Well, we have discussed many times, the secret is, where does my happiness lie? All my life I was seeking one thing and one thing alone. That is permanent happiness and permanent peace. I have tried everywhere, I have tried in getting *knowledge*, learning things in this world.

I have tried in accomplishing things, achieving things, acquiring things in my relationships. But in the end, every happiness came with associated unhappiness. As we have learned through our life, anything which has the capacity to give me happiness has an equal capacity to give me unhappiness.

In our relationships we know exactly: the closer you are, the more chances of getting hurt. Even though we know what we are looking for and look everywhere in our life, we can't find our happiness. So that's the secret.

And whatever makes me find that will be the *knowledge* which will be royal knowledge. So Brahmagnan is the secret. Unless you have the Brahmagnaan, you will never find this permanent happiness.

And Brahma Vidya is the Raja Vidya. And why it is called Rajavidya. Raja Vidya is something which is available to all.

The road which is available to everybody, Rajmarg, anybody can pass through that road, not restricted. It is the Raja Vidya because it is available to all. So the Brahma Vidya is the Rajavidya because this *knowledge* is available to all.

Brahma Ghana is the royal sacred. Because everyone has a birthright to know that knowledge. And still none of us is capable of finding it easily.

So Bhagavan said that that is the knowledge, that is the secret. I'm going to tell you which is Pavitram Ida Muthamam. It is the highest purifier.

Once you wake up from your dream, the waking state is the highest purifier of your dream state. All your problems of the dream state go away. So we have started learning that Brahmagna is the one secret I need to unlock.

And the key is the Brahma Vidya. And therefore rest of the chapter is spent in describing what Brahman is, what is the nature of Brahman and what my relationship is with Him. So we have elaborately seen that there is nothing in this world which is other than Brahman.

In his manifest form he becomes this Prakriti, this manifestation. Anything which I see is nothing but the manifestation of the same reality. From science point of view, we have discussed the singularity at one time because of the Big Bang.

It is now a plurality and someday it will recede back into singularity again. So the same entity which is pervading everywhere is the basis of this reality as we know. And then what is my relationship? You see it's a relationship less relation that all the qualities of Brahman are in me because I am his manifestation.

I am nothing but that this world is created by the Creator out of his own self. Because there is no other material was available to Him. Only available material to create this world was his own self.

Because if you think that there is other material available then he obviously is not complete God. So we have to come to the conclusion that his self and this universe and myself is one and the same. But I just can't recognize it.

That is the Avidy which we have to dispel. So this knowledge will dispel that Avidya Bhagavan said and therefore it is Rajavidy. So we have learned the nature of the Brahman that everything is because of Brahman.

Everything resides in Brahman but Brahman does not reside in it. In other words, my limitations are not in Brahman. My ignorance is not part of Brahman.

The Creator with his power of Maya he creates this universe through the Mayapati. He is the Lord of Maya, Lord of this illusion. But I am under the spell of Maya and therefore I'm in a Maya Jal.

I'm in the web of Maya. I can't see it clearly what my self is. He said the Vidya which will take me there would be the Raja Vidya, that which dispels my ignorance about my own self.

When I start seeing my relationship clearly with him then I will be Dharmaatma. I'll be a righteous soul. So Bhagavan has talked about the why people can't see it because of the Moga Asa Mogha actions.

I'll find my happiness here, I'll find my happiness there. And that's where we are confused. But the Mahatma, they single pointedly seek that happiness at the source of happiness which is the Brahman which is the Almighty Lord which is my own self.

So what is my relationship with Him? He is as close to me as my own self. But there is no special relationship he is with me. Because I am a Dharmatma and others are not good people.

He says I am same to Samoham Sarva Bhulteshu. My relationship to them is same as my relationship to you, him, her, my relationship to my children. If they have my four children, that's exactly same.

But one is closer to me than another, because he identifies with me more, he writes to me more, he calls me up more, he comes to see me more -- so I have more relationship with him. The one who never calls me, never writes me, never comes to Thanksgiving dinner -- I have less relationship with him. But my relationship with all of them is exactly the same.

Samoham Sarva Bhuteshu -- everything and every being is made up of me alone. Therefore relationship is exactly same. Just as my relationship with my left leg and right leg exactly same.

Even though I rely on my left leg more because right leg is broken. So Bhagavan says Samoham Sarva Bhuteshru and each one is the birthright to know this. But because we are deluded, therefore I don't recognize it.

Just because I think that I have not done something right in my past that does not stop me from realizing this truth. Durachara -- Su is a prefix meaning supreme. Su-Durachara means one who is the highest sinner.

Even he has the right to realize me. Bhajate Mam Ananya Bhak -- once he single-pointedly identifies with me. Sadhu Eva Sa Mantavyaha Samyak Vyavasito Hi Saha -- once he is rightfully resolved, once he has completely realized what is the right way of living, what is his swadharma, then he should be considered a Sadhu.

This is Krishna's missionary zeal to expand the tent to its infinity. Everybody is in it, nobody left out. So once that person is rightly resolved, we must consider him as a good person.

Forget about what his past is all about. And the next verse says why that is because Kshhipram Bhavati Dharmatma. Once you have a right resolve, you very soon will become what you resolved to become.

See, it's all about your conviction about what is right and what is wrong. What is the right action? What is the wrong action? What is the right way of living and what is the wrong way of living. This is the right way to live.

You will become that in no time. Bhagawan saswat shantim ni gachati. And you will achieve that in eternal peace.

Peace which I had been seeking all my life and I have blamed everybody other than me. Children are not behaving to my expectations. Once you resolve rightfully where your Santi is, you will in no time achieve it.

Satsvatsanti m ni gachadhi. Such a person will achieve that eternal peace in no time. Kaunteya Pratijanihi Na Me Bhaktah Pranashyati.

It is obviously a little pat on Arjuna's back. Because the Pandavas, at no time during their life, ever questioned their relationship with Krishna or their faith in Krishna. So in our case also, if I have complete faith in that Supreme Lord who is myself, then my peace lies there.

Then Bhagavan says Na Me Bhaktah Pranashyati -- one who identifies with me will never be destroyed. Never be destroyed in the sense that he will never lose his peace again. Once I have decided where my peace is and am rightfully pursuing it single-pointedly, Bhagavan said he will never go back to getting unhappy again.

The next verse has been difficult for people to translate and understand. Mam Hi Partha Vyapashritya Ye Api Syuhu Papayonayaha. Then he described: Striyo Vaishyah Tatha Shudrah Te Api Yanti Param Gatim.

They also achieve my being. They are the people who are born in Papayoni. Correct understanding can only be gained if we can define Papayoni correctly.

That's where the problem is, right? Because he actually enumerated and gave examples of classes of people who are born in Papayoni. It is very loosely translated as "sinful birth." Well, then you have to define sin. Sin we have defined as a negative impression on my mind which is damaging to my chances of getting peace.

When my mind is agitated, no matter how much of a Gnani I am, I will not have peace. We know that when the mind is agitated with any negative impression, there is no peace. Papa is that which robs away my peace.

So Papayoni is the environment which has the most chances of creating negative impressions on my mind. Environment is not something I control. So if I am placed in that environment, it is not my fault.

It is not something I have chosen; I happen to be in that environment. In modern day, we call it the disadvantaged class of people, or minority. In India, Jains have fought very hard to be classified as a minority, and they finally got the same status as Muslims and Christians who are considered minorities in India.

It is not that they are saying, "We are bad, just consider us." No, they say, "We are disadvantaged because we are not the majority." So Papayoni creates an environment which has more chances of putting negative impressions on my mind. Bhagavan said that people who do not have the privilege of being in the most pious and best environment -- and those people are Striya, Vaishya, Tatha Shudra -- in which society, in which time of history, do you think that women have had the same rights as men, including in 2016? We know they are always disadvantaged. It is not their fault.

It is the society's fault if the way it is designed does not give them equal opportunity. There is a movie coming up, the Birth of a Nation. It's about how and I have not seen anything.

I just saw a clip on one of those talk show. They said that in the slavery days a black child and white child will be playing together till the age of about 11. About 11 they will decide that only now the black child has reached highest of his or her development.

So he doesn't need to be sent to school or do anything about it. He can now start working. White child will continue in his development of learning and going to school.

So is that something you consider a Papa Yoni -- because the child is born in that yoni, or because the society is not giving him an opportunity? Bhagavan said: the society which has not given them the opportunity they deserve -- an opportunity rightfully theirs, which is their birthright -- we are not giving them that. Even though you are born in that class of people who are disadvantaged, you have equal right to achieve the highest potential. In those days, and even today, there are classes which are disadvantaged.

Striya, Vaishya, Tatha Shudra -- women, merchants, laborers -- by history, everybody can vouch for it that they never had equal rights.
snippets.reflection:
"Kshipram bhavati dharmatma" - one who is rightly resolved quickly becomes righteous. This is the transformative power of conviction. Once you truly decide on the direction of your life, the becoming follows swiftly. "Shashvat shantim nigacchati" - such a person attains eternal peace. Then Krishna makes a solemn declaration: "Kaunteya pratijanihi na me bhaktah pranashyati" - O Arjuna, proclaim this truth: my devotee never perishes. This is not just Krishna's promise; He asks Arjuna to declare it, making the disciple a witness and messenger of this assurance.

 Verse 32 is often misunderstood. "Papa-yonayah" does not mean sinful by birth but disadvantaged by circumstance - those in environments that make spiritual pursuit more difficult. Women, merchants, laborers - in ancient society, these groups had fewer opportunities for formal spiritual study. Krishna's point is revolutionary: even those whom society has marginalized can attain the highest goal ("te'pi yanti param gatim"). The Gita democratizes liberation. Your birth, social status, education, or past mistakes do not disqualify you. This is "Krishna's missionary zeal to expand the tent to infinity" - everybody is included, nobody left out.

 Verse 33 then asks: if even the disadvantaged can reach the Supreme, how much more easily can those with advantages - the learned, the devoted, the royal sages? "Anityam asukham lokam imam prapya bhajasva mam" - having come to this impermanent, joyless world, worship Me. This week, honestly assess: What excuses have you been making for not deepening your spiritual practice? Whatever they are - lack of time, education, purity, worthiness - Krishna has removed them. The question is no longer "can I?" but "will I?"
snippets.shortReflection: You've been half-committed to the thing you say matters most. What would it look like to actually decide? Not to be perfect, but to truly choose a direction and trust that the transformation follows the commitment, not the other way around.

snippets.title: Day 127: Raja Vidya Raja Guhya Yoga

The Creator with his power of Maya he creates this universe through the Mayapati. He is the Lord of Maya, Lord of this illusion. But I am under the spell of Maya and therefore I'm in a Maya Jal.

I'm in the web of Maya. I can't see it clearly what my self is. He said the Vidya which will take me there would be the Raja Vidya, that which dispels my ignorance about my own self.

When I start seeing my relationship clearly with him then I will be Dharmaatma. I'll be a righteous soul. So Bhagavan has talked about the why people can't see it because of the Moga Asa Mogha actions.

I'll find my happiness here, I'll find my happiness there. And that's where we are confused. But the Mahatma, they single pointedly seek that happiness at the source of happiness which is the Brahman which is the Almighty Lord which is my own self.

So what is my relationship with Him? He is as close to me as my own self. But there is no special relationship he is with me. Because I am a Dharmatma and others are not good people.

He says I am same to Samoham Sarva Bhulteshu. My relationship to them is same as my relationship to you, him, her, my relationship to my children. If they have my four children, that's exactly same.

But one is closer to me than another, because he identifies with me more, he writes to me more, he calls me up more, he comes to see me more -- so I have more relationship with him. The one who never calls me, never writes me, never comes to Thanksgiving dinner -- I have less relationship with him. But my relationship with all of them is exactly the same.

Samoham Sarva Bhuteshu -- everything and every being is made up of me alone. Therefore relationship is exactly same. Just as my relationship with my left leg and right leg exactly same.

Even though I rely on my left leg more because right leg is broken. So Bhagavan says Samoham Sarva Bhuteshru and each one is the birthright to know this. But because we are deluded, therefore I don't recognize it.

Just because I think that I have not done something right in my past that does not stop me from realizing this truth. Durachara -- Su is a prefix meaning supreme. Su-Durachara means one who is the highest sinner.

Even he has the right to realize me. Bhajate Mam Ananya Bhak -- once he single-pointedly identifies with me. Sadhu Eva Sa Mantavyaha Samyak Vyavasito Hi Saha -- once he is rightfully resolved, once he has completely realized what is the right way of living, what is his swadharma, then he should be considered a Sadhu.

This is Krishna's missionary zeal to expand the tent to its infinity. Everybody is in it, nobody left out. So once that person is rightly resolved, we must consider him as a good person.

Forget about what his past is all about. And the next verse says why that is because Kshhipram Bhavati Dharmatma. Once you have a right resolve, you very soon will become what you resolved to become.

See, it's all about your conviction about what is right and what is wrong. What is the right action? What is the wrong action? What is the right way of living and what is the wrong way of living. This is the right way to live.

You will become that in no time. Bhagawan saswat shantim ni gachati. And you will achieve that in eternal peace.

Peace which I had been seeking all my life and I have blamed everybody other than me. Children are not behaving to my expectations. Once you resolve rightfully where your Santi is, you will in no time achieve it.

Satsvatsanti m ni gachadhi. Such a person will achieve that eternal peace in no time. Kaunteya Pratijanihi Na Me Bhaktah Pranashyati.

It is obviously a little pat on Arjuna's back. Because the Pandavas, at no time during their life, ever questioned their relationship with Krishna or their faith in Krishna. So in our case also, if I have complete faith in that Supreme Lord who is myself, then my peace lies there.

Then Bhagavan says Na Me Bhaktah Pranashyati -- one who identifies with me will never be destroyed. Never be destroyed in the sense that he will never lose his peace again. Once I have decided where my peace is and am rightfully pursuing it single-pointedly, Bhagavan said he will never go back to getting unhappy again.

The next verse has been difficult for people to translate and understand. Mam Hi Partha Vyapashritya Ye Api Syuhu Papayonayaha. Then he described: Striyo Vaishyah Tatha Shudrah Te Api Yanti Param Gatim.

They also achieve my being. They are the people who are born in Papayoni. Correct understanding can only be gained if we can define Papayoni correctly.

That's where the problem is, right? Because he actually enumerated and gave examples of classes of people who are born in Papayoni. It is very loosely translated as "sinful birth." Well, then you have to define sin. Sin we have defined as a negative impression on my mind which is damaging to my chances of getting peace.

When my mind is agitated, no matter how much of a Gnani I am, I will not have peace. We know that when the mind is agitated with any negative impression, there is no peace. Papa is that which robs away my peace.

So Papayoni is the environment which has the most chances of creating negative impressions on my mind. Environment is not something I control. So if I am placed in that environment, it is not my fault.

It is not something I have chosen; I happen to be in that environment. In modern day, we call it the disadvantaged class of people, or minority. In India, Jains have fought very hard to be classified as a minority, and they finally got the same status as Muslims and Christians who are considered minorities in India.

It is not that they are saying, "We are bad, just consider us." No, they say, "We are disadvantaged because we are not the majority." So Papayoni creates an environment which has more chances of putting negative impressions on my mind. Bhagavan said that people who do not have the privilege of being in the most pious and best environment -- and those people are Striya, Vaishya, Tatha Shudra -- in which society, in which time of history, do you think that women have had the same rights as men, including in 2016? We know they are always disadvantaged. It is not their fault.

It is the society's fault if the way it is designed does not give them equal opportunity. There is a movie coming up, the Birth of a Nation. It's about how and I have not seen anything.

I just saw a clip on one of those talk show. They said that in the slavery days a black child and white child will be playing together till the age of about 11. About 11 they will decide that only now the black child has reached highest of his or her development.

So he doesn't need to be sent to school or do anything about it. He can now start working. White child will continue in his development of learning and going to school.

So is that something you consider a Papa Yoni -- because the child is born in that yoni, or because the society is not giving him an opportunity? Bhagavan said: the society which has not given them the opportunity they deserve -- an opportunity rightfully theirs, which is their birthright -- we are not giving them that. Even though you are born in that class of people who are disadvantaged, you have equal right to achieve the highest potential. In those days, and even today, there are classes which are disadvantaged.

Striya, Vaishya, Tatha Shudra -- women, merchants, laborers -- by history, everybody can vouch for it that they never had equal rights.
snippets.reflection:
The final verse of Chapter 9 distills the entire teaching into four instructions: "Man-mana bhava" - fix your mind on Me; "mad-bhakto" - be My devotee; "mad-yaji" - sacrifice to Me; "mam namaskuru" - bow to Me. These are not four separate practices but one integrated orientation: complete absorption in the Divine through thought, feeling, action, and humility. The promise follows: "Mam evaishyasi" - you shall come to Me alone.

"Yuktvaivam atmanam mat-parayanah" - having thus united the self, with Me as your supreme goal. The Sanskrit "parayana" means ultimate destination, final refuge. When the Divine becomes your parayana - not one goal among many but THE goal that contains all others - liberation is assured. This is not about abandoning worldly responsibilities but about recognizing what they ultimately serve. The executive working to support family, the artist creating beauty, the scientist seeking truth - all activities can have mat-parayanah (the Divine as supreme goal) as their hidden foundation.

This verse appears again at the end of Chapter 18, framing the entire Gita's teaching. Chapter 9 reveals the royal secret: you are not separate from the Divine you seek. The path is simply the progressive removal of the illusion that you ever were separate. This week, make this verse your constant companion. When the mind wanders, return: "Man-mana bhava" - let my mind rest in You. When devotion wavers, remember: "mad-bhakto" - I am Your devotee, whether I feel it or not. When action becomes self-serving, redirect: "mad-yaji" - this is my offering. When pride arises, bow: "mam namaskuru" - I am not the doer; You are the source and goal of all.
snippets.shortReflection: Your mind wanders to your phone during conversations, to work during dinner, to regret during morning coffee. What would one hour feel like if your attention, emotion, action, and intention were all aimed at the same thing?

snippets.commentary:
Prakriti has three constituent parts: Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas.

Everything in this Prakriti is made up of these three Gunas; whichever has the predominance, that becomes my nature. Sattva is purity, Rajas is activity, and Tamas is inertia. Everything in this *prakriti* is made up of these three gunas, and we have learned the nature of Prakriti in chapter seven.

Up to chapter six we learnt about us as the limited beings and the makeup of our beings. From chapter 7 onward, we are learning about the nature of the supreme, the Lord. In chapter seven we learnt about his lower natures.

Bhagavan said this Ashtadha Prakriti: Bhumi, Apah, Analaha, Kham, Vayu, Mana, Buddhi, Ahankara. The eight —five great elements, Mind, intellect, and Ahankara —are the nature of *prakriti*, my lower nature. These are not different from me, but they are my lower nature in the sense of the grosser manifestation which you and I can perceive through our senses.

We discussed Prakriti in chapter seven. Chapter eight said that in Prakriti, things are unmanifest in the beginning, then manifest in the middle, then unmanifest again. So Prakriti itself has two aspects.

One is manifest, one is unmanifest. There is unmanifest, Prakriti. There is manifest Prakriti.

Bhagawan said, other than this unmanifest, there is another unmanifest which is my higher. Prakriti, which always remains unmanifest, is the support of all things and beings. So in chapter 8, Akshara Brahma *yoga*, we learnt about this unmanifest nature of Purusha remaining unmanifest, it supports everything.

Bhagawan said that I'm the origin of all things and beings and I'm also the dissolution of all things and beings. I get confused about my being and therefore I'm not experiencing the very nature of the supreme. The very nature of the supreme is Sat-Chit-Ananda — Sat is existence, Chit is knowledge, and Ananda is happiness or bliss.

So right now I'm not truly experiencing Sat. I know I exist, but I'm afraid I'll become non-existent. I'm not experiencing Sat fully.

I know something, but I don't know everything, so I'm not experiencing Chit either. And Ananda is my biggest problem. Happiness comes and goes.

For a while I'm happy, and most of the time I'm just pursuing happiness. So I'm trying to get out of the impermanent nature of Ananda into the permanent nature of Ananda, trying to find out where that permanent Ananda is. Bhagavan in the ninth chapter says that's the royal secret, the greatest secret: it is your very nature to be Sat-Chit-Ananda, but you are not experiencing it.

That knowledge which connects me back to my real nature is the royal knowledge. So that was chapter nine. At the end of chapter nine, Bhagavan said the only way one can experience this is Manmana Bhava.

Make your mind focused on me. Offer yourself to me. Make me as your goal Yuktva Mat Parayanaha.

In other words, completely identify with me and you will experience that Ananda which you are seeking. Now how do I get to that level where I can completely identify with him is the subject of chapter 10. So it's called Vibhuti Yoga.

Yoga of divine glories. I see, perceive, touch and feel this world of my experiences. But I break them all down into perishable things and beings.

Anything which I see, I can say I understand this. This is just a table. All this, I understand this.

Well, I understand this is plant kingdom. So I break this down into the impermanent, perishable conglomeration of things and beings which by very nature they are impermanent and not divine. I don't consider them as divine.

I don't say this table is divine. I don't consider my colleagues as divine. Even when some wise person comes.

But he is not Bhagavan. We have difficulty if somebody calls himself Bhagawan because we cannot associate the divinity with the objects of my perception. So how to change that and start seeing Divinity in everything I see and touch and feel is the subject of chapter 10.

Therefore it is called Yoga of Divine Glory. How to see this divinity, this divine glories in everything and being that I come across in the world of my experiences, my world of my perception. So Bhagavan starts this chapter without waiting for Arjuna to ask questions because he saw that he is enjoying it and he wanted to continue the theme which he started in chapter seven about the Prakriti.

When he says, this Prakriti is nothing but my lower nature. Everything in this Prakriti Aa Sesah. There is nothing left in this Prakriti which is not divine.

But we don't really see that way. In fact, we divide this world into good and evil. We have some level of acceptance that good is divine.

But we are difficult when it comes to bad and ugly. I can't associate divinity with it. This chapter will say that even that is only possible.

Bad is only possible because of my presence and evil is only possible because of my presence. There is nothing that can happen or exist in this world without me. So chapter opens with Bhagavan's statement says Bhuya Eva Mahabaho srunume paramam vacha yatta te aham Priyamanaya vakshyami Hita Kamya.

I wish your welfare Hita Kamiya. Therefore I'm going to continue. And in last chapter I told you that this knowledge is available to all.

And we discussed that verse which is very troublesome to discuss and say. Those who are born in Papayonayaha Triya vaishya tathakshadraha. Even they have equal right when they come to me.

If they focus their mind onto me. We discuss why Papayoni. Anything which takes me away from my identification with the supreme is sin.

That which does not recognize my true potential which is Sat chit in Ananda is Papa. It is the impurity on my mind which is right now not letting me see who I am. An environment which is more likely to create wrong impressions on my mind is Papa Yoni.

Yoni is a collection of people which creates an environment that is similar for each other —a symbiotic relationship. It's like a satsang in reverse —bad company. If I'm put in that environment where I get more sinful impressions on my mind, I have less chance of rising out of it.

Even those people who are disadvantaged by their environment —those who are put in a society that does not give them the equal right to achieve what they try to achieve —can still rise above that. Triya Vaishya Tatakshudra. Interestingly, the Vaishyas never complained about this verse.

Only two groups complain. Vaishya didn't say why we are included in it as well. We are higher than you now.

All business people are worshipped now, not Kshatriyas and Brahmanas. So Bhagawan says that at the time of Mahabharata, Vaishyas were not considered as high as the Brahmins and Kshatriyas. I heard when I was growing up.

Which profession you are supposed to take? Uttam Kheti Keti Farming. Madhyam Vyapa and Kanishta Nokri. The worst is you want to work for somebody is Kanishta.

We all work for corporate and feel great about it. If you can't do farming then only you do Vaipa. So they were considered lower in that society.

Now today in India, if you tell someone to become a farmer —how many farmers are committing suicide? Why would you want me to do farming? But in that society, Kshatriyas were farmers. Janakaraj, when he was tilling his land, found Sita. Kshatriyas, the kings, were themselves landlords and farmers.

So those people in that environment had a great chance to uplift themselves by getting this knowledge. But others did not have those equal rights. Women, Vaishya, Kshudra.

But even they can get this knowledge and come to me. But you are a Mahabaho. You are the mighty armed person who has all the opportunities and all the prerequisites to know this.

So Bhuya Eva Mahabaho again. Listen to my very important words. I think you have come to a level that you are understanding what I'm saying.

Manmana Bhava Madh Bhakta Madhya ji Mam namaskaru. I heard Obama saying the other day, stay focused. Don't get distracted by the protesters.

Don't get distracted by your doubts in your mind. Bhagavan says Paramam vacha yate aham Priyamanaya. And I'm only telling those people who likes to listen to this type of knowledge.

Vakshyami Hitakami Ayyaa. Because I wish welfare for you all. And therefore I'm telling you.

So what I'm telling you is what we had started in the last chapter saying. What is the royal secret? Aham Adhi Devanam Maharshinam Chasarva Sah. Neither the Devas in the heavens nor the great Rishis know my origin.

What is the source of my being? Not on the great Rishis, not the Devas. Because even in Puranas, Devas have their own limitations. Devas are considered pretty greedy.

They want to have everything. Devas, they don't know. And Rishis, they are distracted by their own intellect.

See, when we learn something, we get to a level where our intellect will become an obstacle. We can't experience it because we keep doubting ourselves. So Bhagavan says, even they don't know.

Because the source of the Deva and Rishis is me. Dheerananda's very famous example. Batteries in the flashlight.

If you're in a dark room and I have flashlight, I can see everything in the room. But somebody says, what type of batteries are you using, Rajan? I say, well, let me take it out. I take out the batteries.

I put the batteries back. Light is back, but I can't see the batteries. I said, I don't know till tomorrow morning.

So the source of the light in the flashlight is the batteries. And therefore I cannot know through the light of the flashlight the type of batteries I'm using. Through my intellect, which is the Rishi, I cannot know the source of my being.

I constantly try to contemplate through my intellect by deduction and inferences who I am. Bhagavan said, you will not know that the Rishis, our intellect, the knower, the seer in us is the Rishi. In the Devas are our sense perceptions.

To illumine something which is illuminated by my senses. So my senses are the Devas. Without them, the world is not existent for me.

You remove the one sense of seeing. The world of sight is gone. You remove the hearing.

The world of sound is gone. You remove all five senses. The world is illuminated by my senses.

So they are Devas through my senses. I am trying to find Bhagavan. I want to see Bhagavan.

I want to see the presence of Bhagavan. In the laboratory, when somebody dies, what happens? Where is that atma is going? The people have done experiments of people dying. And what is it that leaving they cannot find it simply because Bhagavan said, because I am the source of this Deva Dhanda, I am the source of your senses and your intellect.

You will never be able to find me through this. Because the instrument cannot find its own source. Bhagwan says, aham, Adhi Diwanam, Maharishi Nam Cha Sarvasa.

I'm not available to any of those, to the sense perceptions or by intellectual inquiry. I'm only available by contemplation and identification. By identification that I will be able to find myself.

Yom Ajam Anadim Chavaiyati. One who knows that I am that I. Whichever way you apply it, when applied to the supreme, he is the God.

Bhagawan says "I" —that includes everything.
snippets.reflection:
Krishna declares that neither the celestial beings (Devas) nor the great sages (Maharishis) can fully comprehend His origin, for He is the source of them all. This teaching invites us to a profound humility: the instruments we use to understand reality - our senses and intellect - are themselves products of that supreme reality. Just as batteries in a flashlight cannot illuminate themselves, our mind and senses cannot fully grasp their own source. Yet knowing Him as "unborn, beginningless, and Lord of the universe" liberates us from delusion and all conceivable sin.

Consider how you typically try to "figure out" the divine through analysis and reasoning. These verses suggest that intellectual understanding alone has limits - the knower cannot fully objectify its own source. Instead, Krishna offers this knowledge out of love ("priyamanaya" - to one who is dear) and for our welfare ("hitakamyaya"). Today, practice approaching spiritual understanding not as a puzzle to solve, but as a relationship to deepen. When you encounter something beyond your comprehension - a moment of unexpected grace, an inexplicable feeling of peace, the mystery of consciousness itself - instead of immediately trying to analyze it, allow yourself to simply rest in not-knowing.

Ask yourself: "How would my daily life change if I truly accepted that my mind cannot fully grasp its own source? What would it mean to approach the divine with the heart of a beloved, rather than only the intellect of an investigator?"
snippets.shortReflection: You're trying to understand your purpose using the same mind that's asking the question. But what if the tool you're using—your thoughts, your logic—can't illuminate what it came from, just like a flashlight can't shine on its own batteries?

snippets.commentary:
Bhagavan is immanent because he resides in the hearts of all beings — Ishvara Sarva Bhutanam Hrideshe Arjuna Tishtathi. Ishvara is residing in the hearts of all beings, therefore immanent. But he's also transcendental because we do not recognize him.

This chapter started out by Bhagavan saying in the second verse, I am not known to anyone. Neither the Devas, the *divine* beings or the divine senses, know me, nor the Great Rishis know me. He is not known by the mind or the intellect. By applying the normal tools of my cognition, I cannot know Ishvara. Therefore he is transcendental. So these two aspects of Bhagavan we have to overcome, in a sense, to know Him.

We have to find altar of meditation. We have completed the first segment of *karma* *yoga*, culminated in a Dhyana Yoga to meditate upon that supreme Self, my true Self. But what to meditate upon is what we have been discussing since last three chapters 7, 8 and 9. And Bhagawan in various ways told us what his real nature is that I am all pervading. Everything is strung into me. There is no reality other than me.

But it's still difficult for us to meditate on those aspects of Bhagavan. So the Vibhuti Yoga, the glories of the Lord, are required to meditate upon, to focus on. Something which I can identify through the limited means that I have, is my mind and intellect. So in this chapter, the Bhagavan is giving us the Vibhuti, that which I can identify and vouch for his presence. It is something like when I am in a deep sleep at night and wake up suddenly if I really want to know whether the sun is outside or not. That means, is it a day or not?

When I open my windows and I see sunlight, I do not see the sun, but I see sunlight. The presence of sunlight tells me that sun has risen. The sun is there outside. I may not be able to see sun for various reasons. Maybe a building is blocking my view, maybe so bright that I cannot see it. But the very fact that I can experience the sunlight, it tells me that sun has risen.

In the same way, if I know the Vibhutis Sri Bhagawan says, if you can identify the qualities which emanate from me, which are my real qualities, then you should be able to vouch for my presence. The Lord resides in all hearts, in all beings, in all things. But I cannot vouch for it right now. So Bhagawan is giving us the tools to realize his presence. So in verse 3, Bhagavan concluded Yomam Ajam Anadim, Chaviti, Loka Maheshwaram. I am not known to the Devas.

I am also not known to the Rishis, the great sages. I am not known through intellect nor I am known through mind. However, if one knows that I am Ajam Anadim, I am the source of all being. I am birthless and beginningless. It is uncaused, caused, then it is birthless. There is nothing before me.

Therefore there is nothing is causing my existence. And also I'm beginningless because there's nothing before me. Loka Maheshwaram, the Lord of all the entire creation is there because of me. Because of the entity which is beginningless and birthless, the entire Jagat exists, the Bhagavan, the Lord Ishvara is the material cause and efficient cause for this Jagat. When he created this universe out of his own Maya, there was no other material available to him. From his own self, from his own qualities.

He provided the material as well as the knowledge, the efficient cause to create this Jagat. So the creation, if it all comes out of he is the Loka Maheshram. He is the Lord of all the beings. Lord is the one on whom my existence depends. So my Lord is my own consciousness. Without that, my existence as this limited being does not exist.

The day consciousness is not there, I will not be nil Bhatt. I'll be just a dead body. So Bhagavan said Asammudasam, the one who is not deluded by these appearances, he will be relieved of all the sins. In other words, all the ignorances, all the ignorant ideas that I have about myself as a limited being, I'll be liberated from. And then he enumerates those 20 qualities of the supreme Being, the divinity. These qualities in people, in things and beings, exist because of my presence. Those qualities are somewhat easy to understand.

Buddhi, Gnanam, Asamoha, Shamah, Satyam, Damaha, Shamaha. Buddhi is intellect, Nischayatmika Buddhi — that which decides what is right and wrong. So when I feel that I'm exhibiting my Buddhi because I can decide it is day and not night, that's my Buddhi. Bhagavan says that because of my presence in you, this Buddhi exists in you at the microcosm. This Buddhi I use for deciding what's outside in this world. Gnanam — this Buddhi now gives me knowledge of what is real and what is unreal.

Asammoha and non illusion. When I have Buddhi and I apply it to find out whether it is day outside or night, when I wake up, it gives me non illusion. Even though it was dark in my room, there is no difference between day and night in my room. But as soon as I open the window, I knew it's a day outside. That is because of my Buddhi that if there is sunlight outside, the sun has risen and therefore it is a day. So that created a Samohaha.

Non-illusion, no delusion, no confusion. Out of these three, I develop other qualities such as Kshama (forgiveness), Satyam (truth), Damaha (control of the Indriyas), and Shamaha (control of the mind). We've seen in Tattva Bodh that Shamah is Mano Nigrahaha, and Damaha is control of the senses such as eyes and ears. Now, if I see that somebody is not yet convinced that it's day outside — even though I have concluded that it is day — if my wife doesn't agree with me, then I forgive her.

I think she has not seen outside yet. Because of my knowledge, my Buddhi, my non-delusion, I can forgive other people who are still not at that level. She has not woken up completely. She cannot see the light outside — to her, it's still night. I can forgive her because of my knowledge.

If I have no knowledge, there will be confusion. We will be fighting about it. But because I have knowledge, I can have Kshama and I can vouch for the truth that it is day outside. I can control my actions and also my mind. All this emanates from the same source — my own consciousness at the vyashti, at the microcosm. I have all these exhibiting through me.

Because of that divinity, the consciousness functioning through me, I'm identifying with it. Sukham Dukham Bhavah Abhavah, Bhayam cha Abhayam eva cha. These are the pairs of opposites I have to deal with in this world — this world which I have created out of my own consciousness. In deep sleep, there was no world outside to deal with. There were no pairs of opposites.

There was no confusion about day or night. But as soon as I woke up and I have this Buddhi and Gnana exhibiting through me. Now I have to deal with this world outside which has pairs of opposites. So Kannadukha Bhava and Abhava. Existence and non existence, birth and death. Bhayam cha Bhayam Bhaya is a positive emotion which protects me from getting myself hurt.

If I have no Bhaya of jumping from a third floor window, then I'm going to hurt myself. So this fear of getting hurt is actually protecting me. So therefore it's a positive emotion. And Abhaya and fearlessness. Things which I am very sure about. I'll be fearless no matter what.

Somebody tells me that I do not exist. So things which I so sure about my existence, I'm fearless. Things which I'm not sure about my existence. After my death, I'm fearful. I have fear of death because I have no idea what will happen after my death. I'm fearless about my existence right now.

Because I know who I am and how I exist exist. So there's both fear and fearlessness emanating from my identification with my consciousness. Ahimsa, non injury, Samatha, equanimity, Tusthi, contentment, Tapaha, disciplines, austerity, Dhanam, charity, Yashaha, Fame and also Ayyashaha ill fame. All these I experience because of my identification with myself as my conscious conscious being. These 20 qualities are given as the glories of that supreme Lord. These are the basic qualities through which he manifests in this world through beings.

He resides in the hearts of all the beings. And when those beings identify with him, these positive qualities are exhibited through them. Then what about the opposites of this? Like Hinsa, Abudhi, Agnana, Samoha. It is nothing but non identification with the self. When I identify with the Divinity within me, all these positive qualities of the divinity will be manifesting through me.

When I'm not identifying with that divinity, then the lack of those qualities will be exhibiting. So the lack of qualities are not really any qualities. They are just lack of good qualities. Something similar to how there is nothing called cold — just a lack of heat. Heat I can identify as a form of energy, but cold has no form of energy.

It just lack of heat creates sensation of cold. Lack of Ahimsa creates Himsa. Lack of Buddhi creates Abuddhi — one who doesn't know anything. Lack of knowledge creates ignorance. So the negatives which we see in this world is because of non identification with the true self. Bhagavan said this entire Jagat is created by my own mind using my own self as the material.

My Maya is the material, therefore he is the Loka Maheshwaram. Without him no world is possible. Without you being conscious of your world, your world cannot exist. Without me being conscious of my world, my world does not exist. And therefore he, the Supreme Lord who is functioning through all beings as their consciousness. He is the Lord of all all the beings.

So he is justifying why he is Loka, Maheshwaram, Bhavanti, Bhava, Bhutana, Mata Eva, Pruthakvida. These varieties of expressions you see in this world through various beings with all these qualities in the various levels, this permutation combinations, all these 20 qualities creates this multitude of personalities in this world. Somebody has more Buddhi, somebody has more Kshama, somebody has more Ahimsa. All these manifestations in this world through beings. But anytime I see the expression of any of these qualities, I must know that divinity is present in that being. Bhavanti Bhava Bhutanam Mata Eva Prithak Vidhaha.

All these different kinds of qualities of being arise from me alone. Without that one common thread which we call it consciousness, life, none of these are possible. And therefore we should know when we see these qualities that the Lord is present. And therefore when we meet each other, when we see the exhibition of any of these qualities, we have to do Namaste that I see the divinity in you is emanating through you as kindness. All these qualities are nothing but the glories of the Lord and Bhagawan. Meditate on those glories.

These are your means, the tools for you to meditate on the divine self that you are. Then Bhagavan concludes by giving a complete picture of the creation. Maharsayah, Saptapurve, Chatvarohu, Manamahata, Madbhava Manasa Jata, Esam, Loka, Imah, Prajaha.
snippets.reflection:
These verses reveal twenty divine qualities that emanate from the Lord's presence: Buddhi (intellect), Jnana (wisdom), Asamoha (non-delusion), Kshama (forgiveness), Satya (truth), Dama (sense-control), Shama (mind-control), Sukha and Dukha (pleasure and pain), Bhava and Abhava (birth and death), Bhaya and Abhaya (fear and fearlessness), Ahimsa (non-injury), Samata (equanimity), Tushti (contentment), Tapa (austerity), Dana (charity), Yasha and Ayasha (fame and ill-fame). Each of these exists in beings only because of the divine presence within. When we see someone display wisdom, forgiveness, or fearlessness, we are witnessing the Lord's light shining through that individual.

The teaching also clarifies something crucial: negative qualities are simply the absence of these positive divine expressions. Just as cold is not a thing in itself but merely the absence of heat, ignorance is the absence of knowledge, cruelty is the absence of compassion. This understanding transforms how we view both ourselves and others - rather than seeing "bad" as a positive force, we recognize it as non-identification with our divine nature. Today, when you encounter any of these twenty qualities in yourself or others - a moment of genuine forgiveness, an act of charity, a flash of wisdom - pause and recognize: "This is divinity expressing itself."

Reflect on these questions: "Which of these twenty qualities do I most naturally express? Which ones feel distant from me? Can I see even difficult emotions like fear or the experience of loss as part of the divine tapestry of existence, present only because consciousness is present?"
snippets.shortReflection: Intelligence, confusion, patience, anger, contentment, anxiety—you experience all of these but identify with none of them permanently. They arise in you like weather patterns. So who is the sky that contains them all?

snippets.title: Day 130: Divine Manifestations
snippets.sanskrit:
एतां विभूतिं योगं च मम यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः |
सोऽविकम्पेन योगेन युज्यते नात्र संशयः ||

अहं सर्वस्य प्रभवो मत्तः सर्वं प्रवर्तते |
इति मत्वा भजन्ते मां बुधा भावसमन्विताः ||

मच्चित्ता मद्गतप्राणा बोधयन्तः परस्परम् |
कथयन्तश्च मां नित्यं तुष्यन्ति च रमन्ति च ||
snippets.transliteration:
etāṁ vibhūtiṁ yogaṁ cha mama yo vetti tattvataḥ
so ’vikampena yogena yujyate nātra sanśhayaḥ

ahaṁ sarvasya prabhavo mattaḥ sarvaṁ pravartate
iti matvā bhajante māṁ budhā bhāva-samanvitāḥ

mach-chittā mad-gata-prāṇā bodhayantaḥ parasparam
kathayantaśh cha māṁ nityaṁ tuṣhyanti cha ramanti cha
verseTranslations: He who rightly understands My manifested glory and My Creative Power, beyond doubt attains perfect peace.
I am the source of all; from Me everything flows. Therefore the wise worship Me with unchanging devotion.
With minds concentrated on Me, with lives absorbed in Me, and enlightening each other, they ever feel content and happy.
snippets.commentary:
By his power of Yoga he appears to us as many. So you go to the jewelry shop, the gold is gold, but the Vibhuti of gold with all the jewelries you see, that's the glory of the gold you see in the jewelry shop.

And the yogic power is the jeweler who is the yogic power, that efficient cause with which he creates many out of this one gold. So Bhagavan said that I am the source of all the beings in this chapter, but says not many people can realize that. Even the Rishis, Maharisis and the Devas Sura Ganaha, even they cannot recognize that.

The reason being that I am the source of even those who we consider to be the higher beings, such as Sura Ganaha and Mahari says, and therefore the effect cannot find its own source. All this Saptarisis, sanat, Kumaras and 14 Manus, they're all born out of my mind. In other words, anything which you consider is the source of your being, source of your human race or your existence, all came out of me, born out of my mind.

And after that, all the progeny of those are also me. However, it appears to us as many because of our own *ignorance* about our own *self*. Now the goal is to unwind that clock from where we started and reached to this point of ignorance and remove that ignorance.

So, Aham Sarvasya Prabhavah, Matta Sarva Pravartate, Iti Matva Bhajante Mam Budhaha Bhava Samanvitaha —but one whose intellect is steady, Bhava Samanvitaha, they will see me as the source of all the beings. Everything is pervaded by me. With such understanding and such *devotion*, one who worships me, they obviously will get me.

And then: Macchitta Madgat Pranah Bodhayantah Parasparam Kathayantash cha Mam Nityam Tushyanti cha Ramanti cha. What we don't have in our life is contentment and delight. Our life is full of discontent and dejection.

It is often said, our life is like the cardiogram: unhappiness, unhappiness, little happiness, unhappiness, little happiness. That's the story of our life. What we're seeking is exactly the contentment.

I want to be satisfied, I want to be content. I want to have bliss. Then I want to enjoy my life.

That's what we are looking for. And everything we have tried so far in our life has its own limitation. So that is what we are lacking.

Bhagavan says the only people who achieve this are Macchitaha —those whose mind is absorbed in me. In other words, I have come to the conclusion that the Lord is the source of all being. And we have seen from the logic of spirituality that this world was created by God, using the only material available to him, which is his own *self*.

You and I cannot be anything different than his own self. With that understanding, if my mind is resting in him always, anything I see, anything I feel, anything I touch is nothing but his self. Machittaha Madgat Pranaha —everything that is happening with my life, my Prana.

Wider view of Prana: any experience which I have through my sense organs is nothing but his experience alone. Because I have come to the firm conclusion that this world could not have been created out of anything but God's own self. There is no other material available to him to create this world but his own self.

We constantly remind each other that you and I are nothing but the Lord's own self. It reminds me of a kind of practical joke. When I was in the Dallas group, a lot of Americans who were involved in what I do said, "Rajan, I noticed something.

You guys always say, 'Hari Om.'" In Chinmaya Mission we meet each other and say, "Hari Om." But he heard it as "hurry home." He said, "I know now why you guys have a better family life. You remind each other constantly. Your wife must be waiting.

Rajan, go home, otherwise you'll be in trouble. You remind each other, hurry home. Then you won't have any trouble." But the real meaning of Bodhayantaha Parasparam is that we constantly remind each other and enlighten others that there is no other self in you or in me but the same self.

That's why Namaste means "I bow down to you" —the same self which is in me is in you. Bodhayantaha Parasparam Kathayantash cha Mam Nityam —constantly speaking about me, constantly reminding ourselves in all our actions that everything happening in my life, every experience that I'm experiencing, is nothing but the Lord's glory alone. Tushyanti cha Ramanti cha —they're content and they're reveling in their own self.

Distinction between Kridanti and Ramanti. Krida requires an outside object to interact with —to play a ball or whatever. Ramanti is reveling in yourself; by yourself you're enjoying.

That is Ramanti. So the two things we always are lacking is this contentment and the joy. Bhagavan said, you can only get by your mind constantly focused on the self.

All your activities are devoted to the self. Reminding, enlightening each other that we are the manifestation of the same Lord. And then Kathayanti cha —speaking about that will lead you to contentment and enjoyment.

Dadami Buddhi Yogam Tam Yena Mam Upayanti Te. Those who do what we have discussed in the previous verse — Bhagawan says, now what is my job? Tesham Satata Yuktanam Bhajatam Priti Purvakam Dadami Buddhi Yogam Tam Yena Mam Upayanti Te. I give them Buddhi Yoga.

Those who are doing what we just discussed —constantly focusing their mind on the self, all their activities dedicated to the self, enlightening each other and speaking about it —they're content. Because Bhagavan said, I give them Buddhi Yoga. Now, Buddhi Yoga is not this Buddhi that we know as part of Mana, Buddhi, Chitta, Ahankara.

That Buddhi is used to decipher the world of objects. With this intellect I try to decide my experiences —whether this is right or that is right —and I come to a conclusion. So that is the ordinary Buddhi.

But this is Yogic Buddhi. Buddhi we associate with knowing something. Becoming firmly convicted about something is Buddhi.

Waffling is the mind — I like, I dislike. I know, I don't know, this or that. Once I decisively know, that's Buddhi.

In this case, I now decisively know what my self is. There is no doubt left in my mind anymore. Up till now I had a doubt: what is my relationship with the Lord? Is he really looking after me or not? Well, I'm doing his puja —does he know that I'm doing his puja? Therefore, make sure that we publish it in Bharadwani that I did Lakshmi Puja. "Lord, you know that it was published in Bharadwani.

Now it's your responsibility." Bhagavan said, I give them that Buddhi which gives you that contentment and joy. Te Yena Mam Upayanti Te. With that Buddhi Yoga they come to me.

Our journey started from when we separated from ourselves by ignorance and started thinking, "This is me, this body is me, this mind is me, this intellect is me." And now at my age, I realize that not only this body which I was born with and then grew out of food, but the steel plate in my leg and the acrylic lens in my eye is also "me." No difference between the lens I was born with. I actually asked my ophthalmologist. I said, doesn't it come with a lifetime warranty? He said, no, it doesn't.

I said, how about this one? He said, this has a limited warranty too. All that I consider me turns out to be something I have borrowed from this world. Bhagavan said, once that awareness takes place that there is nothing but the self exists.

You know there is nothing but "I" that exists. That parallax is now removed between my lower self and the higher self. Tesham Eva Anukampartham Aham Ajnana Jam Tamah Nashayami Atma Bhavastho Jnana Dipena Bhasvata.

So now it seems like Bhagavan is doing all that very partially —only for those who put in all this effort. And he really doesn't care about people like us who are constantly busy with our business and our studies and our professions. But Bhagavan is ever compassionate, and all religions say that, including Christianity.

Bhagawan is never considered as one who is harshly judging people. He's ever compassionate, but he has his own limitations. Unless I seek his compassion, he does not have the power to shower his compassion on me.

Let's say I have five children and four of them never talk to me —only one talks to me. My compassion is only revealed to the one who is constantly with me. The other four have never experienced my compassion because they never allowed me to show it to them.

That sun is always compassionate to give you sunlight. But as long as I keep the windows closed, he doesn't have any power to give you compassion. He has to patiently wait outside your window till you allow him to come inside your room by opening the windows.

Then he can shower his compassion by giving you the light. It is us where we have to become worthy of his compassion. So Bhagawan said, Tesham —those we just talked about, all the qualities they have achieved.

Tesham Eva Anukampartham Aham Ajnana Jam Tamah. What has made me feel different from my own self, from God? My own ignorance. The self is self-effulgent.

It has its own revelation. It becomes revealed to you by its own glory. Myself, I'm always aware.

Under whatever condition, I know I exist. That requires no intellectual conviction or intellectual argument about whether I exist or not. Everything else requires my intellectual conclusion.

Am I an architect or a doctor? I come to the conclusion I cannot be anything but an architect. I never went to medical school. So all these things which my upadhi requires —my intellectual conclusion that "this is who I am" —but "I exist" requires no intellectual argument.

It reveals to me that I exist, in my awareness. So Bhagavan says, what has removed you from that revelation that yourself and the God-self are one? Your ignorance, created by identification with the non-self —my body, my mind, my intellect —that created an avarana, a veiling, over my understanding that I exist. And that veiling once removed, no other efforts are required.

Good example. I'm looking for my key in the room and the key is lying on the table. But the room is pitch dark.

Obviously I can't find my key. But somebody with his compassion turned the lights on. With that compassion of turning the light on, now the light shines on my key and I see my key.

The person didn't have to produce a key. Just out of compassion, he removes the darkness in the room and I find my key. In the same way, Bhagawan said, the self was always dwelling in my own heart.

It is always revealing that I exist. But I consider that "I" to be this limited "I" —the existence which I feel all the time, I now take it for granted. It is talking about my body, my mind, my intellect, my achievement, my position, my relationship.

That's "I." Bhagawan said, with the destruction of this ignorance by all the things which we have talked about, I remove that darkness by lighting up the Jnana Dipa, the light of knowledge, in your heart. And you come to this revelation that my existence is of that supreme self.
snippets.reflection:
These verses describe the blessed state of those who truly understand Krishna's Vibhuti and Yoga: "Macchitta Madgata-pranah" - minds absorbed in Me, lives dedicated to Me. Such devotees enlighten each other (Bodhayantah parasparam), constantly speak of the divine (Kathayantah), and experience both contentment (Tushyanti) and joy (Ramanti). Notice how this spiritual path is not solitary - it involves mutual enlightenment and shared discourse. The greeting "Hari Om" or "Namaste" is not mere social courtesy but a constant reminder: the divine in me recognizes the divine in you.

The distinction between Kridanti (playing with external objects) and Ramanti (reveling within oneself) is profound. Our usual happiness depends on external conditions - we need something outside ourselves to enjoy. But the devotee described here experiences Ramanti - a self-contained joy that needs nothing external. This contentment comes from the firm conviction: "I am the source of all; from Me everything flows" (Aham sarvasya prabhavah). When this understanding moves from intellectual assent to lived experience, the endless seeking stops.

Today, practice "Bodhayantah parasparam" - mutual enlightenment. Share a spiritual insight with someone, or ask about their understanding. Notice how speaking about truth deepens your own grasp of it. And throughout the day, when happiness comes, ask: "Is this Krida - dependent on something external? Or can I touch that Ramanti - the joy of simply being?" What would it mean for your life to be truly "Madgata-prana" - your very life-breath dedicated to recognizing the divine in all?
snippets.shortReflection: Who actually helps you grow—the people who agree with everything you say, or the ones who challenge you to think differently? Real spiritual practice isn't lonely self-improvement; it's showing up to conversations that change you.

snippets.title: Day 131: The Lamp of Wisdom
