Therefore it is not possible. But what we try to do as human beings, we personify that reason in one person. So therefore he said, bhagavan, I'm seeing this vision in your body.

Even in our life, what we do is all the divinity that we can think of or we have imagined of. We assign that to one person. We want to see that in one person.

So therefore we say, bhagavan, I see all that in Chinbananda somebody says, I saw all that in Bhagavan Rajneesh, somebody says, because we gather all that conceptualization of divinity into one person, we want to see that in one person. And then we get disappointed because a person by very nature cannot have all the attributes of that entire divinity. But if we change our perspective, then we will be able to see that.

So Bhagavan said, yadibaha divi Surya Sahastrasya Bhavet yukpat Uthita Sadrushi saa saad Bhasah Tasya mahat manah. Splendor of that being which represents totality, heirs of thousands of sons. You cannot describe it.

Tatra Ekastam, Jagat Krishnam, Pravibhaktam, Anekata, it's all centered into one. Because that's what Arjuna asked for. I want to see all that centered into you, all in one.

Right now I see them as Pravibhakta, different parts. I know this cosmos exist as nature, as Lord's manifestation, but in different parts I can manage. I can manage to understand.

It is your world, his world, her world, my planet, different planets. There are different parts of his manifestation. From my narrow perspective, I can understand it.

But now he says, Tatra Ekastam is centered into one Jagat Krushnam. The entire Jagat Jagat includes everything. Jagat includes your physical cosmos as well as your emotional cosmos and your intellectual cosmos.

Everything that you can think of that the greatness of our Hinduism, it has included in Astra, Prakriti, mind, intellect and ego. Without that, your world is not complete. If I can put all this together, one person and what that vision would be, that's what Arjuna is seeing right now.

In that Mahatma Deva Devashya Sari re. Arjuna saw in the body of the God of Gods. Krishna is no longer a person.

Dhritarashtra can relate to who he knew as the king of Yadavas or Pandava's ally. But now he says he's a Deva Devasya, the God of all the gods. So he said, I see the Maruta and I see Rudras, all these Devas, all the deities which he is the God of all those deities.

Everything that we have imagined, who has the control over this world, he has control over all of them. Deva Deveshary, Pandavahatada, Pandava Arjuna. Arjuna saw in the body of that God of gods this splendor of thousands of suns blazing at the same time.

So what could be the reaction of Arjuna Vishma Yavista overcame by the wonderment? He's completely dumbfounded. Rustiroma is here standing on hands. I don't know if the English translation of in our language it's very well used.

Goosebumps is the only thing come to my mind in English. He's having goosebumps. He's completely dumbfounded looking at this.

He asked for it, but did not know what to expect. Now he's seeing in the body of the God of God because he's all that vision is personified in one person. Ristiroma Dhananjaya Dhananjaya again Arjuna Pranasya Silasadvam.

Once you have that experience, as soon as you see him, Chamatkar I may not believe anything about when he does Chamatkar, he takes out a Rolex watch and gives you namaskar right there. So Pranamya Sirasadevam, as soon as he realized the nature of this total being is surrendered. We don't surrender right now because we don't think this is all true, even though we kind of learn and all that.

But when it comes to our life, we say, no, no, I have better control. I have people come to me and say, stop coming to class. I think it was actually giving him less motivation to do things.

So right now our motivation in working in a world is we don't have much trust in him. We don't think he can take care of it. I really need to look out for myself, look out for number one.

That used to be a mantra when I came to this country. Somebody has started and said, think about number one. Number one is you start from thinking about you first, then comes everybody else.

Your family, your children, your. Start from you take care of yourself first and then go to. But here he said he realized that he is nobody with whom he is relating to what he is seeing Nobody.

So Pranaam is Sirasa Devam Dandavat Pranam Only the South Indians do that Dandavat Pranayama Punjabi is doing Mathotic they just put the head on and Gujaratvi yeah Pranamya Sirasadevam, Once you have understood the greatness of who you are relating to, you are completely surrendered to him.
snippets.reflection:
In these verses, Arjuna sees the entire universe with its manifold forms "all embraced in One" - the supreme Lord. His response is immediate and visceral: dumb with awe, hair standing on end, head bowed, hands clasped in salutation. He sees all the powers of Nature, the various creatures, the Progenitor Brahma on his lotus throne, the Sages, and the shining angels. Notice the dramatic shift: the moment Arjuna truly perceives Krishna's nature, spontaneous surrender arises. He does not decide to bow; bowing happens naturally.

This points to why we do not surrender in daily life - we have not truly seen. We may intellectually accept spiritual teachings, but when push comes to shove, we still believe we have better control, that we need to "look out for number one." Arjuna's goosebumps and spontaneous prostration show what happens when intellectual understanding becomes direct perception. The teaching suggests that true surrender is not an act of will but a natural response to genuine recognition of the divine.

Reflect today on your relationship with surrender. When you say "Thy will be done" or "I trust the universe," is it genuine recognition or merely words? Notice the situations where you grip tightly, trying to control outcomes. Ask yourself: What would I need to truly see for surrender to arise spontaneously? Consider that perhaps you are not lacking in willingness to surrender but in the clarity of perception that makes surrender the obvious and natural response. Practice today by consciously acknowledging your limitations in even small matters - traffic, weather, others' moods - and notice if a sense of release naturally follows this honest recognition.
snippets.shortReflection: Real surrender isn't something you decide to do. It's what happens naturally when you finally see clearly. Right now, you're gripping and controlling because you haven't truly seen how little control you actually have. What would need to become obvious for you to let go?

snippets.title: Day 147: No Beginning, No End
snippets.sanskrit:
अनेकबाहूदरवक्त्रनेत्रं पश्यामि त्वां सर्वतोऽनन्तरूपम् |
नान्तं न मध्यं न पुनस्तवादिं पश्यामि विश्वेश्वर विश्वरूप ||

किरीटिनं गदिनं चक्रिणं च तेजोराशिं सर्वतोदीप्तिमन्तम् |
पश्यामि त्वां दुर्निरीक्ष्यं समन्ता द्दीप्तानलार्कद्युतिमप्रमेयम् ||

त्वमक्षरं परमं वेदितव्यं त्वमस्य विश्वस्य परं निधानम् |
त्वमव्ययः शाश्वतधर्मगोप्ता सनातनस्त्वं पुरुषो मतो मे ||
snippets.transliteration:
aneka-bāhūdara-vaktra-netraṁ
paśhyāmi tvāṁ sarvato ’nanta-rūpam
nāntaṁ na madhyaṁ na punas tavādiṁ
paśhyāmi viśhveśhvara viśhva-rūpa

kirīṭinaṁ gadinaṁ chakriṇaṁ cha
tejo-rāśhiṁ sarvato dīptimantam
paśhyāmi tvāṁ durnirīkṣhyaṁ samantād
dīptānalārka-dyutim aprameyam

tvam akṣharaṁ paramaṁ veditavyaṁ
tvam asya viśhvasya paraṁ nidhānam
tvam avyayaḥ śhāśhvata-dharma-goptā
sanātanas tvaṁ puruṣho mato me
verseTranslations: I see Thee, infinite in form, with, as it were, faces, eyes and limbs everywhere; no beginning, no middle, no end; O Thou Lord of the Universe, Whose Form is universal!
I see thee with the crown, the sceptre and the discus; a blaze of splendour. Scarce can I gaze on thee, so radiant thou art, glowing like the blazing fire, brilliant as the sun, immeasurable.
Imperishable art Thou, the Sole One worthy to be known, the priceless Treasure-house of the universe, the immortal Guardian of the Life Eternal, the Spirit Everlasting.
snippets.commentary:
Out of *compassion*, you explained to me that you are the source of all beings.

You are the resting place of all beings. Nothing exists which is away from you. Everything I see is the manifestation of you alone.

So now my *delusion* is gone about what is right and what is wrong. However, I would like to see that form of yours in its totality in one place. In the previous chapters we have seen his *prakriti* Astada Prakruti.

So you can say you can experience, you are seeing it every day. His Eightfold Prakriti, you are experiencing and seeing every day. But I still can't see it in one place.

I basically see as the plurality what I want to see as one entity. That's basically what we are all struggling with. Intellectually, we understand what Bhagavad Gita says.

But when it comes to day-to-day life, it is very difficult to comprehend. So Arjuna said, my *delusion* is gone. I understand, but I want to see it, I want to experience it.

And in response, Bhagavan said that if you wish to, I will show you, but you will not be able to see it from your present way of looking at the world, from your present eyes. You will not be able to see it the way you see the world right now -- it will remain divided. Because right now I see my world as I, an individual, and everything else as individual entities.

If I see it that way, I will never be able to see the unity in them. If I change my perspective and see it from the singularity's point of view, and include myself in it, then I'll be able to see it. That's you have to change your perspective.

So I'll give you that perspective. Divyam Dadami te Chakshuhu. I'll give you that vision and then you will be able to see.

Having said that, he showed the Swarupa, and Sanjaya was the witness. He confirmed that, yes, Yogeshwara Krishna showed Arjuna his Virat Swarupa. And Sanjaya described on his own what Arjuna saw: Aneka Vaktra Bahu -- many mouths and many hands, as if thousands of suns were blazing in the sky at the same time.

It is so resplendent and difficult to see. He also showed us Arjuna's reaction: having seen that, Arjuna -- Pranamya Shirasa Devam -- as soon as he saw who Krishna in his real form is, he basically completely surrendered to him. And then what he said is this.

Now we are discussing from verse 15 onward. As we have discussed before, the Bhagavad Gita is generally in Anushtup Chanda. But these verses are in Trishtup Chanda, because there is more to describe.

So these are much longer verses, with more words packed into each verse. This is beautiful poetry, a prayer describing the nature of the Supreme Being. From Arjuna's perspective, when he sees that Swarupa, he sees things which are common to his experiences.

When we go to any other town -- like we went to New York and I say I'll go to Manhattan -- what am I going to say? I'm going to see the buildings, 911 memorial, One World Tower, because that's the world I see is what Manhattan is all about. So now what Arjuna sees in that Swarupa is what he is familiar with. He says, pasyami Devan Tava Deva, Deva Sarvantatham Bhuta Visesanga O Deva.

He doesn't say Krishna anymore, but O resplendent Being. I see in your body all the other Devas. In this Puranic culture, we have assigned deities to each force of nature, and those resplendent beings, the Devas -- he said, I see in your body all of them.

Pasyami Devan, Tava Deva Dehe. In your body I see them all. Tatha Bhuta Visesa Sangana, various groups of other beings.

Brahmanam Isam, Kamala, Sanastha -- and I see the Lord Brahma. Both ways. He said, this could mean Lord Brahma, or it could mean Brahma and Isha -- Brahma and Shiva -- Kamala Sanastha sitting on the lotus.

I see the whole creation in you, and I see the Creator himself. You are the creation and you are the creator. I see everything all in one.

Tatahu Rishis Cha Sarva -- and I see all the rishis. It's like everything is flashing through his eyes. Everything he has learned about divinity in this world is flashing at the same time.

And also Uragan Cha Divyan -- and I see also the divine serpents. This is one of the techniques poets use -- to take you to the most sublime level and then bring you all the way down to the lowest of the low. So I see all the divine beings, including the Lord Creator himself, but also all the serpents.

The entire universe, from the lowest of the low to the highest of the high -- I see in your body at one time. And then he says Aneka Bahu Udar Vaktra Netra. Sanjaya has already described that before to Dhritarashtra.

Now Arjuna himself says: I see infinite hands. Bahu -- hands, Udara -- stomachs, Vaktra -- mouths, Netra -- eyes. Pasyami tvam Sarvato Anantarupam: I see you facing everywhere.

He is now realizing that this is not something he will be able to describe. Infinite mouths, infinite hands, infinite eyes. As we have discussed earlier, once you take the space out of our world and keep all the beings lumped as one..

Right now I have two hands and you have two hands. But when you are together there are many hands. All the hands in this world are his hands.

All the legs in this world are his legs. All the mouths in this world are his mouths. He is experiencing that.

But then he says, anywhere I see -- you know, like a 360-degree movie projected all over. You are focused on one side, and what happened to the other side? Still the same movie, just different parts. But we can't describe where that movie starts and where that picture ends.

We actually went to the 9/11 memorial. They have a presentation on three sides. When people enter, they start putting their strollers against those walls as if they're just walls.

Then someone comes and moves all of them because the movie is going to play on all three sides. Then we are focusing on one wall and realize, oh, there are details I'm missing on this side. And then, what about that side? We realized we will never be able to capture all three sides at the same time.

It's beyond my capacity to see all three sides at once. So Arjuna is experiencing something at a much grander scale and says, I will not be able to describe everything that I can see. Pasyami tvam Sarvato Anantarupam -- I see you everywhere with infinite forms.

There is no end to what I see in you. Naantam Namadhyam Napunah Ta Adim -- we have learned this before in previous chapters. Bhagavan himself said: I don't have any beginning, I don't have any end.

I am the resting place of everything. Now Arjuna tells him: Bhagavan, I see you as you are -- no end, no beginning, no origin. Pasyami Vishweshvara Vishwaroopa -- he is accepting the fact that you are the Lord of all the universe, and this is your Vishwaroopa.

This is your infinite form. What I'm experiencing now is your real nature: you are beginningless, you have no middle and no end. Wherever we stand is the ever-present.

Whatever we left behind is our past. What we have not yet experienced is our future. But if we experience all of it at the same time, there is no beginning, no end, no past, no future.

So he's seeing everything in his present. You are the Lord of the whole universe and I am seeing your Vishwaroopa. Kiritinam Gadhinam Chakrinam Cha -- here, Arjuna is now recognizing that what he's seeing is the divine form he always perceived as the Lord.

Kiritinam Gadhinam Chakrinam Cha Tejo Rashim Sarvato Diptim Anantam: I see you with the crown, the club, and the discus -- the universal form of Vishnu with his four hands holding a lotus, a club, a discus, and a conch. And then he is wearing the crown. Only one who has complete control of his self can wear the crown.

Vishnu is the only one who has complete control of the self. Therefore he wears the crown, which means he has the authority. We wear the crown temporarily.

Whenever I feel I am in authority, I wear my crown. But that only lasts for a limited period of time. My authority slips away before I even realize.

My authority is like the cardboard crown in a drama. While I'm on this drama stage, I have that cardboard crown. As soon as I'm off this stage, the crown is gone.

Vishnu carries that authority all the time. That's why he wears the crown. So he holds the lotus which signifies purity and knowledge.

And then he has a conch to wake you up from your ignorance. If you don't listen to the call for waking up, then he uses his club, the gada, to shape you up. And if you shape up, all well and good.

If not, the chakra will annihilate you, just destroy you. So that's how the creation and maintenance continue. Bhagavan gives you all the chances to shape up.

If you don't shape up, time will take care of you. So Arjuna sees that form as the totality. Kiritinam Gadhinam Chakrinam Cha Tejo Rashim Sarvato Diptim Anantam -- a mass of radiance.

Sarvato Diptim -- blazing everywhere. In the previous verses, Sanjaya says it is like a thousand suns blazing in the sky. Here Arjuna says Tejo Rashim Sarvato Diptim Anantam -- everywhere it's blazing.

And what he's seeing is not the light of any sun, but the light of the self, the consciousness, that which illumines everything. Anant Diptim -- infinite teja. So he is experiencing resplendence of the self.

Pasyami tvam Durniriksham Samantha. But it is difficult to see. It is difficult to perceive the light of consciousness itself.

Through the light of my consciousness, I understand everything. I see all these things -- Kiritinam Gadhinam Chakrinam Cha -- the crown, the club, the discus. But seeing the consciousness itself, your splendid being, is difficult to see directly.

From the light of my consciousness, I can describe everything. But describing my consciousness itself is not possible. So Dur Niriksham -- I cannot grasp it.

Dur Niriksham Dipta Anala Arka Dyutim Aprameyam. That light is blazing all around like fire and sun, and it's incomprehensible. He comes to the conclusion that what he is seeing is undefinable.

At the same time, whatever I want to see, I'll see in it. In any museum or gallery, we go and look at the pictures. Every visitor will see something different.

Even in our world, we see what we want to see. We'll never see the things we do not want to see. As soon as we see something which is not conducive, we will run away from it.

Many years ago, when I first started working on a forensic lab and medical examiner's office, the first time I met with them they shared statistics about how many people go through an autopsy, how many people die. And the statistics showed something like one in four persons goes through an autopsy.
snippets.reflection:
Arjuna declares three profound realizations: he sees the Lord everywhere with "no beginning, no middle, no end"; he sees the radiance that is difficult to gaze upon, "glowing like blazing fire, brilliant as the sun, immeasurable"; and he recognizes Krishna as "Imperishable, the Sole One worthy to be known, the priceless Treasure-house of the universe, the immortal Guardian of the Life Eternal." The vision reveals that what we normally see as limited forms with clear boundaries - a beginning here, an end there - are actually expressions of something without any such limits.

Consider how we normally perceive everything with boundaries: this person started here and will end there, this project has a deadline, this relationship has a history. We carve up reality into manageable pieces. But Arjuna now sees that these boundaries are imposed by our minds, not inherent in reality itself. The crown, scepter, and discus he sees represent complete authority (crown), the power to shape (scepter), and the wheel of time and action (discus) - symbols that Krishna is not merely present in the universe but is its controller, sustainer, and essential nature.

For your practice today, look at something you consider "complete" - a finished task, a relationship that ended, a chapter of life that closed - and contemplate: Where exactly did it begin? What conditions led to those conditions? Trace backward and notice how the "beginning" dissolves into endless prior causes. Then trace forward: How does what ended continue to influence the present? See how "no beginning, no middle, no end" applies even to ordinary experiences. This contemplation can soften the rigid boundaries we place on life events and open us to sensing the continuous, beginningless, endless flow of existence.
snippets.shortReflection: You think everything has clear edges: this relationship started here, that job ended there, you were born on this date. But trace any beginning backward or any ending forward and the boundaries dissolve. Where do 'you' actually begin or end?

snippets.title: Day 148: The Worlds Tremble
snippets.sanskrit:

पश्यामि त्वां दीप्तहुताशवक्त्रम् स्वतेजसा विश्वमिदं तपन्तम् ||

द्यावापृथिव्योरिदमन्तरं हि व्याप्तं त्वयैकेन दिशश्च सर्वाः |
दृष्ट्वाऽद्भुतं रूपमुग्रं तवेदं लोकत्रयं प्रव्यथितं महात्मन् ||

snippets.transliteration:
anādi-madhyāntam ananta-vīryam ananta-bāhuṁ śhaśhi-sūrya-netram
paśhyāmi tvāṁ dīpta-hutāśha-vaktram sva-tejasā viśhvam idaṁ tapantam

dyāv ā-pṛithivyor idam antaraṁ hi
vyāptaṁ tvayaikena diśhaśh cha sarvāḥ
dṛiṣhṭvādbhutaṁ rūpam ugraṁ tavedaṁ

verseTranslations: Without beginning, without middle and without end, infinite in power, Thine arms all-embracing, the sun and moon Thine eyes, Thy face beaming with the fire of sacrifice, flooding the whole universe with light.
Alone thou fillest all the quarters of the sky, earth and heaven, and the regions between. O Almighty Lord! Seeing Thy marvellous and awe-inspiring Form, the spheres tremble with fear.
The troops of celestial beings enter into Thee, some invoking Thee in fear, with folded palms; the Great Seers and Adepts sing hymns to Thy Glory, saying All Hail.'
snippets.commentary:
In the last chapter, Arjuna had asked Krishna: tell me how I should feel your presence, the presence of the divine, the presence of that all-pervading *self*, and how I can meditate upon that. In response, Bhagavan gave him various examples of excellence in this world from various walks of life -- applicable to Arjuna and also to us -- showing that from our day-to-day life, from our cultural backgrounds, from our spiritual quest, we find examples all around us of excellence and can feel the Lord's presence.

As we discussed in chapter 10, anytime I see excellence, my mind recognizes it as God's blessings, the grace of God. In other words, divinity is evident in excellence. Bhagavan gave various examples for Arjuna and said, when you see this, it will remind you of my presence in all things and beings.

I'm not limited to those excellent manifestations, but that's where you will find it easier to experience my presence. And now that Arjuna has heard that, he says: I'm still not experiencing that oneness, the oneness which you talk about throughout this discourse. I have intellectually appreciated it and come to the conclusion that that's what it is -- that there is one singular entity pervading this entire universe, which is you, the Supreme *self*.

But I need to have that experience. I would like to experience that oneness. This, is similar to how we scientifically make any concept or theory our own *knowledge*.

First I need to gather all the evidence and data. And then, once I have gathered all the data and evidence, I need to demonstrate that the phenomenon exists. I gather all information about how water is formed.

In chemistry class, two molecules of hydrogen and one molecule of oxygen can create water. But at some point, I want to see the demonstration -- in the lab, I create that situation and then see how hydrogen and oxygen create water. In a similar fashion, Arjuna has now understood, but he wants to see a demonstration.

So the chapter starts with Arjuna Vacha. Arjuna said: Mat Anugraha Ya Paramam Guhyam Adhyatma Sangnitam Yat Tvaya Uktam Vachasthena Moho Ayam Vigato Mama. With your compassion for me, you have given me this secret knowledge.

And as you have said, the *self* is indestructible, imperishable. One who considers himself to be the slayer or the slain -- in both cases, he is wrong. There is nothing to grieve over in the changes which take place in this world, including death, because death is not the end of existence.

It is only the end of existence in the form of this body. So Moho Ayam Vigato Mama -- by this discourse of yours, you have given me the secret knowledge. Bhavapyayo Hi Bhutanam Shrutao Vistaraso Maya Tvattah Kamala Patraksha Mahatmyam Api Cha Avyayam -- I have also heard the origin and destruction of beings, O lotus-eyed Krishna, from you, and also your inexhaustible greatness.

I heard the greatness of the self, the supreme Brahman, that which is not limited by anything. And therefore my delusion is gone. I understand it clearly now.

Evam Etat Yatha Attha Tvam Atmanam Parameshwara Drashtum Icchami Te Rupam Aishwaram Purushottamam. However, I would like to see that form as you described yourself -- that oneness in this world of plurality. I have understood that you pervade the entire universe and therefore there is no existence separate from you.

However, at this time I cannot see that, and I would like to see that. I would like to experience that oneness of yours. Manyase Yadi Tat Shakyam Maya Drashtum Iti Prabho -- if you think it is possible for me to see that divine form, then, O Lord of Yogas, show me that imperishable form which includes everything in this world.

I would like to see that complete form of yours where everything is in yourself. It is easier for me to see your presence in this world of plurality. It is easier for me to see gold in gold jewelry.

I can take one look at it, experience the gold in it, then pick up another piece. As long as the excellence is there, in other words, the gold is apparent and not covered by something -- the gold is manifested in the jewelry -- I can see the gold in it. So it is easier to see the divinity in the world of plurality for us.

What is not possible for us generally is seeing all the plurality in that one single entity. I can imagine that God is in you. God is in me, God is in He, God is in she.

If my mind and intellect has achieved that level of purity, level of understanding, then I start seeing the divinity in all beings. And therefore, in our culture, when we meet each other, we say, namaste, Namah te, I bow down to you. I'm not bowing down to the limited self which is standing in front of me.

Because I may have my own opinion about that person, but I still do. Namaste to all of the people I meet, at least culturally. That's what we should be doing or we are doing.

Who we are bowing down to is the divinity in that person that I recognize. The divinity in me and divinity in you is the same. So I respect the divinity in you.

I bow down to you with that recognition. My transaction with you would be always of very friendly, very congenial, and not adversarial. Because I have recognized that myself and yourself has one thing in common, that consciousness, the divinity which makes me who I am.

The same divinity, the same consciousness is within you. What I have trouble imagining or perceiving or seeing is that the whole divinity is one, and you and I are in it. And we have heard in Bhagavad Gita before, Bhagavan says, I am not in them, they are in me.

The car is in the space, the space is not in the car. When I see a car which was built in Germany, there was space inside. When it was in Germany, there was German space.

And they seal it tight and then transport that car to United States. Now the car is here, the space is still intact which was sealed in Germany. Now, whether the space in the United States is the German space or American space in the car -- obviously the answer is simple.

The space inside the car is American space. So what happened to the German space which was in the car when it was sealed tight in Germany? The answer obviously depends on our way of seeing space. As long as I see the space in the car, I have difficulty imagining what happened to that German space.

When it came to America, the space was inside the car. The car was never opened till it came here. Well, it should still be German space in it, right? But if I start seeing that the space was not in the car, but the car was in the space, then I do not have any difficulty.

The car was traveling in the space. And therefore wherever the car is, that country's space is in that car, because the car is traveling in the space. For me to imagine that, I have to first have a perception of space as a totality without any gap.

If German space is one space and American space is another space, I will have difficulty. But if I can imagine a homogeneous, continuous, universal space, now I can see everything is in it. So what you and I have difficulty in recognizing is the unity between myself and yourself and herself, and also the objects in this room -- this is because of the distance between us.

I am here and you are there, you are there and she is somewhere else. What is separating us from each other is the space. What is separating me from my father is the time.

My father lived up to 1975 and I'm here today in 2014 thinking about it. So we are separated from each other by time. So there are two things which creates this world of plurality for me, and that is space and time.

We have also heard from sages and scientists that this concept of space and this concept of time is creation of my mind. So one can say, well, what is the distance between here and D.C.? It's too long a journey. And somebody else will say it's too close, it's only a two hour drive.

So my mind creates the valuation of whether it's too far or too close -- that's the conception of space in my mind. Same thing with time. If somebody says I'll be back in half an hour, well, is it too soon for me or too long for me? I can't wait for half an hour.

You need to be back here in 10 minutes. Because my conception of time is different than his conception of time. For him half an hour is too short, and for me half an hour is too long.

Well, anytime somebody goes to India for a vacation and when they come back, and if I ask that person, so how was your vacation? The answer is it was great, but it was too short. And I say, how long were you there? He said four weeks. For me, that's too long a time.

I only go there for a week or two. So for me a two weeks vacation is good enough, but for them four weeks is too short, because when you are enjoying yourself, four weeks seems too short. But if you were suffering because of the heat or monsoon and all the other things which we normally complain about, you'll say, boy, it was too long.

I tried, and then I finally was ready to get out. So even time is a concept of my mind. If these two concepts of my mind are wiped out, then I will see the world completely differently.

If the concept of space is wiped out from my mind, then I will see you and I and everyone in this room come together as one entity. There is no space between us. We are all joined together and we will be one entity with different limbs, but we are all together.

Good analogy in his commentary. There is a toy maker making toys from clay. And he has various toys and various dolls: elephant, tiger, baby and a bird.

And then he decided, no, this is not good. I need to use this clay for something much larger, more sellable. He takes all those dolls and compresses them into one ball of clay.

And when he compressed them together, what he has done is taken all the space away from each other. Previously they were sitting on a table or in a display box as separate entities. Once he gathers them and lumps them into one, now it's a big lump of clay.

At the same time, I can see the face of the elephant on the surface of that lump. I also see the baby's smile. I also see the tiger's face.

What is taken away from each other is the space. The same way, the events in my life have a time value -- it was in my past, or it is in my present, or it will be in my future. My childhood is in my past.

My youth is in my past. My old age is in my present.
snippets.reflection:
These verses reveal the cosmic form as filling all space between heaven and earth, with the sun and moon as eyes, and a face beaming with sacrificial fire "flooding the whole universe with light." Arjuna observes that all three worlds tremble with awe and fear at this vision, while celestial beings enter into the Lord - some invoking Him in fear with folded palms, while Great Seers and Adepts sing hymns saying "All Hail." This shows that even enlightened beings respond to ultimate reality with reverence and wonder.

 The key teaching here involves space and time as mental constructs that create our experience of separation. 's analogy of the toymaker is illuminating: when clay dolls - elephant, tiger, baby, bird - are compressed into one ball, all the space between them disappears, yet traces of each remain visible on the surface. Similarly, what separates you from your father is time; what separates you from your neighbor is space. Remove these mental constructs, and all beings merge into one entity.

 This is not philosophy but a description of actual perception when the divine vision is granted. For today's practice, work with your perception of space. When you see a friend, recognize that the "distance" between you is a concept in your mind. When you remember someone who has passed, notice that the "time" separating you is also a mental construct. Experiment with the feeling of closeness to someone physically far away, or connection to an ancestor long gone. What changes when you treat space and time not as absolute barriers but as perspectives that can shift? This is the beginning of understanding how Arjuna could see "the whole universe, movable and immovable" within a single form.
snippets.shortReflection: The distance between you and your friend is just a thought. The time between you and your grandmother is just a mental construct. What changes when you realize that space and time are perspectives, not prisons?

Seeing Thy stupendous Form, O Most Mighty, with its myriad faces, its innumerable eyes and limbs and terrible jaws, I myself and all the worlds are overwhelmed with awe.
When I see Thee, touching the Heavens, glowing with colour, with open mouth and wide open fiery eyes, I am terrified. O My Lord! My courage and peace of mind desert me.
snippets.commentary:
In the last chapter, Arjuna had asked Krishna: tell me how I should feel your presence, the presence of the divine, the presence of that all-pervading *self*, and how I can meditate upon that. In response, Bhagavan gave him various examples of excellence in this world from various walks of life -- applicable to Arjuna and also to us -- showing that from our day-to-day life, from our cultural backgrounds, from our spiritual quest, we find examples all around us of excellence and can feel the Lord's presence.

As we discussed in chapter 10, anytime I see excellence, my mind recognizes it as God's blessings, the grace of God. In other words, divinity is evident in excellence. Bhagavan gave various examples for Arjuna and said, when you see this, it will remind you of my presence in all things and beings.

I'm not limited to those excellent manifestations, but that's where you will find it easier to experience my presence. And now that Arjuna has heard that, he says: I'm still not experiencing that oneness, the oneness which you talk about throughout this discourse. I have intellectually appreciated it and come to the conclusion that that's what it is -- that there is one singular entity pervading this entire universe, which is you, the Supreme *self*.

But I need to have that experience. I would like to experience that oneness. This, is similar to how we scientifically make any concept or theory our own *knowledge*.

First I need to gather all the evidence and data. And then, once I have gathered all the data and evidence, I need to demonstrate that the phenomenon exists. I gather all information about how water is formed.

In chemistry class, two molecules of hydrogen and one molecule of oxygen can create water. But at some point, I want to see the demonstration -- in the lab, I create that situation and then see how hydrogen and oxygen create water. In a similar fashion, Arjuna has now understood, but he wants to see a demonstration.

So the chapter starts with Arjuna Vacha. Arjuna said: Mat Anugraha Ya Paramam Guhyam Adhyatma Sangnitam Yat Tvaya Uktam Vachasthena Moho Ayam Vigato Mama. With your compassion for me, you have given me this secret knowledge.

And as you have said, the *self* is indestructible, imperishable. One who considers himself to be the slayer or the slain -- in both cases, he is wrong. There is nothing to grieve over in the changes which take place in this world, including death, because death is not the end of existence.

It is only the end of existence in the form of this body. So Moho Ayam Vigato Mama -- by this discourse of yours, you have given me the secret knowledge. Bhavapyayo Hi Bhutanam Shrutao Vistaraso Maya Tvattah Kamala Patraksha Mahatmyam Api Cha Avyayam -- I have also heard the origin and destruction of beings, O lotus-eyed Krishna, from you, and also your inexhaustible greatness.

I heard the greatness of the self, the supreme Brahman, that which is not limited by anything. And therefore my delusion is gone. I understand it clearly now.

Evam Etat Yatha Attha Tvam Atmanam Parameshwara Drashtum Icchami Te Rupam Aishwaram Purushottamam. However, I would like to see that form as you described yourself -- that oneness in this world of plurality. I have understood that you pervade the entire universe and therefore there is no existence separate from you.

However, at this time I cannot see that, and I would like to see that. I would like to experience that oneness of yours. Manyase Yadi Tat Shakyam Maya Drashtum Iti Prabho -- if you think it is possible for me to see that divine form, then, O Lord of Yogas, show me that imperishable form which includes everything in this world.

I would like to see that complete form of yours where everything is in yourself. It is easier for me to see your presence in this world of plurality. It is easier for me to see gold in gold jewelry.

I can take one look at it, experience the gold in it, then pick up another piece. As long as the excellence is there, in other words, the gold is apparent and not covered by something -- the gold is manifested in the jewelry -- I can see the gold in it. So it is easier to see the divinity in the world of plurality for us.

What is not possible for us generally is seeing all the plurality in that one single entity. I can imagine that God is in you. God is in me, God is in He, God is in she.

If my mind and intellect has achieved that level of purity, level of understanding, then I start seeing the divinity in all beings. And therefore, in our culture, when we meet each other, we say, namaste, Namah te, I bow down to you. I'm not bowing down to the limited self which is standing in front of me.

Because I may have my own opinion about that person, but I still do. Namaste to all of the people I meet, at least culturally. That's what we should be doing or we are doing.

Who we are bowing down to is the divinity in that person that I recognize. The divinity in me and divinity in you is the same. So I respect the divinity in you.

I bow down to you with that recognition. My transaction with you would be always of very friendly, very congenial, and not adversarial. Because I have recognized that myself and yourself has one thing in common, that consciousness, the divinity which makes me who I am.

The same divinity, the same consciousness is within you. What I have trouble imagining or perceiving or seeing is that the whole divinity is one, and you and I are in it. And we have heard in Bhagavad Gita before, Bhagavan says, I am not in them, they are in me.

The car is in the space, the space is not in the car. When I see a car which was built in Germany, there was space inside. When it was in Germany, there was German space.

And they seal it tight and then transport that car to United States. Now the car is here, the space is still intact which was sealed in Germany. Now, whether the space now in the United States is the German space or American space in the car, obviously the answer is simple.

The space inside the car is American space. So what happened to the German space which was in the car when it was still tight in Germany? The answer obviously is in our way of seeing space. As long as I see the space in the car, I have difficulty imagining what happening to that space which was German space.

When it came to America, the space was inside the car. Car was never opened till it came here. Well, it should have been a German space in it.

But if I start seeing that the space was not in the car, the car was in the space, then I do not have any difficulty. Car was traveling in the space. And therefore wherever the car is, that country space is in that car, because car is traveling in the space.

For me to imagine that, I have to first have a perception of a space as a totality without any gap. A German space is one space, an American space is another space, I will have difficulty. But if I can imagine a homogeneous, continuous, universal space, now I can see everything is in it.

So what you and I have difficulty in recognizing the unity between myself and yourself and herself, and also the objects in this room is because of the distance between us. I am here and you are there, you are there and she is somewhere else. What is separating us from each other is the space.

What is separating me from my father is the time. My father lived up to 1975 and I'm here today in 2014 thinking about it. So we are separated from each other by time.

So there are two things which creates this world of plurality for me, and that is space and time. We have also heard from sages and scientists that this concept of space and this concept of time is creation of my mind. So one can say, well, what is the distance between here to D.C.

And so on. So it's too long a journey. And somebody will say it's too close, it's only two hour drive.

So my mind creates the valuation whether it's too far or too little, that the conception of space in my mind, same thing. If somebody says I'll be back in half an hour, well, is it too soon for me or too long for me? I can't wait for half an hour. You need to be back here in 10 minutes.

Because my conception of time is different than his conception of time. For him half an hour is too short, and for me half an hour is too long. Well, anytime somebody goes to India for a vacation and when they come back, and if I ask that person, so how was your vacation? The answer is it was great, but it was too short.

And I say, how long were you there? He said four weeks for me, too long a time. I only go there for a week or two. So for me a two weeks vacation is good enough for them four weeks is too short, because when you are enjoying their four weeks seems too short.

But if you were suffering because of the heat or monsoon and all the other things which we normally complain about, if I'm suffering. I'll say, boy, it was too long when I tried. And then I finally was ready to get out.

So even time is a concept of my mind. If these two concepts of my mind are wiped out, then I will see the world completely differently. If the concept of space is wiped out from my mind, then I will see you and I and everyone in this room come together as one entity.

There is no space between us. We are all joined together and we will be one entity with different limbs, but we are all together. Good analogy in his commentary.

There is a toy maker making toys from clay. And he has various toys and various dolls. Elephant, tiger, baby and a bird.

And then he decided, no, this is not good. I need to use this clay for something much larger, more sellable. He takes all those dolls and compresses them into one ball of clay.

And when he compressed them together, what he has done is taken all the space away from each other. Previously they were sitting on a table or in a display box as separate entity. Once he gathers them and lumps them into one.

And now a big lump of clay. At the same time, I can see the face of the elephant on that surface of that lump. Also see the baby smile.

Also see the tiger's face. What is taken away from each other is the space. The same way the events in my life has a time value of it was in my past, or it is in my present, or it will be in my future.

My childhood is in my past. My youth is in my past. My old age is in my present.
snippets.reflection:
In these verses, Arjuna witnesses hosts of beings - Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, Sadhyas, divine healers, the Winds, demons and saints alike - all gazing at the cosmic form in amazement. Then comes a shift: Arjuna begins to feel overwhelmed and terrified. Seeing the stupendous form with myriad faces, innumerable eyes and limbs, and "terrible jaws," he confesses: "I am terrified. My courage and peace of mind desert me." The vision that began with wonder now reveals its awe-inspiring and fearsome aspect.

This is a crucial teaching about spiritual growth. We often approach the divine expecting only comfort, beauty, and peace. But the complete vision includes what we might call the "terrible" aspects - destruction, death, the dissolution of everything we hold dear. Arjuna wanted to see totality, and totality includes both creation and destruction, both the pleasant and the fearsome. His terror is the natural response of the ego when it confronts something that completely transcends its capacity to control or even comprehend.

Today, reflect on what aspects of reality you resist seeing. Do you avoid thinking about death? Do you turn away from suffering in the world? Do you prefer a "nice" spiritual path without difficult truths? Arjuna's experience suggests that mature spirituality requires facing the full picture - not just the comforting divine but also the destroyer, not just light but also the consuming fire. Ask yourself: What would it mean to accept that the same consciousness that creates also destroys? That the God you pray to for protection is also the power behind everything that threatens you? Sitting with this paradox, without resolving it too quickly, is itself a spiritual practice.
snippets.shortReflection: You want a spiritual path that feels good - peace, light, comfort. But the full picture includes everything you'd rather not look at: death, loss, the destruction of what you love. Are you ready for the whole truth, or just the pleasant parts?

verseTranslations: When I see Thy mouths with their fearful jaws like glowing fires at the dissolution of creation, I lose all sense of place; I find no rest. Be merciful, O Lord in whom this universe abides!
All these sons of Dhritarashtra, with the hosts of princes, Bheeshma, Drona and Karna, as well as the other warrior chiefs belonging to our side;
I see them all rushing headlong into Thy mouths, with terrible tusks, horrible to behold. Some are mangled between thy jaws, with their heads crushed to atoms.
snippets.commentary:
We all want to know Bhagavan. But Bhagavan says, if I show you my Roop, it may not be as pleasant as you think.

So Arjuna asked for it and he got what he wished for. Both concepts of space and time are wiped out from his mind. Now he sees this entire Jagat without any space, and also without any time difference.

So first he described what he saw and said, I see that everything is within you. I see with many mouths, many hands, many stomachs, many legs. In other words, all the legs and all the mouths which I consider to be individually assigned to individual are all yours.

I see them all into you. He also saw everything that he has ever encountered in his life. Devas, all the deities -- I see all of them in you.

So he described what he sees. Then he also sees the condition of other beings looking at this great form: all these people are entering into you. Some are fearful and some are praising your glory.

Those who have not comprehended the reality are fearful of it. When we are not sure about the outcome of our actions in life, we are fearful. Those who are wise enough to not get perturbed by whatever the outcome is, they are blissful and praising the Lord because they have accepted everything.

So I see those wise people are praising you, but others are entering into you in fear. And then he says, I also see you as Vishnu. I see you as that Almighty Vishnu.

Kiritinam Gadinam, Chakri Namcha. With all your attributes, I see you. But then he says, I also don't see any middle, end or beginning.

And all the space between the heavens and earth is filled with you alone. Up till now what I considered nothingness -- there is no such thing as nothingness anymore. Everything is you and you alone.

So I see you all around me and everything in you. And now I also see how the world is looking at you, how the other beings react. He still keeps himself out of this.

He is an observer observing an object. His experience is all objective. Right now he is describing what's happening to others.

This is how we observe our world. We keep ourselves out of it and then say, oh, he is not doing exercise, he is going to be suffering, he is smoking, he is going to have cancer. We keep ourselves out of it.

We look at the world and see how they are doing and how they are feeling and how they are behaving. So up to now he is looking at everything and saying, everybody is entering into you. Some are fearful, some are praising you.

I see the deities, I see everything into. You are filling all the spaces. But then he starts having the other side of the experience.

It's not all wonderful -- life has its positive moments and negative moments. And when you focus on one, you can always give a biography of a person showing how great he was and how accomplished he was. Every funeral I go to, I realize there is not an average person in this world.

Everyone says how great the person was, what he accomplished, and how loving he was. I have never heard somebody say, "He was such an average person. He didn't really accomplish much in his life.

He was a terrible husband, a cruel father." Because we focus on what is good in that person, we highlight all the goodness in him. So up till now Arjuna was only focusing on the divinity. Then he sees Brahma seated on the lotus.

All the deities are praising, all the vasavas and maruts and everybody is praising. And they are all dumbfounded just looking at this great. They're looking in wonderment.

Even the wise person also gets awed by the nature. Even people like Einstein, who are pure scientists -- he could not figure out what God's game is all about. That's why he said, "God doesn't play dice." He had complete *faith* that God wouldn't be doing something random.

He had faith in God's laws of nature, that we can figure them out. This world is very predictable from our perspective; there's nothing unpredictable in this world, really. With that predictability, we can plan our life.

I'll get up at 6 o'clock and then I'll do this, then I'll be at class at 10. We can plan that because it's predictable. Everything you can predict from when I leave my house.

The unpredictable part is what will happen during that period. And once we look at that, we start getting fearful. Well, you can get in an accident.

You are at Times Square walking around and somebody just drives a car onto the sidewalk. It's unthinkable, unpredictable. Unpredictable things do occur.

So there is positive and there is negative. From our perspective, from our relative world, there is positive and negative. Now Arjuna, from his perspective, says what is also not so pleasant.

He says: Nabhas Sprisham Diptam Anek Varnam Vyattananam Dipta Vishala Netram Drashtva Hi Tvam Pravyathitantaratma Dhritim Na Vindami Shamam Cha Vishno. Having seen your form touching the sky, inflaming with many colors, your open mouth and fiery eyes -- I am shaken up inside. I have no courage, no peace.

Up till now, I had a place in this world where I had staked myself and said, "This is where I am, and this is who I am in relationship to the world." The moment I feel insignificant anywhere -- in my organization, in my society, in my community, in my family -- I start getting depressed. We keep our balance by having that *self*-assessment of ourselves as an important being. The moment we drop that, we become completely fearful.

We do not know where we stand. That's why when people retire, they often lose their sense of what is important. Roger Ailes ruled Fox channel for a long time.

As soon as he was disgraced and ousted, he died within a year. Had he still been at Fox, he probably would have continued for another 10 years. People lose their bearings in life and therefore lose their stability.

So he said, Dhritim Na Vindami Shamam Cha Vishno -- I do not see what I can do. I don't think I'm capable of anything, and I have no peace because of that. Danshtra Karalani Cha Te Mukhani -- now he gives the other side of the coin.

Up till now, he was talking about all existence, seeing everything existing in you. I see that everything is existing in you and everything is supported by you. But now he says Danshtra Karalani Cha Te Mukhani Drashtva Eva Kala Anala Sannibhani -- I see in your mouth these terrible teeth, fearsome teeth, and fire blazing in your mouth.

Disho Na Jane -- I don't see the directions. I do not see my place in life; I do not see my place in this universe. Up till now, I had a complete sense of who I am and where I am.

In my family, there is a placement -- I know who I am. I know who I am in my community. I know who I am in my company.

I know who I am as a citizen. There is a bearing I can describe. I'm at 1537B Knuckles Road.

I can tell you how to come to me. There is a complete sense of placement and direction. I am such-and-such in the community.

So I had a complete sense of my worth and my place in this universe. But once I see the mortality -- that everything is rushing towards you, and so am I -- that changes everything. Right now, I see my life in a static picture.

I always see myself as existing now. It's a static picture in my head. Everybody else sees me getting old.

It's very hard for you to imagine yourself to be growing and deteriorating. You have to constantly remind yourself, you know, I can't do that anymore. I have to keep telling myself, I'm an old man.

Because I don't see myself as an old man. I have to remind myself. The other day I was reading something.

Some psychoanalyst says that the difference between a normal person and a psychopath is that a psychopath has to be reminded that certain behavior is not acceptable. A normal person naturally knows what is acceptable behavior in a society. A person suffering from that mental condition who becomes a sociopath or psychopath does not have that natural bearing.

Somebody has to constantly tell him, "This is not acceptable, this is not acceptable." Only then can he function in society. So Arjuna said, having seen this mortality -- that everything is rushing towards you, that there are terrible teeth and blazing fire in your mouth, that you are the resting place of everything, that all names and forms, including mine, will be destroyed in you -- therefore, I do not know what my place in life is. I am fast-forwarding my life right now.

Normally, I see my life one frame at a time. Therefore, it is a static picture I am seeing. I see every moment as one frame at a time.

I have forgotten the last frame, and I don't know the next frame. It's a static picture, and I consider that as my existence. But fast-forward my life.

We have DVR, obviously -- we record all the shows. Sometimes I say, "Meena, you have 24 episodes of this Satyameva Jayate. When are we going to get rid of them?" She says, "Oh, no, no, I'll finish.

I'll do speed watching." I had heard of speed reading, but speed watching! Fast-forward for three minutes and the whole show is done. A person's whole episode is over in two minutes. If our life is fast-forwarded, the eulogy at the end of your life tells the story.

Somebody will give your entire life in two minutes: he was born in Surat, went to high school here, then went to architecture school, went to Africa, then taught Bhagavad Gita, and died. Entire life summarized in two minutes or less. When you fast-forward your life, the only thing you see is that you are rushing towards your death.

That's all you're doing every moment. And we have to keep reminding ourselves -- we have birthday celebrations to say, "This is not bad so far." So he said, I do not know where I stand. Disho Na Jane Na Labhe Cha Sharma.

Having seen my mortality and insignificance, I can't find any peace. What is the purpose of my life? We completely realize that all I consider to be my abilities are of no value when you are sick. And I have explained this before -- when you are sick, you can tell me anything about anything, but I'm not listening right now.

I just can't feel good about anything. I have a fever of 105 and you want to talk to me about Bhagavad Gita? Forget about it right now. I can't find any bearing.

And Arjuna said, I'm in that situation. I can't find it. So he said, Prasida Devesha Jagannivasa -- be gracious to me, O Lord of the universe.

This is, the true *surrender*. Intellectually saying "Bhagavan, tera tujhko arpan, kya lage mera" -- intellectual surrender really means nothing, because you still think "I am surrendering." That *ego* is still very much there. "I am good, I am doing puja, I am doing meditation." That "I" is so solidly there that the surrender is of not much value.
snippets.reflection:
Arjuna now sees the fearsome mouths with terrible jaws "like glowing fires at the dissolution of creation" and cries out: "I lose all sense of place; I find no rest." Even more disturbing, he sees all the sons of Dhritarashtra, Bhishma, Drona, Karna, and warriors from both armies rushing headlong into these terrible mouths, "some mangled between Thy jaws, with their heads crushed to atoms." The cosmic vision has revealed not just abstract unity but the concrete reality that everyone Arjuna knows is heading toward destruction.

 This is the point where intellectual understanding becomes visceral. We all know that everyone dies, but Arjuna is seeing it happen - not as a future event but as a present reality from the cosmic perspective. The verse about losing "all sense of place" is particularly significant. Our sense of identity depends on knowing our place - in family, society, time. When we see that this placement is temporary and that we are all rushing toward the same dissolution, our ordinary bearings disappear. This is terrifying for the ego but liberating for the seeker who is ready.

 For today's practice, try 's exercise of "fast-forwarding" your life. Imagine someone giving your eulogy - your entire life summarized in two minutes. What remains significant from this perspective? What falls away as trivial? Then extend this to everyone you will interact with today: each person you see is also moving toward their end. This is not meant to be morbid but to shift priorities. What conflicts would dissolve if you truly saw the temporary nature of all positions and identities? What kindness would become more natural? Let the awareness of universal mortality open compassion rather than despair.
snippets.shortReflection: Everyone you know is dying. Not someday - right now, with every breath. You can live as if you have forever, prioritizing trivial conflicts and petty wins, or you can let this truth reorganize what actually matters. Which will it be today?

snippets.title: Day 151: Rivers Rushing to the Sea

verseTranslations: As rivers in flood surge furiously to the ocean, so these heroes, the greatest among men, fling themselves into Thy flaming mouths.
As moths fly impetuously to the flame only to be killed, so these men rush into Thy mouths to court their own destruction.
Thou seemest to swallow up the worlds, to lap them in flame. Thy glory fills the universe. Thy fierce rays beat down upon it irresistibly.
snippets.commentary:
In the last chapter, Arjuna had asked Krishna: tell me how I should feel your presence, the presence of the divine, the presence of that all-pervading *self*, and how I can meditate upon that. In response, Bhagavan gave him various examples of excellence in this world from various walks of life -- applicable to Arjuna and also to us -- showing that from our day-to-day life, from our cultural backgrounds, from our spiritual quest, we find examples all around us of excellence and can feel the Lord's presence.

As we discussed in chapter 10, anytime I see excellence, my mind recognizes it as God's blessings, the grace of God. In other words, divinity is evident in excellence. Bhagavan gave various examples for Arjuna and said, when you see this, it will remind you of my presence in all things and beings.

I'm not limited to those excellent manifestations, but that's where you will find it easier to experience my presence. And now that Arjuna has heard that, he says: I'm still not experiencing that oneness, the oneness which you talk about throughout this discourse. I have intellectually appreciated it and come to the conclusion that that's what it is -- that there is one singular entity pervading this entire universe, which is you, the Supreme *self*.

But I need to have that experience. I would like to experience that oneness. This, is similar to how we scientifically make any concept or theory our own *knowledge*.

First I need to gather all the evidence and data. And then, once I have gathered all the data and evidence, I need to demonstrate that the phenomenon exists. I gather all information about how water is formed.

In chemistry class, two molecules of hydrogen and one molecule of oxygen can create water. But at some point, I want to see the demonstration -- in the lab, I create that situation and then see how hydrogen and oxygen create water. In a similar fashion, Arjuna has now understood, but he wants to see a demonstration.

So the chapter starts with Arjuna Vacha. Arjuna said: Mat Anugraha Ya Paramam Guhyam Adhyatma Sangnitam Yat Tvaya Uktam Vachasthena Moho Ayam Vigato Mama. With your compassion for me, you have given me this secret knowledge.

And as you have said, the *self* is indestructible, imperishable. One who considers himself to be the slayer or the slain -- in both cases, he is wrong. There is nothing to grieve over in the changes which take place in this world, including death, because death is not the end of existence.

It is only the end of existence in the form of this body. So Moho Ayam Vigato Mama -- by this discourse of yours, you have given me the secret knowledge. Bhavapyayo Hi Bhutanam Shrutao Vistaraso Maya Tvattah Kamala Patraksha Mahatmyam Api Cha Avyayam -- I have also heard the origin and destruction of beings, O lotus-eyed Krishna, from you, and also your inexhaustible greatness.

I heard the greatness of the self, the supreme Brahman, that which is not limited by anything. And therefore my delusion is gone. I understand it clearly now.

Evam Etat Yatha Attha Tvam Atmanam Parameshwara Drashtum Icchami Te Rupam Aishwaram Purushottamam. However, I would like to see that form as you described yourself -- that oneness in this world of plurality. I have understood that you pervade the entire universe and therefore there is no existence separate from you.

However, at this time I cannot see that, and I would like to see that. I would like to experience that oneness of yours. Manyase Yadi Tat Shakyam Maya Drashtum Iti Prabho -- if you think it is possible for me to see that divine form, then, O Lord of Yogas, show me that imperishable form which includes everything in this world.

I would like to see that complete form of yours where everything is in yourself. It is easier for me to see your presence in this world of plurality. It is easier for me to see gold in gold jewelry.

I can take one look at it, experience the gold in it, then pick up another piece. As long as the excellence is there, in other words, the gold is apparent and not covered by something -- the gold is manifested in the jewelry -- I can see the gold in it. So it is easier to see the divinity in the world of plurality for us.

What is not possible for us generally is seeing all the plurality in that one single entity. I can imagine that God is in you. God is in me, God is in He, God is in she.

If my mind and intellect has achieved that level of purity, level of understanding, then I start seeing the divinity in all beings. And therefore, in our culture, when we meet each other, we say, namaste, Namah te, I bow down to you. I'm not bowing down to the limited self which is standing in front of me.

Because I may have my own opinion about that person, but I still do. Namaste to all of the people I meet, at least culturally. That's what we should be doing or we are doing.

Who we are bowing down to is the divinity in that person that I recognize. The divinity in me and divinity in you is the same. So I respect the divinity in you.

I bow down to you with that recognition. My transaction with you would be always of very friendly, very congenial, and not adversarial. Because I have recognized that myself and yourself has one thing in common, that consciousness, the divinity which makes me who I am.

The same divinity, the same consciousness is within you. What I have trouble imagining or perceiving or seeing is that the whole divinity is one, and you and I are in it. And we have heard in Bhagavad Gita before, Bhagavan says, I am not in them, they are in me.

The car is in the space, the space is not in the car. When I see a car which was built in Germany, there was space inside. When it was in Germany, there was German space.

And they seal it tight and then transport that car to United States. Now the car is here, the space is still intact which was sealed in Germany. Now, whether the space now in the United States is the German space or American space in the car, obviously the answer is simple.

The space inside the car is American space. So what happened to the German space which was in the car when it was still tight in Germany? The answer obviously is in our way of seeing space. As long as I see the space in the car, I have difficulty imagining what happening to that space which was German space.

When it came to America, the space was inside the car. Car was never opened till it came here. Well, it should have been a German space in it.

But if I start seeing that the space was not in the car, the car was in the space, then I do not have any difficulty. Car was traveling in the space. And therefore wherever the car is, that country space is in that car, because car is traveling in the space.

For me to imagine that, I have to first have a perception of a space as a totality without any gap. A German space is one space, an American space is another space, I will have difficulty. But if I can imagine a homogeneous, continuous, universal space, now I can see everything is in it.

So what you and I have difficulty in recognizing the unity between myself and yourself and herself, and also the objects in this room is because of the distance between us. I am here and you are there, you are there and she is somewhere else. What is separating us from each other is the space.

What is separating me from my father is the time. My father lived up to 1975 and I'm here today in 2014 thinking about it. So we are separated from each other by time.

So there are two things which creates this world of plurality for me, and that is space and time. We have also heard from sages and scientists that this concept of space and this concept of time is creation of my mind. So one can say, well, what is the distance between here to D.C.

And so on. So it's too long a journey. And somebody will say it's too close, it's only two hour drive.

So my mind creates the valuation whether it's too far or too little, that the conception of space in my mind, same thing. If somebody says I'll be back in half an hour, well, is it too soon for me or too long for me? I can't wait for half an hour. You need to be back here in 10 minutes.

Because my conception of time is different than his conception of time. For him half an hour is too short, and for me half an hour is too long. Well, anytime somebody goes to India for a vacation and when they come back, and if I ask that person, so how was your vacation? The answer is it was great, but it was too short.

And I say, how long were you there? He said four weeks for me, too long a time. I only go there for a week or two. So for me a two weeks vacation is good enough for them four weeks is too short, because when you are enjoying their four weeks seems too short.

But if you were suffering because of the heat or monsoon and all the other things which we normally complain about, if I'm suffering. I'll say, boy, it was too long when I tried. And then I finally was ready to get out.

So even time is a concept of my mind. If these two concepts of my mind are wiped out, then I will see the world completely differently. If the concept of space is wiped out from my mind, then I will see you and I and everyone in this room come together as one entity.

There is no space between us. We are all joined together and we will be one entity with different limbs, but we are all together. Good analogy in his commentary.

There is a toy maker making toys from clay. And he has various toys and various dolls. Elephant, tiger, baby and a bird.

And then he decided, no, this is not good. I need to use this clay for something much larger, more sellable. He takes all those dolls and compresses them into one ball of clay.

And when he compressed them together, what he has done is taken all the space away from each other. Previously they were sitting on a table or in a display box as separate entity. Once he gathers them and lumps them into one.

And now a big lump of clay. At the same time, I can see the face of the elephant on that surface of that lump. Also see the baby smile.

Also see the tiger's face. What is taken away from each other is the space. The same way the events in my life has a time value of it was in my past, or it is in my present, or it will be in my future.

My childhood is in my past. My youth is in my past. My old age is in my present.
snippets.reflection:
Arjuna uses two powerful metaphors to describe what he sees: rivers flooding furiously into the ocean, and moths flying impetuously into flame "only to be killed." Both images share a common quality - the movement is irresistible and ends in dissolution of individual identity. The river does not choose to merge with the ocean; the moth does not choose to enter the flame. This is the inherent nature of manifestation returning to its source. Then Arjuna sees the Lord "swallowing up the worlds, lapping them in flame" with glory filling the universe.

The river metaphor is particularly instructive. A mighty river like the Ganges has its own identity, its own name, its own course through the landscape. People build cities on its banks, write poems about it, worship it. Yet eventually, inevitably, it disappears into the ocean and loses all separate identity. From the ocean's perspective, there is no Ganges - only water that briefly took a particular form and path. This is true of every individual life, every civilization, every world.

Today, contemplate your life as a river. Where did "you" really begin? In your birth? Your parents' meeting? The formation of Earth? Trace the current of your existence backward and find no true beginning. Now follow it forward - where does "you" end? In death? In the memories others hold? In the effects of your actions rippling outward? See how the boundaries of your identity are not as fixed as they appear. The practice is not to become nihilistic but to recognize that you are already part of the ocean taking the temporary form of a river. Living from this recognition brings both humility and freedom.
snippets.shortReflection: You have a name, a story, relationships, a career. It all feels so solid and permanent. But you're like a river that temporarily has its own identity before inevitably disappearing into the ocean. What would you do differently if you really felt this?

snippets.title: Day 152: I Am Time
