verseTranslations: Tell me then who Thou art, that wearest this dreadful Form? I bow before Thee, O Mighty One! Have mercy, I pray, and let me see Thee as Thou wert at first. I do not know what Thou intendest.

Lord Shri Krishna replied: I have shown myself to thee as the Destroyer who lays waste the world and whose purpose is destruction. In spite of thy efforts, all these warriors gathered for battle shall not escape death.
Then gird up thy loins and conquer. Subdue thy foes and enjoy the kingdom in prosperity. I have already doomed them. Be thou my instrument, Arjuna!
snippets.commentary:
We have seen Arjuna's description of what he is seeing, and we have discussed so many times in the last few weeks. What he has seen is everything that he can perceive in this world, all coming together as one, this plurality which is separated from each other.

Now he sees that as one singularity. He also sees all the *divine* beings which he has just heard of in his Vedic training or from the cultural training. He sees all of them -- Brahma, Vishnu, Mahesh -- all of them merged into this one entity.

But he also sees that all these beings are rushing towards the mouth of that supreme being and getting dissolved, disappearing into it. And he comes to this realization that just as the river water is rushing towards the ocean -- intuitively, with inherent nature, not that somebody is propelling it or forcing it, but by its inherent nature. The river water runs from the mountaintops through the plains to the ocean.

Just as the moth instinctively rush towards its death into the flame, river rushes towards the ocean, loses its identity. Mighty river, like Ganges or Yamuna or even Patomak or James, once it disappears into the ocean, there is no identity of the river of its own. It just becomes part of the ocean.

It seems that is the true nature of the river and the moth. So he sees that all the beings are without any hesitation, they're rushing towards the mouth of this great being and disappearing into it. And then he sees that this great being is seemingly enjoying this act of all these beings disappearing into his mouth, some get stuck.

He makes sure that nobody is left out when we do some task. And we are so happy about it, that we are so proud of that. In the end we try to inspect and say, is there anything left? That's basically equivalent to licking up what's going into his mouth -- making sure that all these beings are getting dissolved into his own being.

And now Arjuna says, I don't understand any of this. Akyahi me ko bhavan ugrarupaha -- tell me, O being with a very fierce form. Namostu te deva or prasida -- if you want to ask somebody who you are and that person is not smaller than you, you better be a little respectful first.

He does ask and say, I want to know who you are. But first, Namostute devara prasida -- you are the supreme Lord, so I bow down to you, have mercy on me, because I don't understand. I am not capable of understanding who you are.

And vignatum ichami bhavantam adyam -- I have completely and clearly recognized that you are the Adi being. You are the original being. All beings are nothing but the manifestation of you.

They come from you, they go into you. But you are that original Bhavantam adyam. You are that original being.

Vignatum ichami -- I want to know, which in normal terms we say, I want to know God. I know he is the supreme being. At least from my childhood religious training I understood that he controlled this world.

Vigna tam ichami bhavanta madhyam -- even after having this global vision, the cosmic vision, our intellect is not capable of understanding it. Nahi prajanami tavapravratyam -- also, I have no idea why you are doing this activity which I see right now. Isn't that something we ask all the time? I don't know why Bhagawan does this thing, why there is a tsunami, why there is an earthquake, or why Bill Gates and Steve Jobs are successful and not every IT person in this country.

I do not know what you are doing, Bhagwan. I hope you know what you are doing. Basically Arjuna puts it in his word very respectfully saying I want to know you O supreme Being.

I clearly recognize you are the original being, but I also don't understand what you are engaged in right now. I see all these beings going into your mouth and getting crushed. He has also seen -- we have seen -- that all Kauravas are going into his mouth, as well as all the great kings on both sides.

See, anytime we have a vision, we focus on something closer to our own situation. Anytime you have a dream, the dream is always something related to what you were thinking about in the last week or so. So even when he sees this whole cosmic vision, he focuses on the Kauravas going into his mouth.

All the kings from the Kauravas as well as the kings from our side, going into his mouth. He says, I don't understand what you are engaged in right now. And in response to that, Bhagavan says, Kalo'smi -- I am time.

Lokaksha Kruta Pravrad daha -- I am engaged in destroying this world. I can see the world from both perspectives. Either I can see it from a constructive perspective or a destructive perspective in nature.

Actually both simultaneously keeps going on. Something gets destroyed, something gets built. I can fix my perspective only on the destruction part and say why this thing is happening.

I can look at the statistics in the newspaper and say how many people die every day and say oh God, billions of people die. I don't know whether millions or billions, but I'm sure there are plenty because every several seconds there's somebody dies in the United States. I read somewhere about how many people die every day, and if I look at that and say God, why do you do this? This many people dying every day.

Don't you have better things to do than just killing? Right now Arjuna is just seeing this destruction going on. So Bhagavan's answer is also exactly that. Kalaha Asmi, I am all devouring time.

I was born in 1948. In 2012, I'm an old man, but sometime in the 2000-somethings I won't be around. That's what Lokakshaya krita pravadha means.

You're seeing me destroying this world. As you know, the world as I know right now, is actually rushing towards its own destruction. All my friends and relatives and all of them, one after the other, they're all rushing towards their own death.

Kalavasmi lokaksha Kruta Prabhradha. From your perspective, Arjuna, I am that all devouring time. Right now what you are seeing is I am engaged in destroying these worlds.

Lokan sama hartum iha pravrutaha ruteapi tvamna Bhavishyanti swarve e avasthitaha pratyanikeshi odaha. Even without you -- now coming down very personally to Arjuna -- Arjuna had said, I don't want to engage in this war. The whole purpose of this *divine* vision Arjuna wanted to have was connected to all the philosophy Bhagavan gave him in the second chapter about why he should engage in this war.

Bhagavan had said, look, whoever takes birth will die. Beginning they unmanifest, they will manifest for a while, they will unmanifest in the end. So you don't worry about it.

Whatever the little role you are given in this drama, you take part and take credit for it and you don't worry about who's going to die and who's going to survive. But Arjuna was not clear. So he said, well let me see this entire vision now.

He sees the entire vision and then he says I don't understand what are you doing? And Bhagawan basically said, don't worry about it, I am time. I'm going to destroy everything in time. Whether you take part in it or not.

Even without you, none of the warriors in front of you shall live. Whether you take part in this war or not is immaterial. Their destiny is to die in time.

Whenever their time will come, they will die. Because I am that all devouring time. Tasmat Utestha Yashola Basva -- all you have to do is take credit for it.

Everybody says Bill Clinton was the best president in his time. We all thrived and our country has this surplus we never had seen in all these times before. And George Bush came and completely messed it all up.

But I'll tell you what, if George Bush was the president at the time when the technology bubble was blowing up, he would have the same credit. He just happened to be at that time a president. And we can blame Obama all we want.

About 8% or 9% unemployment. But even if Bill Clinton is today, he would have the same problem. Because this thing is driven by this cycle, cosmic cycle, economic cycles, whatever the cycle you want to call it, you just happen to be there.

And if you're a smart person, you do your part and take credit. Become that instrument in this giant will of *dharma*. So therefore Bhagavan said, look, all these people are already killed by me.

Without your help also they will get killed. You just saw that every being is rushing towards their death in my mouth. Get up Yashola Basra and get the fame that you deserve.

Jitva Satrun Bhangshvarajam Samruddham -- get victory over your enemies and enjoy the kingdom. *maya* Evey Thai Nihitaha Purva Meva -- I have already killed all these people before you decided to start this war. Nimittamatram Bhava Savya Sachin -- so you just become the Nimitta Matra. If somebody gives you credit and says, why don't you become our group's leader and do this petition to such and such? It's not that the guy who is making a petition is the only guy who came up with the idea or we are just giving him a credit.

Look we can all go and talk. You become our leader. Arjuna, I'm just giving you this opportunity.

To become the Nimitt Matra because you deserve it. We always choose a person who has the best capabilities or the best qualification to become the representative of our group. We try to elect the best person who could be our president by looking at his qualifications.

So becoming a Nimitta Matra is also something to be very proud of. That somebody has given us a chance considering us to be worthy of it. So when Bhagavan said, you become Nimitta Matra for something, you should take great pride in it and get up and do it., in this case it is Arjuna.

But in our case also, we get this chance all the time. Bhagavan gives us the ability, capability, and opportunity to do something at our level in this world. And Bhagavan saying the same thing, look, I have already done this thing.

It will be done whether you take part in it or not. But you have this opportunity. Why don't you take this chance and become Nimitta Matra? Become the instrument in my hand and take the credit and enjoy the credit.

Bhagavan said to Arjuna, same thing. These people are killed. You just do your part.

You had been trained for these wars, stand up for the right cause. Take your credit and enjoy the fruits. Dronam Chabism Cha Jayadratham cha Karnam Tatha Anyanabi Yodavira *maya* Hatam Stumhi Jahimam Vyatista.

Nobody gives us this kind of guarantee before we start anything. "Rajan, go and do this. You are going to win it. Don't worry about it.

I already took care of it." Once in a while somebody does it for us too. Our father comes and says, "Beta, don't worry about it. I already talked to him.

They are going to hire you," right? So Bhagavan said, look, you are worried about a few of them. Whether you admit it or not, you think, how can I fight in front of these great warriors such as Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, and Karna? Bhagavan specifically mentions them and says I have already killed them.
snippets.reflection:
These verses contain one of the most famous declarations in the Gita: "Kalo'smi" - I am Time. When Arjuna asks who this terrible being is and what his intention is, Krishna reveals himself as "the Destroyer who lays waste the world." Then comes the practical instruction: "Gird up thy loins and conquer... I have already doomed them. Be thou my instrument (nimitta matra)." The warriors will die whether Arjuna fights or not; his participation does not determine the outcome but gives him the opportunity to fulfill his dharma.

The concept of "nimitta matra" - being merely an instrument - is revolutionary. We typically think our actions determine outcomes. But Krishna suggests that from the cosmic perspective, outcomes are already determined by the flow of time and karma. Our role is not to determine results but to participate fully and righteously in the unfolding. This is not fatalism but freedom from the anxiety of results. A surgeon operates with full skill; the outcome depends on many factors beyond her control. Her job is excellent action, not guaranteed results.

For today's practice, approach one significant task with the attitude of "nimitta matra." Do your absolute best while inwardly acknowledging that you are an instrument, not the ultimate doer. Notice how this shifts your relationship to anxiety and pressure. Ask yourself: In what areas of life am I exhausting myself trying to control what time will ultimately determine anyway? Where can I be a more willing instrument, doing excellent work while leaving results to the larger flow?
snippets.shortReflection: You're exhausting yourself trying to control outcomes that are already in motion. What if your job isn't to determine results but to show up fully and do your part? What anxiety would lift if you truly believed that?

Sanjaya continued: "Having heard these words from the Lord Shri Krishna, the Prince Arjuna, with folded hands trembling, prostrated himself and with choking voice, bowing down again and again, and overwhelmed with awe, once more addressed the Lord.
Arjuna said: My Lord! It is natural that the world revels and rejoices when it sings the praises of Thy glory; the demons fly in fear and the saints offer Thee their salutations.
snippets.commentary:
We have seen Arjuna's description of what he is seeing, and we have discussed so many times in the last few weeks. What he has seen is everything that he can perceive in this world, all coming together as one, this plurality which is separated from each other.

Now he sees that as one singularity. He also sees all the *divine* beings which he has just heard of in his Vedic training or from the cultural training. He sees all of them -- Brahma, Vishnu, Mahesh -- all of them merged into this one entity.

But he also sees that all these beings are rushing towards the mouth of that supreme being and getting dissolved, disappearing into it. And he comes to this realization that just as the river water is rushing towards the ocean -- intuitively, with inherent nature, not that somebody is propelling it or forcing it, but by its inherent nature. The river water runs from the mountaintops through the plains to the ocean.

Just as the moth instinctively rush towards its death into the flame, river rushes towards the ocean, loses its identity. Mighty river, like Ganges or Yamuna or even Patomak or James, once it disappears into the ocean, there is no identity of the river of its own. It just becomes part of the ocean.

It seems that is the true nature of the river and the moth. So he sees that all the beings are without any hesitation, they're rushing towards the mouth of this great being and disappearing into it. And then he sees that this great being is seemingly enjoying this act of all these beings disappearing into his mouth, some get stuck.

He makes sure that nobody is left out when we do some task. And we are so happy about it, that we are so proud of that. In the end we try to inspect and say, is there anything left? That's basically equivalent to licking up what's going into his mouth -- making sure that all these beings are getting dissolved into his own being.

And now Arjuna says, I don't understand any of this. Akyahi me ko bhavan ugrarupaha -- tell me, O being with a very fierce form. Namostu te deva or prasida -- if you want to ask somebody who you are and that person is not smaller than you, you better be a little respectful first.

He does ask and say, I want to know who you are. But first, Namostute devara prasida -- you are the supreme Lord, so I bow down to you, have mercy on me, because I don't understand. I am not capable of understanding who you are.

And vignatum ichami bhavantam adyam -- I have completely and clearly recognized that you are the Adi being. You are the original being. All beings are nothing but the manifestation of you.

They come from you, they go into you. But you are that original Bhavantam adyam. You are that original being.

Vignatum ichami -- I want to know, which in normal terms we say, I want to know God. I know he is the supreme being. At least from my childhood religious training I understood that he controlled this world.

Vigna tam ichami bhavanta madhyam -- even after having this global vision, the cosmic vision, our intellect is not capable of understanding it. Nahi prajanami tavapravratyam -- also, I have no idea why you are doing this activity which I see right now. Isn't that something we ask all the time? I don't know why Bhagawan does this thing, why there is a tsunami, why there is an earthquake, or why Bill Gates and Steve Jobs are successful and not every IT person in this country.

I do not know what you are doing, Bhagwan. I hope you know what you are doing. Basically Arjuna puts it in his word very respectfully saying I want to know you O supreme Being.

I clearly recognize you are the original being, but I also don't understand what you are engaged in right now. I see all these beings going into your mouth and getting crushed. He has also seen -- we have seen -- that all Kauravas are going into his mouth, as well as all the great kings on both sides.

See, anytime we have a vision, we focus on something closer to our own situation. Anytime you have a dream, the dream is always something related to what you were thinking about in the last week or so. So even when he sees this whole cosmic vision, he focuses on the Kauravas going into his mouth.

All the kings from the Kauravas as well as the kings from our side, going into his mouth. He says, I don't understand what you are engaged in right now. And in response to that, Bhagavan says, Kalo'smi -- I am time.

Lokaksha Kruta Pravrad daha -- I am engaged in destroying this world. I can see the world from both perspectives. Either I can see it from a constructive perspective or a destructive perspective in nature.

Actually both simultaneously keeps going on. Something gets destroyed, something gets built. I can fix my perspective only on the destruction part and say why this thing is happening.

I can look at the statistics in the newspaper and say how many people die every day and say oh God, billions of people die. I don't know whether millions or billions, but I'm sure there are plenty because every several seconds there's somebody dies in the United States. I read somewhere about how many people die every day, and if I look at that and say God, why do you do this? This many people dying every day.

Don't you have better things to do than just killing? Right now Arjuna is just seeing this destruction going on. So Bhagavan's answer is also exactly that. Kalaha Asmi, I am all devouring time.

I was born in 1948. In 2012, I'm an old man, but sometime in the 2000-somethings I won't be around. That's what Lokakshaya krita pravadha means.

You're seeing me destroying this world. As you know, the world as I know right now, is actually rushing towards its own destruction. All my friends and relatives and all of them, one after the other, they're all rushing towards their own death.

Kalavasmi lokaksha Kruta Prabhradha. From your perspective, Arjuna, I am that all devouring time. Right now what you are seeing is I am engaged in destroying these worlds.

Lokan sama hartum iha pravrutaha ruteapi tvamna Bhavishyanti swarve e avasthitaha pratyanikeshi odaha. Even without you -- now coming down very personally to Arjuna -- Arjuna had said, I don't want to engage in this war. The whole purpose of this *divine* vision Arjuna wanted to have was connected to all the philosophy Bhagavan gave him in the second chapter about why he should engage in this war.

Bhagavan had said, look, whoever takes birth will die. Beginning they unmanifest, they will manifest for a while, they will unmanifest in the end. So you don't worry about it.

Whatever the little role you are given in this drama, you take part and take credit for it and you don't worry about who's going to die and who's going to survive. But Arjuna was not clear. So he said, well let me see this entire vision now.

He sees the entire vision and then he says I don't understand what are you doing? And Bhagawan basically said, don't worry about it, I am time. I'm going to destroy everything in time. Whether you take part in it or not.

Even without you, none of the warriors in front of you shall live. Whether you take part in this war or not is immaterial. Their destiny is to die in time.

Whenever their time will come, they will die. Because I am that all devouring time. Tasmat Utestha Yashola Basva -- all you have to do is take credit for it.

Everybody says Bill Clinton was the best president in his time. We all thrived and our country has this surplus we never had seen in all these times before. And George Bush came and completely messed it all up.

But I'll tell you what, if George Bush was the president at the time when the technology bubble was blowing up, he would have the same credit. He just happened to be at that time a president. And we can blame Obama all we want.

About 8% or 9% unemployment. But even if Bill Clinton is today, he would have the same problem. Because this thing is driven by this cycle, cosmic cycle, economic cycles, whatever the cycle you want to call it, you just happen to be there.

And if you're a smart person, you do your part and take credit. Become that instrument in this giant will of *dharma*. So therefore Bhagavan said, look, all these people are already killed by me.

Without your help also they will get killed. You just saw that every being is rushing towards their death in my mouth. Get up Yashola Basra and get the fame that you deserve.

Jitva Satrun Bhangshvarajam Samruddham -- get victory over your enemies and enjoy the kingdom. *maya* Evey Thai Nihitaha Purva Meva -- I have already killed all these people before you decided to start this war. Nimittamatram Bhava Savya Sachin -- so you just become the Nimitta Matra. If somebody gives you credit and says, why don't you become our group's leader and do this petition to such and such? It's not that the guy who is making a petition is the only guy who came up with the idea or we are just giving him a credit.

Look we can all go and talk. You become our leader. Arjuna, I'm just giving you this opportunity.

To become the Nimitt Matra because you deserve it. We always choose a person who has the best capabilities or the best qualification to become the representative of our group. We try to elect the best person who could be our president by looking at his qualifications.

So becoming a Nimitta Matra is also something to be very proud of. That somebody has given us a chance considering us to be worthy of it. So when Bhagavan said, you become Nimitta Matra for something, you should take great pride in it and get up and do it., in this case it is Arjuna.

But in our case also, we get this chance all the time. Bhagavan gives us the ability, capability, and opportunity to do something at our level in this world. And Bhagavan saying the same thing, look, I have already done this thing.

It will be done whether you take part in it or not. But you have this opportunity. Why don't you take this chance and become Nimitta Matra? Become the instrument in my hand and take the credit and enjoy the credit.

Bhagavan said to Arjuna, same thing. These people are killed. You just do your part.

You had been trained for these wars, stand up for the right cause. Take your credit and enjoy the fruits. Dronam Chabism Cha Jayadratham cha Karnam Tatha Anyanabi Yodavira *maya* Hatam Stumhi Jahimam Vyatista.

Nobody gives us this kind of guarantee before we start anything. "Rajan, go and do this. You are going to win it. Don't worry about it.

I already took care of it." Once in a while somebody does it for us too. Our father comes and says, "Beta, don't worry about it. I already talked to him.

They are going to hire you," right? So Bhagavan said, look, you are worried about a few of them. Whether you admit it or not, you think, how can I fight in front of these great warriors such as Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, and Karna? Bhagavan specifically mentions them and says I have already killed them.
snippets.reflection:
Having heard Krishna declare "I am Time" and "I have already killed them," Arjuna responds with trembling, prostration, and choked voice. Sanjaya notes he was "overwhelmed with awe, bowing down again and again." Then Arjuna speaks: "It is natural that the world revels and rejoices when it sings the praises of Thy glory; the demons fly in fear and the saints offer Thee their salutations." He is processing the vision intellectually while still emotionally shaken.

Notice the different responses to the divine revelation: demons flee in fear, saints offer salutations, and the world rejoices in singing praises. How we respond to truth depends on our nature and readiness. The same reality that terrifies the unprepared becomes a source of devotion for the mature seeker. Arjuna stands at the threshold - shaken but not fleeing, overwhelmed but still present and engaged. This is the response of a genuine seeker: neither running away nor pretending everything is fine.

Reflect today on how you respond to difficult truths. When you encounter the reality of impermanence, do you flee into distraction? When you see the suffering in the world, do you turn away or remain present? The spiritual path is not about achieving a state where nothing disturbs you but about developing the capacity to remain present with whatever arises. Practice today by staying with one uncomfortable truth for just a few minutes longer than you normally would. Notice the impulse to flee and gently remain. This builds the capacity that allows transformation.
snippets.shortReflection: When you encounter a hard truth about yourself or the world, do you flee into distraction, or can you stay present with it? Spiritual growth isn't about never being disturbed - it's about developing the capacity to remain when everything in you wants to run.

snippets.sanskrit:

verseTranslations: How should they do otherwise? O Thou Supremest Self, greater than the Powers of creation, the First Cause, Infinite, the Lord of Lords, the Home of the universe, Imperishable, Being and Not-Being, yet transcending both.
Thou art the Primal God, the Ancient, the Supreme Abode of this universe, the Knower, the Knowledge and the Final Home. Thou fillest everything. Thy form is infinite.

Thou art the Wind, Thou art Death, Thou art the Fire, the Water, the Moon, the Father and the Grandfather. Honour and glory to Thee a thousand and a thousand times! Again and again, salutation be to Thee, O my Lord!
snippets.commentary:
What is the nature of this conditioned self? He learned that the self is immortal. The conditionings are perishable. The conditionings -- this body, this mind, this intellect -- are perishable.

But the *self* is imperishable. And therefore, while working in this world, keep that self in mind, identify with that self. But that is not very naturally happening to people. So Bhagavan talked about how to act in this world, addressed Arjuna, that you should act in this world in the spirit of Yajna. You will be then gradually detach yourself from this *ego* and will be able to identify with yourself. So then obviously Arjuna wanted to know the nature of that imperishable self.

So from chapter seven, Bhagavan said, I am the source of all the beings and things. Aham krutnasya jagadah prabhavaha pralayah t -- I am the source and dissolution of all things and beings in this world. So that's my relationship to you: I am the source of all the beings, and therefore also the source of you. And then he says, matthaha parataram na asti kincit anyat asti dhananjaya -- there is nothing higher than me.

There is nothing higher than this *self*. Therefore you should identify with the self. But Arjuna obviously was not ready to take this on its face value. The Bhagavan said, I am the source of all the beings and all the things. He wanted to know more. So he said, I want to know in detail your glories.

Because he is still identifying with Krishna as Krishna, and himself as Arjuna. How can Krishna be the Lord of all the beings? Arjuna, identifying with his limited self, is speaking from his ego's perspective and projecting his world. Krishna is speaking from his identification with the Supreme. He said, I am the source of all the beings. So Arjuna said, explain to me in detail, because I actually love hearing about your great glories, all the powers of this omnipresent, omniscient being.

So in chapter 10 we have a detailed description of Bhagavan saying that you can see my glory in everything that is splendid, wonderful, strong -- anything where you can find something which catches your eye.

That's me at the core of all beings. I am the sweetness in sugar, I am the light in sun, I am the liquidity in water. And even he says Dyutam, Chalaya, Tamasmi, even I am the gambling and the fraudulence. Even that also somebody can only cheat you if he is alive and conscious and consciousness is working through him. Everything that you see in this world, the core of all beings and things, is me and me alone. Nothing other than me exists.

Arjuna heard all that, but he's still not satisfied. He's still not grasping the whole idea of the omniscience and omnipotence of the Lord -- how the Lord can be everywhere. So he says, I want to see it. I have no doubt; you said this and also many others have said so before you. So I have no doubt about it. I take it for granted that what you are saying is correct.

Because time and again, sages after sages from generations have come and confirmed that this is the truth. So I am not doubting it now. You, Krishna, telling me so, I have no doubt -- but I want to see it. And therefore in chapter 11 we see that Krishna grants him this great vision of totality, where Arjuna can see all at once -- the past, present and future, an entire universe in one glimpse. And what he sees is that up till now the things which he has been seeing as different entities are all merged into one.

They're all part of the one entity. Therefore he describes and says, I'm seeing that you have thousands of mouths and thousands of hands and thousands of legs and thousands of stomachs. Because every stomach is yours, every hand is yours, every mouth is yours. So I see now all of them as part of the one entity. I'm seeing wonderful sights -- all these forms and colors and all the deities, things which I have not seen before, I have not even imagined before. I'm seeing all of them.

So he's enchanted by that form. But then he sees the other side of it. Other side of creation is always destruction. This is the other side of it. He sees that now all those beings which I see existing in him also rushing towards his mouth to get destroyed. Every name and form in this world is helplessly rushing toward its own destruction within the self which is supporting it.

So he starts getting really nervous about it that everyone is rushing towards your mouth to get destroyed. And I see the great people, the great heroes are helplessly rushing towards your mouth and getting destroyed. And that vision really terrified him. We had this notion about Bhagavan as one who is compassionate, serene, and creative. But the destructive aspect -- we never focus on that. Arjuna, while listening to all the discourses before, all the glories, all the splendid descriptions given --

I am the light in the sun. I am the fragrance in flower. So he was expecting it will be all well and good. Once I see the totality, it will be wonderful. My mind will be at peace. And after that there will be no problem.

But he sees the other side of it. He says everything is getting destroyed. Every name and form is getting destroyed in the being of that great Mahatma, the great person, the Purusha, the one entity. So he says, I'm terrified. I can't find my place in life. I don't know where I am and I'm losing my bearing.

So tell me, who are you and what are you up to? Because I have never imagined your form like this. See, only in our culture, in our religion, we have terrible forms of God also -- Kali and Shiva doing Tandava and Rudra and Pralaya. But in most cases we want to see him as a very calm, serene, and peaceful God. But when you want to understand God in totality, Bhagavan says, you have to know this also.

So he sees this destruction happening. Bhagavan says, I am the world-devouring time. Kalo'smi -- I am that time which devours everything. Within time, all names and forms will be destroyed. Everything dissolves into time. Things exist in time, get destroyed by time.

I am that all-devouring time. What you are seeing right now is my form which devours all names and forms. What are you up to right now? I'm engaged in destroying the world as you know it. The world as you and I know it is already getting destroyed by Bhagavan. Every second, every millisecond, it's constantly getting destroyed.

My reality yesterday is no longer my reality today. My reality today will no longer be my reality tomorrow. So it's constant, constantly destroying my world. And I am on the other end, constantly trying to keep my world in a status quo. I want to keep it exactly as I like. I think I'm right now in a better situation.

Let's keep it that way. So we have a tug of war between Bhagavan and me. I try to keep it; he wants to destroy it. So when I see his all-destroying power, I ask, why are you doing this? He says, my purpose is clear: I am the time who devours everything.

And right now you are seeing me destroying the world. As you know, and directly addressing. Arjuna said you were afraid that you will kill all these people. You thought that you are so powerful that you will kill all these people. Therefore you were afraid of taking part in this war. He said, I have already killed them all.

From our perspective, we are all alive and trying to survive. But Bhagavan says, there's time. I have already killed all of you -- for whatever time it is, you are going to be killed by time. No matter how many cryogenic clinics open in Richmond -- there is one opened, I guess, recently.

The time may be in years, maybe in millennia. But you will be destroyed by time. I've already destroyed you as the name and form you exist. I already killed you. Whether you take part in this game or not. You think that you don't want to take part in destroying these people?

These people are already destroyed, because as we learned, what will get destroyed is the conditioning. Only the self is immaculate, permanent, without any limitations. So these people are already destroyed as they exist -- whether they are Karna, Bhishma, or Jayadratha. Even though they seem invincible from your perspective, and they have powers so much greater than yours.

But they are killed by me. So my advice to you, Arjuna, is take charge of your life. Do what you were trained to do. Do what you thought was the purpose of your life. To establish the rule of justice and punish the people who are evil doers. I have already killed them.

You take the credit and then enjoy this kingdom. And that's where Bhagavan stopped. Then Sanjaya now takes a chance to tell Dhritarashtra what's happening. Sanjaya Vacha -- etatshrutva vachanam Kesavasya Krutanjalir vaipamanaha Kiriti namaskritva Bhuya evaha Krishnam Sagadgadam Bhitebhitaha Pranamya. He's giving a running commentary. He says, having heard these words from Krishna --

That I already killed all of them. I am the one who devours everything. I am the one who kills. You just take the credit and enjoy the victory. Only you can take credit or enjoy victory if you take part in it. If I don't take part, there is no chance.

There is 100% chance of me losing if I don't buy a lottery ticket. Guaranteed 100% chance of not winning the lottery. That's at least the surest outcome I can say. But if I think I have a chance to win 1 in 10 million, I have to buy a lottery ticket. I have to take part in it. So Bhagavan said, I already decided who the winner is.

You go ahead and buy a lottery ticket if you think you can. But if you don't take part, you will have no chance to win this thing. So Arjuna, therefore get up and do your duty. Result is decided by me. But you have a duty to perform your actions, for which you are trained, which you thought is the purpose of your life. And you must pursue that.

Having heard this, Sanjaya said that this Kiriti, the crowned one, Krutanjali Vepamanha -- his folded palms trembling, because he is still shaken up by this vision of all death and destruction happening constantly in this great self. The self remaining what it is, the names and forms are created in it and getting destroyed all the time. Namaskritva -- having prostrated to him -- Bhuya Eva Aha Krishnam -- he said the following words. He is choked with emotions, choked with the realization of what the self is all about. Up till now, I was in control of my life.

I thought I can control it. I have accomplished things. I have acquired abilities and promises. I suddenly realized that those things are of no value unless there is a support from the Almighty. The consciousness functioning through me. I may be the best architect, but if I'm in a coma, it doesn't do any good to anybody.
snippets.reflection:
Arjuna now offers a prayer of deep recognition: Krishna is "greater than the Powers of creation, the First Cause, Infinite, the Lord of Lords." He declares Krishna to be "the Primal God, the Ancient, the Knower, the Knowledge and the Final Home... the Wind, Death, Fire, Water, the Moon, the Father and the Grandfather." This comprehensive list shows Arjuna seeing Krishna not as one god among many but as the source and essence of all divine principles and natural forces.

The teaching here is about the relationship between the many and the One. We worship different aspects of divinity - some pray to a nurturing mother aspect, others to a powerful protector, still others to wisdom or prosperity. Arjuna's vision reveals that all these are expressions of one reality. Wind, Death, Fire, Water - seemingly separate forces - are all manifestations of the same supreme consciousness. This does not diminish the deities but reveals their ultimate unity.

For today's practice, notice the divine in multiple forms throughout your day. See consciousness in the sustaining power of your breath (Vayu), in the natural limits and endings you encounter (Yama), in the transformative fire of your digestion and passion (Agni), in the flowing adaptability of water. Instead of thinking "this is different from that," practice seeing each as a face of the same underlying reality. When you say "namaste" to someone, recognize you are bowing to the same consciousness that looks out through your own eyes. This practice of seeing unity in diversity is the practical application of Arjuna's vision.
snippets.shortReflection: You divide the world into categories: work vs. spirituality, ordinary vs. sacred, mundane vs. divine. But what if the breath moving through you right now, the water you drink, the fire of your passion - what if these are all faces of the same thing looking back at you?

You and your friend are really mad at each other. And the other friend, you know, Rajan, I'm so sorry I did that. That's the end of the story.

Let's go see a movie together. It's a very different relationship. And then when you're in love, when somebody is beloved to you, no matter what differences you have.

And you're mad at each other, as soon as one person says, "I'm sorry," that's the end of the story.
snippets.reflection:
Having recognized Krishna's true nature, Arjuna becomes acutely aware of how he has treated Krishna casually in the past. He recalls addressing him familiarly as "Krishna," "Yadava," "Friend" - calling him by first name, joking with him, perhaps even insulting him in jest during meals or leisure. "Whatever insult I have offered to Thee in sport or in repose... alone or in a multitude, I ask Thy forgiveness." This is the natural response when we suddenly realize the divine was present all along in what we treated as ordinary.

This teaching applies directly to our relationships. The same consciousness that Arjuna saw in Krishna's cosmic form is present in every person we encounter. How do we treat the divine when it appears as our spouse, our child, our colleague, the stranger at the store? The casual disrespect, the thoughtless words, the failure to truly see the other - Arjuna recognizes these as offenses against the divine itself.

Today, bring awareness to how you treat the people closest to you - precisely because familiarity often breeds carelessness. Notice when you dismiss, interrupt, or fail to fully see someone you interact with regularly. Arjuna's recognition that Krishna was "O Thou Who art without an equal" applies to the unique, irreplaceable consciousness in each person. Practice pausing before responding to a family member or close friend, and silently acknowledge: "The divine is present here." Notice how this small recognition changes the quality of your interactions.
snippets.shortReflection: You're most careless with the people closest to you - dismissing your partner, half-listening to your kids, interrupting your friends. The divine is showing up in your kitchen, in your car, in every conversation, and you keep treating it casually. When will you truly see who's in front of you?

And you're mad at each other, as soon as one person says, "I'm sorry," that's the end of the story.

Arjuna appeals to three relationships where forgiveness comes naturally: "as father to son, as friend to friend, as lover to his beloved." Then he makes his request: "I rejoice that I have seen what never man saw before; yet I am overwhelmed with fear. Please take again the Form I know." He asks to see Krishna with "the crown, the sceptre and the discus" - the familiar four-armed Vishnu form he grew up venerating. The cosmic vision, while revelatory, is more than he can bear.

This reveals something important about spiritual growth: we can only integrate as much truth as we are prepared to hold. Arjuna's request is not weakness but wisdom - he knows his limits. The cosmic vision showed him ultimate reality, but he needs to return to a form he can relate to, worship, and live with. Similarly, moments of profound spiritual insight often need to be followed by integration into ordinary life.

Reflect today on your own capacity to hold truth. Have you had experiences or insights that were overwhelming? How did you integrate them? Notice the balance between reaching for expanded awareness and respecting your current capacity. What "gentle form" of the divine can you relate to in daily life? What practice or image or relationship helps you connect with the sacred in a sustainable way? Honor both the aspiration for ultimate truth and the need for forms that support your current stage of development.

The normal perception we have is I and the world exists. And therefore there is a duality.

There is a constant struggle between I and the world, where I define myself as me and the world as everything else. And then this world we divide into two: the world which I like and the world which I don't like. So our whole life pursuit is to align with the world which I like and avoid the world which I don't like. Vedanta says, all of life, the pursuit is to avoid what is unpleasant and to gain what is pleasant. And this pursuit creates the friction, and that creates more unhappiness, more dissatisfaction, because almost everyone around me is trying to do the same thing. And then we are in competition to get out of that race. If I can get that vision of oneness, then I can have that everlasting peace that I am seeking.

So Bhagavan showed this roop to Arjuna. And Arjuna sees this world without any space and time. The dividing factor between I and the world is the space and time. And once that is taken off, I see this world as one entity ever strung into each other by a common thread. But this is an overwhelming picture for Arjuna. So he said, I'm delighted to see this, but at the same time I am completely overwhelmed and I'm fearful.

So oh Lord, show me your form which is much gentler and which I am most comfortable with, which is that of Vishnu. We want to see Bhagavan in a form which is most comfortable to us, as we have discussed last time. So he says, show me with your form with the Kiritinam Gadinam, Chakrinam Hastam, with the crown and mace and Chakra which I'm so familiar with. Right from my childhood I've seen Vishnu's pictures and anytime somebody says, have you seen cosmic form? All of us say, oh yes, yeah, I've seen Bhagavad Gita pictures and you know, Shiva. Sure, because we have seen all the paintings of Shiva.

So we had a familiarity. We have formed an image of God in our head, and any image other than that -- the whole understanding that this Almighty is nothing but the source of all these beings and is all these beings -- is not really a comforting thought. Therefore, very conveniently, we divide the world into good and bad. Everything good happening is *divine*; bad happening is evil. Tsunami is evil, earthquake is evil. But in reality, it's all part of the whole phenomenon called this world. There's nothing evil or good about it.

Arjuna asked for that, and then Bhagavan said in his response -- *maya* prasannena tava Arjuna, Idam Rupam Param Darsitam, Atma Yogat -- the last verse which we have seen. He said, I showed you the supreme form of mine graciously, because you are my devoted student, a friend, and a devotee. With my *yoga*, with my power of changing your perception, I have showed you my form. Not that this form was never available. It is always available to those who can see it. Radio waves are always here for those who can tune into them -- the fact that we're not tuning into them doesn't mean they're not there. The form was always there. Arjuna did not have the capacity to see it. But my yoga gave you that perception which was Tejomayam Vishwam, Anantam, Adyam, Yanme tvad anyena Drishta Purvam -- the splendid and all-encompassing Vishwam, all-pervading infinite form which you have seen and not seen by any other before. The point is that no one in this state of mind, state of evolution, state of understanding has seen this thing. If I say, "Well, I actually saw it while driving down to work yesterday" -- well, that's not true, not going to happen. Because then I won't be able to drive, because I lose that whole perception of the road, my car, and me as separate. I can't have these two together -- the perception of me and this world as separate, and the perception of me and the world as one and the same -- both at the same time.

Because others are trying to see this by the means which they find most convenient and appropriate. We are also trying to find that source of happiness which has *infinite* power to make us happy. So we try our own way.

We say we will have the best education. We want our children to be the happiest in this world. What are we going to do? Does it make them happy? In fact, half the time what we have done to make them happy makes them most unhappy. But that's the only means which we know to transfer happiness to someone else.

When I was a teenager and I see people talking about Bhagavad Gita and I used to say, I understand nothing, but someday I really want to know what they're talking about.

So we want to get the knowledge which we think the others have. So we learn Veda, Yajna, all the things which we think is good. Somewhat in a putting-it-down tone, I said this -- that's not the intention. Those are the means to prepare your mind and intellect to a level where he will shine through. We have discussed that a seeker's job is only to do the Antahkarana Shuddhi.

As per our Vedanta, our job is simply to make our Antahkarana -- the internal instrument, which is mind and intellect -- to clean it up, make it ready for his reflection into it. Our job with this mind and its impurities is simply to clean up the impurities. All this we have discussed is actually just for the Antahkarana Shuddhi.

Veda, Dhyana, Yajna, Tapa, Dana, Kriya -- all that is for Antahkarana Shuddhi. If you are doing it for Antahkarana Shuddhi, it will gain its results. This is all I have to do, and I'm done with it. And therefore he says, you are not getting it through these alone. So Bhagavan says, evam rupah sakya aham nrloke --

this form of mine is not possible to be seen in this world of man. Drastum tvad anyena kuru pravira -- Arjuna is Kuru Pravira, the best among the Kurus. It is not possible in this world for anyone other than you to see this by these means alone, because these are the means and not the end -- which we normally confuse as the end. The next verse we just saw is Ma te vyatha. This is a verse which shows what state Arjuna was in. Ma te vyatha cha vimudhabhavah --

Don't be disturbed and don't be fearful. I can see clearly on your face that you are disturbed, overwhelmed, and fearful by looking at this terrible form of mine. Drishtva rupam ghoram idrik mama idam -- having seen such a terrible form of mine. See, again, somewhere in the translation it says "terrific form." But it says Ghoram, which means terrible. Whether it is terrible or terrific -- who decides that?

From our point of view something may be terrible. From some other perspective it is terrific when somebody is taking those pictures of tsunamis from a distance from some satellite and then we are seeing those such a terrific form of tsunami. But guy at that whatever the beach where the tsunami is coming in Japan or wherever that is, it's a terrible form of tsunami. So he says, having seen this terrible form of mine -- because you are seeing it as a jiva, as a limited being, trying to comprehend this overwhelming nature of the self -- it's a terrible form. Vyapetabhih pritamanah -- with your fear dispelled, get your fear out, and pritamanah, have a loving nature again. Punastvam tadeva me rupam idam prapashya.

And now see this form which will remove your fear -- a loving form. Now comes a little bit of a controversy. When Bhagavan came back from his Virat Swarupa, what form did he show? Arjuna had asked for Kiritinam Gadinam Chakrinam Hastam -- you know, Vishnu Roop. But Bhagavad Gita really doesn't say that. Some commentaries have said Bhagavad Gita simply says he came back to his original gentle form as Vasudev Krishna.
snippets.reflection:
Krishna grants Arjuna's request to see a gentler form, then makes a remarkable statement: "Never has it been seen by any but thee... Not by study of the scriptures, not by sacrifice or gift, not by ritual or rigorous austerity, is it possible for man on earth to see what thou hast seen." This seems to negate all spiritual practice - if study, sacrifice, charity, and austerity cannot grant this vision, what can? The answer lies in what these practices prepare us for rather than what they directly achieve.

The teaching here parallels success in any field. Going to architecture school does not guarantee becoming a successful architect - many graduates never practice. The training is necessary but not sufficient. What is also required is devotion and the grace of opportunities. Similarly, spiritual practices purify the mind and prepare us, but the actual vision comes through grace - it cannot be demanded or earned.

For today's practice, examine your relationship to spiritual effort. Are you treating practices as transactions - "I did this much meditation, so I deserve that much peace"? Or are you doing practices for their own sake, to purify and prepare, while remaining open to grace? The vision comes through grace, in its own time, to those who have prepared and remained humble. Today, do your practices with full effort and zero expectation. Offer the effort itself as worship, and release all claims to results.
snippets.shortReflection: You treat your spiritual practice like a transaction: 'I meditated for 20 minutes, so I deserve some peace.' But what if practice doesn't earn anything? What if it only prepares you to receive what can't be demanded - only given?

Krishna speaks with gentleness: "Be not afraid or bewildered by the terrible vision. Put away thy fear and, with joyful mind, see Me once again in My usual Form." Then Arjuna, seeing Krishna's human form again, says: "Seeing Thee in Thy gentle human form, my Lord, I am myself again, calm once more." He has returned to normal perception after the overwhelming cosmic experience.

This return to normalcy is essential. The vision showed Arjuna ultimate reality, but he must live in the relative world, fight the battle, and fulfill his dharma. Spiritual experiences, however profound, must be integrated into daily life. Someone who remains permanently in cosmic consciousness cannot function in the world. The path involves expansion followed by integration, insight followed by application.

Reflect today on how you integrate spiritual insights into ordinary life. Have you had experiences of expanded awareness that you then had to bring back to mundane reality? How did that transition feel? The teaching suggests this is natural and necessary. The goal is not to escape ordinary life permanently but to transform how we engage with it. After touching the cosmic vision, Arjuna will fight the same battle, but with transformed understanding. What insights from your spiritual practice can you bring more fully into your daily activities, relationships, and challenges?
snippets.shortReflection: Peak experiences are powerful, but you can't live on the mountaintop. The real work is bringing what you've seen back down into traffic jams, difficult conversations, and boring Tuesday afternoons. How do you carry your insights into ordinary life?

snippets.title: Day 159: Only Through Devotion
snippets.sanskrit:
श्री भगवानुवाच |
सुदुर्दर्शमिदं रूपं दृष्टवानसि यन्मम |
देवा अप्यस्य रूपस्य नित्यं दर्शनकाङ्क्षिणः ||

नाहं वेदैर्न तपसा न दानेन न चेज्यया |
शक्य एवंविधो द्रष्टुं दृष्टवानसि मां यथा ||

भक्त्या त्वनन्यया शक्यमहमेवंविधोऽर्जुन |
ज्ञातुं दृष्टुं च तत्त्वेन प्रवेष्टुं च परंतप ||
snippets.transliteration:
śhrī-bhagavān uvācha
su-durdarśham idaṁ rūpaṁ dṛiṣhṭavān asi yan mama
devā apy asya rūpasya nityaṁ darśhana-kāṅkṣhiṇaḥ

nāhaṁ vedair na tapasā na dānena na chejyayā
śhakya evaṁ-vidho draṣhṭuṁ dṛiṣhṭavān asi māṁ yathā

bhaktyā tv ananyayā śhakya aham evaṁ-vidho ’rjuna
jñātuṁ draṣhṭuṁ cha tattvena praveṣhṭuṁ cha parantapa
verseTranslations: Lord Shri Krishna replied: It is hard to see this vision of Me that thou hast seen. Even the most powerful have longed for it in vain.
Not by study of the scriptures, or by austerities, not by gifts or sacrifices, is it possible to see Me as thou hast done.
Only by tireless devotion can I be seen and known; only thus can a man become one with Me, O Arjuna!
snippets.commentary:
We have seen in this chapter that Bhagavan showed his cosmic form. So what does that mean? The cosmic form is that form which includes all the forms in this cosmos, in this world, in this Jagat. All the forms at one place, from past, present, and future.

So that negates time. If there is no past, present and future, there is no time. If there is only one entity, one supreme being, then there is no time. I don't require any time to meet myself. I am always there, so there is no time required. It is when I have to meet somebody else, then I have to have time.

The two, it requires time and we can say we'll meet at 10 o' clock every Sunday morning. So as long as there are more than one, there will be time. If there's only one, there is no time. So in this cosmic form, everything is crunched into one. Past, present, future. There is no time also.

If there is one, there is no space. If there is one dot, the dot doesn't require any space. Instead of two dots, there is a distance between the two and there's space between the two. The space is created only when there are two. So in this, all forms are in one. Therefore there is no space also.

Because all forms are within that one form, that one form now becomes the form, the cosmic form. And therefore there is no space. So the space and time are both negated. In cosmic form, to have any form, what you require is space and time. Without space and time, there is no form. So the actual vision that Arjuna had was that of a formless space, supreme being.

But then he describes all these beings in it: I see Brahma, I see Vishnu, I see all the Siddhas, I see all Rakshasas, I see Dhritarashtra's sons. So in the supreme, all the probabilities -- *infinite* probabilities, the infinite amount of forms you can imagine -- you can create in that infinite.

It is something like if one of my clients comes to me and says, "Rajan, here is a piece of land. Design a building." I say, "But what kind of a building? What do you want to use it for?" If you leave everything up to me, I have *infinite* possibilities -- what I can design, what type of building I can design.

There I can say, it can be a hospital, it can be a jail. It can be an office building, a multi-storied office building. Maybe it's a single-story office building. No, no, it can be residential. Well, maybe multi-story. *infinite* possibilities.

To really design a building, I have to eliminate all other possibilities and narrow it down to one. It can't be a hospital because it's not possible here, not needed here. It cannot be a jail because we have no authority to imprison anybody. I have to come down to negate everything until only one choice remains, and that becomes my choice. So for any form, it's necessary that you negate all other forms.

So when I say, let's say Prakashji comes to the room and I see Prakashji -- what I have to do is negate all 7 billion people on this planet. All remaining 7 billion people are not that; that's Prakashji. So to create a form from a probability of *infinite* probabilities in the supreme, I have to negate all other probabilities. Here, Arjuna can see whatever he wants to see. So is the case with us, because we see from a narrow perspective, we negate things, and it comes down to a particular form. So here Bhagavan showed Arjuna the supreme form which is formless but has infinite probabilities and possibilities of forms.

So that was the reason. And therefore Arjuna could see things which are delightful and those which are frightful. When it comes to the delightful, when we think about God as divine, it is very pleasant. But when we think about God who is also responsible for -- or also enabling -- the evil in this world, that is very frightful. Therefore we say, Bhagavan, I don't want to see that part of yours. Show me something which I can live with.

So that's what we have seen so far. Arjuna requested, put me back where I was before. So Bhagavan showed him the same Swarupa as Vasudeva, as Vasudeva's son which he was before as his charioteer. And then Bhagavan told him, look, this form of mine which you have seen -- which has all the forms included from past, present, and future -- is very difficult to see. It is auspicious but very difficult to see. And therefore nobody has seen it before.

You have seen it simply because of my grace -- Atma Yogat. By my yoga I could make you see this. But it is not possible to see through all the other preparations. Learning Veda, Dhyana, Yajna -- these are means but not the goal. You cannot achieve the goal by just preparing for it. Na aham vedena tapasa na danena ijyaya shakya evam vidho drastum -- as you have seen me, it is not possible through study of Vedas or austerities or charities or even sacrifices.

It almost looks like Bhagavan is discouraging us -- none of this is going to be helpful. But Bhagavan is actually making a statement of fact. We can learn from this verse the secret of success in anything. Can I become a successful architect just by going to architecture school? Many of my classmates are in the United States.

They all went to the same school. We all got the architecture degree. None of them are practicing architecture. They're successful in what they are doing. They own motels, they own gas stations and big houses and many cars. But they're not practicing architecture.

So just by going to architecture school, I cannot become a successful architect. So is the case with doctors, engineers. What makes a person a successful professional? The first thing is his devotion to the profession. He has to be devoted to his profession. When I came to this country -- big recession time, 1982, huge recession -- I was in Houston.

Pipe drafting was a big thing there because of all the oil companies. And people said, forget about architecture, do pipe drafting, you will make a lot of money. And I said, there's one thing I will not do, and that is leave architecture. I'll find jobs somewhere. Even drafting in architecture is acceptable, but not pipe drafting. So unless you are devoted to a profession -- that's the first requirement -- but even that doesn't make me successful as a designer of buildings, because I need the grace of my clients.

I may be the best architect on this planet, but if there is no client that I can convince to let me design his or her building, then I won't be able to design. So to become a successful architect who can design a building and construct it, I need the grace of my clients. The ultimate thing I need is grace from the one from whom I am seeking that work, that achievement. But to get there, I have to do a lot more. I can't really just come out and say, "I'm devoted to architecture, give me work."

That's also not possible. You have to train yourself continuously. So that you become proficient and efficient. Then somebody will see that you are capable of doing so. So Bhagavan said, two things I require. One is your devotion to your goal.

And then grace from whoever is the fruit giver. Whoever is responsible to give you that work or that achievement. So Bhagavan says, Na aham vedair tapasa na danena ijyaya shakya evam vidho drastum drishtavanasi mam yatha -- you have seen me, but I am not possible to be seen through all these things alone. We think that preparing ourselves is good enough. But when it is not good enough, what you require is: Bhaktya tu ananyaya shakya aham evam vidho Arjuna jnatum drastum cha tattvena praveshtum cha parantapa.

It is not possible by just preparation. If you are devoted to me -- Bhaktya tu Ananyaya -- by single-minded devotion, it is possible. Bhagavan has given you the secret. What you really require is single-pointed devotion. And devotion, as we have discussed many times, is nothing but love for the divine. And love is nothing but identification.

I love someone because I identify with that person. Because I identify with this class. I like to discuss Bhagavad Gita. You like to discuss Bhagavad Gita. I love people who come to this class. So this identification is love.

I don't love my neighbour's child. As much as I love my own child. I identify with my child, my son. So love is nothing but pure identification. Without identification you cannot love anything or any being. So love for the divine is devotion.

But I cannot love the divine without knowing the divine. And therefore Bhagavan spent the last five chapters defining what the divine is, culminating in this Vishwaroop Pradarshan. So Bhagavan says it is possible. And then Bhagavan gives the steps of that vision: Jnatum drastum cha tattvena praveshtum cha parantapa.

First you have to know. For identifying with anyone. I need to know that person. I have to know that person. I can't fall in love with a girl who I never met. I have to know her first.

So jnatum -- knowing first. In our studies we say the first is Shravanam -- listen to the scriptures, listen to the nature of the Lord. This is what we are doing. We are listening from Bhagavan. Then you will see me.

Then you will know me. You will see me in my essence. Wherever I look, I see you. So that's the vision -- Drastum. In our path, through Mananam (reflection), I create a perception of what I have learned. Bhagavan's form is like that.

And then I reflect on it. Have you seen calendar pictures of Vishwarup Darshan? The painters created those iconic images we've all seen -- Bhagavan with many heads and many arms and fire coming out of his mouth. Of course, painters have their limitations. But if you have listened to the five chapters carefully and then you reflect on it, then Bhagavan says, you will see me in my essence.

The last stage is Praveshtum -- then you will identify with me. Pravesham is to become one, to enter into that self. Right now, I am in my limited being. I'm completely identified with this body, this mind, this intellect.

My identification is so complete that there is no real rivalry between my right hand and left hand, my right leg and left leg. That is complete identification with this limited self -- i.e., praveshtum, entered into that "me." Bhagavan says, if you reflect on that Vishwaroop, then you will also enter into that. You will identify with that supreme as you identify with your limited self right now. Here the operative word is Ananya Bhakti.

With single minded devotion, you shall be able to know me. You shall be able to see me. You shall be able to enter into me. The last word he gives us how to do that. So first he says, this vision is not possible without my grace. But it is possible if you are single mindedly devoted to me.

But how can I develop that single-minded devotion? Bhagavan answers in the last verse of this chapter. Mat Karma Krit -- the very first thing he says is, do everything for me. Continue doing everything you're doing right now. You think you're doing it for you, you're doing it for your family, you're doing it for your country. He says, just think -- it's all me.
snippets.reflection:
Krishna now reveals the secret: "Only by tireless devotion can I be seen and known; only thus can a man become one with Me." The word used is "ananya bhakti" - single-pointed, exclusive devotion. This is followed by a progression: know Me (jnatum), see Me (drastum), and enter into Me (praveshtum). These correspond to the traditional steps of shravana (hearing), manana (reflection), and nididhyasana (meditation/absorption). Knowledge comes first, then vision, then complete identification.

The key insight is that devotion (bhakti) is not mere emotion but deep identification. We love what we identify with - our children, our work, our country. Love and identification go together. To develop devotion to the divine requires knowing the divine (hence chapters 7-10 describing Krishna's nature), then seeing the divine in the world (the vision of chapter 11), and finally entering into complete identification where the sense of separation dissolves entirely.

For today's practice, work with the concept of "ananya" - single-pointed, without another. Examine where your devotion currently goes. Most of us are devoted to many things: comfort, success, approval, security, pleasure. These divided devotions scatter our energy. What would it mean to have all these secondary devotions organized under one primary devotion - to truth, to the divine, to consciousness itself? Begin by noticing when you serve lesser gods throughout the day. Each choice for immediate gratification over deeper truth is a moment of divided devotion.
snippets.shortReflection: Look at where your devotion actually goes - not where you say it goes. Comfort? Success? Others' approval? Your energy is scattered across a dozen small gods. What would your life look like if it all pointed in one direction?

snippets.reflection:
The chapter concludes with a comprehensive instruction: "He whose every action is done for My sake, to whom I am the final goal, who loves Me only and hates no one - only he can realize Me." This single verse summarizes the entire path: Mat-karma-krit (actions for Me), Mat-paramah (I as supreme goal), Mad-bhaktah (devoted to Me), Sanga-varjitah (free from attachment), Nirvairah (without enmity toward any being). These five qualities together describe the integrated spiritual life.

Each quality connects to the vision Arjuna has just witnessed. When you see that all beings are within the divine, acting for God means acting for the good of all. When you see that nothing exists outside the divine, making God your supreme goal means aligning with ultimate reality. Loving God only does not mean hating the world but loving the divine in and through the world. Freedom from attachment follows naturally when you see the temporary nature of all forms. And hatred toward any being becomes impossible when you recognize all beings as expressions of the One.

For your practice today, take these five qualities as a checklist. As you go through your day, ask: Is this action offered to the divine or serving my ego? Is my goal in this moment ultimate truth or temporary gain? Am I relating to this person with love for the divine presence in them? Am I attached to this outcome or free? Do I harbor enmity toward anyone? Do not expect perfection, but use these as orientation points. Each time you remember to check, you strengthen the pathways of spiritual awareness.
snippets.shortReflection: Check yourself throughout the day: Is this action for your ego or for something larger? Are you attached to the outcome or free? Do you resent anyone right now? These aren't theoretical questions - they're real-time diagnostics for how awake you actually are.
