verseTranslations: Enjoying solitude, abstemiousness, his body, mind and speech under perfect control, absorbed in meditation, he becomes free - always filled with the spirit of renunciation.
Having abandoned selfishness, power, arrogance, anger and desire, possessing nothing of his own and having attained peace, he is fit to join the Eternal Spirit.

And when he becomes one with the Eternal, and his soul knows the bliss that belongs to the Self, he feels no desire and no regret, he regards all beings equally and enjoys the blessing of supreme devotion to Me.
snippets.commentary:
All the discussion so far was about Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas -- this is Sattvik, this is Rajasik, and so on.

So the natural tendency is to think, "Well, I'll pick the best which I can find. This looks like *Sattva*, so I'll just do Sattvik things only." But our tendencies and our desires and the coloring of our mind won't let us do that. So the advice from Bhagavan is Sahajam *Karma* kontea sadoshena PI Natya Jat.

Do the actions which come naturally to you -- those which are in line with your own personality, your tendencies, your likings, your dislikings. Do those actions even though you find them to have defects. Because I have learned 17 chapters of Bhagavad Gita now, and suddenly I find that most of my actions are Rajasik.

That's your nature right now that comes naturally to you. That's where the Bhagavad Gita started. Bhagavan said to Arjuna, you are a warrior.

The Rajasic *action* is your nature in the Kshatriya. You can't give it up right now, run towards jungle to meditate, because that will be against your tendencies in nature. That will actually create more harm to your path of evolution than help you.

It won't purify your mind, pollute your mind and confuse your mind. So Sahajam *Karma* kaun teja sadoshana pen Natya Jat. Do not give up the actions which come naturally to you.

Even though you find some defects, they are not perfect. And then Bhagavan said that by doing so you will purify yourself and consolation given to Sarvarambahi kadushena dumena agnihi ava vritaha all actions, no matter how pure you see them have some defects. There is always a side effect to even the best medicine you can take.

The Bhagavan said Any actions which you have to perform in accordance with your nature even if you find the faults in it, continue. Because every *action* will have its own defects. But then what do I do with it? The only thing you can do is perfect your attitude towards your actions.

Actions by nature has their own pluses and minuses but you can change your attitude towards your actions. So the next few verses which we have seen say Asakta Buddhi -- the first thing you do is detach your intellect from your actions. Asaktabuddhi Sarvatra Jitatma Vigataspruhaha -- I'm doing these things because they come naturally to me.

As I said, Gita class is a Kamya *Karma* for me, because I like to do it, it is my *desire* to do it. So if it comes naturally to you, do it. But Bhagavan said, Asaktabuddhehe -- detach your mind and intellect from those actions.

Sarvatra Jitatma -- have *self-control* over your desires, your likings, and dislikes. I'm doing it, but I may not have any control of the outcome. I may not be allowed to do these things; the environment, the situation may not allow me.

I need to be content with that, without *attachment*. I want to do it, but if there is no opportunity to do it, I'll continue with what is available to me. The goal here is to achieve a state of Naishkarmya Siddhi -- whatever I do, I do not feel that I'm doing it.

As I said, when we are working on our hobbies, it's not work. I'm putting in lots of effort, but I don't consider it work because that's my hobby. The other day Krishna told me, "I'm going to call you.

We're going to practice together." Because when we are not practicing, it's not really working. "When are you going to call me?" "Well, Saturday I'm not available," because that becomes work for me. Naishkarmya Siddhi is like this: when everything I do becomes my hobby, I become actionless. It's all basically in line with my nature.

Paramam Sanyasena Adhigacchati -- such a person achieves the highest level of *renunciation*. By doing the things which you are supposed to do, you can achieve *sannyasa*. The definition of *sannyasa* is giving up the sense of agency.

Not giving up things and beings, but giving up the sense of agency -- "I am doing it" and "I am enjoying it." When you give that up, you are a sannyasi. Bhagavan said, if you do all the things in line with your nature, you will never have that sense of agency, nor will you even notice that you are enjoying it. You get so engrossed in the stuff which you do for your hobby that neither you are aware that you are putting lots of efforts into it, nor whether it's painful or enjoyable.

Music practice was the most painful thing I had when I was going to my teacher's classes for that little time. But it was still what I wanted to do. So whether it was a pain or a joy, I never noticed it.

This is something I want to do. That Bhagavan says -- in that state you are neither aware that you are the doer nor aware that you are the enjoyer. When you achieve that state, you have achieved *sannyasa*.

With that the next verse says Siddhim prapto yatha brahma tatha apnoti nibodame sama se nay kaunteya nista *gnana* seya yapara. Now I'll tell you in brief how to reach *Brahman*, having achieved that siddhi -- the Naishkarmya Siddhi. Now everything comes naturally to me.

I do everything naturally. I don't have any anxiety about whether I'm enjoying or suffering through it, or whether good will come out of it. I just enjoy doing it.

Therefore I'm doing it. He said, achieving that siddhi in your actions and achieving *sannyasa* through that -- how you can then achieve *Brahman*, I will tell you now. So now comes the prescription or the detailed guidance of how to achieve that.

The verse we have seen after that is Buddaya visuddaya Yuktah dhruti atmanam niyam yucha. First thing is Buddaya Vishuddaya -- you have to purify your intellect. My intellect is right now polluted by my *ego*.

My *ego* says I am always right, even though everybody else says otherwise. My intellect says I am the smartest among all. So Buddhaya Vishuddaya -- the purified intellect will see things as they are.

The intellect is purified by not having *ego* polluting it. Dhruti Atmanam -- be firm in your own *self*. This is what I want to do.

This is what I like to do. And this is where I am putting my efforts. Dhruti Atmanam firm in your own *self*.

What is my true nature? I know what I really like. I was just listening to NPR yesterday and some guy who was a lawyer and has a nice corporate practice, he gives up and becomes a LEGO artist. I don't know whether anybody heard that.

In other words, he makes complex form of lions and stuff. He's basically an artist whose work is now displayed all these places. But he gave up the job and became a LEGO artist.

And LEGO company provides him free logos. When they have a new LEGO comes out in thousands and he creates whatever. He said that the worst day as an artist is better than the best day as a lawyer.

For me, therefore I did it. He found what he likes. He followed Bhagavad Gita without reading it.

I want to do this no matter what the outcome may be. But this is what I like. Buddaya Visuddhaya Having purified my intellect, what is my true nature? Our intellect typically gets polluted by worrying about what others will think of us.

And therefore we make choices accordingly. We choose our profession -- at least in my time it was very simple. You didn't have to figure out what you like.

If you don't get admission in medicine, go to chemical engineering. Chemical engineering doesn't work out? Go to mechanical engineering. Mechanical doesn't work out? Electrical.

Then civil. And if you are completely out of all that, go to architecture. You didn't have to figure out what you like.

You just figured out what the social scale was. Bhagavan said that's a perfect recipe for disaster for you. Dhruti Atmanam Niyamyacha Sabdayati Visayam Tektva Ragadveso, vidashyacha sabdadi sound, etc.

In other words, all the sense objects from outside which is polluting your mind and intellect. You are not getting disturbed by this. I wish I can become an artist but there is no money in it.

Doctors make more money, so let me go to medicine even though I hate that profession. There was one guy on Kaun Banega Karorpati. He had just done his internship, and Amitabh Bachchan asked him, "So after that, what next?" He said, "What do you mean?" "Don't you want to do MD or MS or something?" He said, "Yeah, I can do MD or MS, but I'm not interested in it." "Why are you not interested in furthering your career?" He said, "I don't like medicine.

My parents wanted me to go to medicine. That's why I went to medicine." But I want to be an IAS officer. I've seen IAS officers.

I've seen what they do and their power and their influence. And that's what I want to be. So I did what my parents wanted me to do.

Now I'm going to do what I want to do. And how do I achieve this purified intellect and *self-control*? Vivikta Sevi, Laghvashi -- now comes the discipline or guidance for how you can find out what you really like. How do you find out what your true nature is? How do I align my actions with my own nature? Vivikta Sevi -- solitude.

Solitude is something we think about. We are all afraid of loneliness. I'll tell you -- when we were young, if on Saturday you had no invitation to go to any party, we didn't know what to do. "Rajan, what are you doing over the weekend?" "So Rajan, how was your weekend?" I said, "It's always the same.

My weekends are always the same." "Which party did you go to?" If you don't get invited to a party, you don't know what to do with your life. That weekend you're completely lost. Learn to be happy with yourself.

Find a way that you can enjoy solitude. That you think, thank God nobody is now here. I can be by myself and enjoy my time.

I'm sure most of your parents went through that. But solitude is a practice to figure out how you can enjoy yourself by yourself. Laghvashi -- eating but little.

Other texts say: eat as much as you would take your medicine. Your medication -- you never take more than what your doctor says you should take. One tablet means one tablet.

That's what the doctor said, right? Not, "Well, the doctor says one, but I'm a little more aggressive about it, so I'm going to take three at a time." Take only what you need. Your food should be just like that -- only what you need. The texts elaborately describe that a quarter of your belly should be filled with food, a quarter left for water, and half left for air.

That much you should eat -- Laghvashi -- because you know that when you're overstuffed, you're uncomfortable and the mind is not available for anything else. Laghvashi Yata-Vak-Kaya-Manasaha -- control over your speech, body, and mind. Vak (speech) includes all organs of *action*.

It's an indicator: all the organs of *action* should be in control. It does not say stop them -- just keep them in control through moderation. Kaya -- body.

The body is the gross form of my mind.
snippets.reflection:
These verses provide the complete prescription for Self-realization. Verse 52 lists the practices: vivikta-sevi (cultivating solitude), laghvashi (eating lightly), yata-vak-kaya-manasa (controlling speech, body, and mind), dhyana-yoga-para (devoted to meditation), and vairagyam samupashrita (established in dispassion). These are not random austerities but a coherent program for purifying the instrument through which we perceive reality. Notice the emphasis on moderation - laghu (light) eating, yata (controlled) faculties - not extreme suppression.

Verse 53 lists what must be abandoned: ahamkara (ego), bala (force/power), darpa (arrogance), kama (desire), krodha (anger), and parigraha (possessiveness). Casting these off, one becomes nirmama (without "mine-ness") and shanta (peaceful), qualifying for Brahma-bhuyaya - becoming one with Brahman. Verse 54 describes the result: Brahma-bhuta (established in Brahman), prasannatma (serene-minded), neither grieving nor craving, equal toward all beings, and attaining supreme devotion.

The path is clear but challenging. Today, practice vivikta-seva - cultivating moments of solitude, even briefly. Examine your laghu-ashi - are you eating more than needed? Practice yata-vak - restraint in speech before responding. These small adjustments accumulate. Also examine: where does ahamkara (ego) drive your actions? Where does parigraha (possessiveness) create suffering? Identify one instance of each today and consciously release it. The promise is profound: through consistent practice, one attains prasannatma - a naturally serene mind that neither grieves loss nor craves gain.
snippets.shortReflection: When was the last time you were truly alone, not just physically but mentally? When did you last let silence be silent instead of filling it? Your mind is noisy because you keep feeding it. One moment of real solitude today—just try it.

snippets.title: Day 232: Devotion Reveals the Divine
snippets.sanskrit:
भक्त्या मामभिजानाति यावान्यश्चास्मि तत्त्वतः |
ततो मां तत्त्वतो ज्ञात्वा विशते तदनन्तरम् ||

सर्वकर्माण्यपि सदा कुर्वाणो मद्व्यपाश्रयः |
मत्प्रसादादवाप्नोति शाश्वतं पदमव्ययम् ||

चेतसा सर्वकर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्परः |
बुद्धियोगमुपाश्रित्य मच्चित्तः सततं भव ||
snippets.transliteration:
bhaktyā mām abhijānāti yāvān yaśh chāsmi tattvataḥ
tato māṁ tattvato jñātvā viśhate tad-anantaram

sarva-karmāṇy api sadā kurvāṇo mad-vyapāśhrayaḥ
mat-prasādād avāpnoti śhāśhvataṁ padam avyayam

chetasā sarva-karmāṇi mayi sannyasya mat-paraḥ
buddhi-yogam upāśhritya mach-chittaḥ satataṁ bhava
verseTranslations: By such devotion, he sees Me, who I am and what I am; and thus realising the Truth, he enters My Kingdom.
Relying on Me in all his action and doing them for My sake, he attains, by My Grace, Eternal and Unchangeable Life.
Surrender then thy actions unto Me, live in Me, concentrate thine intellect on Me, and think always of Me.
snippets.commentary:
We are literally coming to the end of Bhagavan's advice in this chapter. So in the beginning, obviously, we have seen that the goal of life is to achieve permanent happiness. And we have heard from our scriptures that the only way one can achieve that perfect happiness is either one becomes a sannyasi or a yogi. Everyone else is in the rut of life. And therefore, if that's your goal, to achieve that permanent happiness, you have to either become a sannyasi or a yogi.

So the chapter opened with the definition of sannyasi and yogi. The one who has renounced the sense of "I am the doer" -- the sense of agency -- is the sannyasi. And who is the yogi? The one who has given up the *desire* for the fruits of actions is a yogi. So to achieve that permanent happiness, I have to either become a sannyasi or a yogi. And then the prescription came.

It is easier for us to give up the fruits of actions than giving up the sense of agency. *Ego* is so entrenched in my personality right now that for me to think I'm not doing it is more difficult. I must at least give up the expectations for desired results of my actions. I can start with that. If I have to do that, I first have to understand what is action and how it is done, what is my involvement in performing my actions. So we have this detailed analysis of what is *action*, what is an actor, and what propels that *action*.

The *knowledge* propels my actions. My knowledge about myself and this world, my relationship with this world drives me to act in this world. So we have detailed analysis of these three, the *action*, the actor, and the *knowledge*. We have seen that all of these three are driven by the texture of my mind. My mind has either a sattvic, Rajasic or tamasic tendencies that will make me either a sattvic actor, Rajasic actor, tamasic actor, that will drive me to the sattvic actions, rajasic actions or tamasic actions. So the texture of my mind is the basis for my life.

Who I am today is a reflection of my mind. With *self-introspection*, I may come to a conclusion about the makeup of my mind. Right now I'm 20% Sattvic, 60% Rajasic, and 20% Tamasic. I really don't have a choice to change that overnight. Just because I go to a doctor to get my blood work done which I do every four months and they say your cholesterol is too high, triglycerides are way out of control.

Just knowing that, I will not be able to change it right away. Neither is there any magic bullet where I can change it overnight. But I can start on a course of *action* -- a course of *action* which my doctors constantly, every four months, remind me of. I remember the first month, but for three months I take it easy. And as soon as the fourth month comes, I'm vigilant again. I have to be in that prescribed method consistently.

So the first thing is I have to accept my condition. I have to accept that I have the high cholesterol and high triglycerides and I have this propensity to get a heart attack and all that. If I deny that, if I'm in denial -- for a long time I denied my blood pressure. I go to my one doctor, my blood pressure always comes out right. I go anywhere else, my blood pressure is very high. So I go to the insurance company, they check and say, "Your blood pressure is high."

I said, "No, no, you are wrong. Let me go back to my doctor, I'll check it out." For some reason it worked -- every time I go there, my blood pressure is normal. I go anywhere else, my blood pressure is not normal. So I was in complete denial that I have high blood pressure.

Finally I had to accept that I probably do have high blood pressure. So the first step is acceptance -- accepting that I may have this condition. The conditioning which I see as myself is not in my control. It was in my control at one point of time, but it has now become the past. So I have now become who I am because of all my past experiences and actions. And I accept that now I have to work on it.

So first thing I have to do is what comes naturally to me at this time and then take it from there what my goal would be. So Bhagavan said, now if your goal is to achieve permanent happiness, you have come to this conclusion: this is the makeup of your mind. The advice is Sahajam *Karma* Kaunteya Sadosham Api Na Tyajet. Do the actions which come naturally to you, even though they are imperfect. My chosen field of *action* may not be the most popular, the most appreciated.

But that's what my nature is. I like carpentry and I want to be a carpenter. I like arts and I want to be an artist. They always have this hungry artists exhibitions because artists go hungry. But that's the chosen field comes naturally to me. The Bhagavan said, sahajam *karma* kaunteya sadosha bin natya jat.

You cannot give up the field of actions which come naturally to you. First advice, Clear guidance. Stay in the field which comes naturally to you and then go from there. So the next advice is then. Okay, Now I have figured out what my natural field of *action* is. But how should I act so that I'll get the benefit of that?

The next thing is Asaktah Jitatma -- without *attachment* and without any expectation. We have seen there are only two paths: either to become a sannyasi or a yogi. Yogi is the one who gives up Karma Phala, the *desire* for fruits of *action*. So I've found the field of my actions.

I'm ready to now launch my career in that field or my endeavors -- but without any expectation. I will do what I like to the best I can. What comes out of my actions is not in my control, because I am not the *Karma* Faladatta. *Karma* Faladatta is always the Lord, Ishvara, somebody other than me.

I need to leave it to them their duties to perform diligently. I will perform my *duty* diligently. The Bhagavan said, perform your actions without *attachment* expectations in the field which comes naturally to you. Doing so, you will develop *devotion* for me. You will align your thoughts with the one who empowers you to do these actions. So therefore he said, become one with me.

Offer everything to me. And the last few verses which you have seen. He says, bhaktiya mam abhijanati yavat na aschasmi tatvatah tatomam tattvato gnatva visatei tad anantharam. Just by acting in this manner of *offering* everything to him. As we have seen in detail the previous verses, once I decided the field of my actions, I decided that I am not really the one who empowers me to act. The *consciousness* functioning through me as my life empowers me to act.

I'll be only able to conduct Gita classes as long as I'm alive. The day I drop dead, Gita classes will be history. That's because my *consciousness* in me allows me to understand Bhagavad Gita. So the empowering authority is something other than me. That which connects the electricity in this room is the empowering authority for the electricity. We have lights, we have air conditioning.

Right now we are pretty happy. Things are working fine. But when they first rented the place, the electricity wasn't there. He thought, "I am the Almighty for this place." Calls me up and says, "Not working."

I said, I think the machine is not working. Electricity is not connecting through Dominion Virginia Power. Dominion Virginia Power is the final authority that the electricity comes here. I have a limited power to turn the switch on and off when I need that. But in that limited power, I start thinking because it is always there. I think I am in control and I can turn this thing on and off.

It is only when the power goes out I realize I am just a Nimitta Matra. Virginia Power decides whether I have electricity or not. As long as that electricity is functioning through this space, I can control this space. When Dominion Virginia Power connection is disconnected, no matter how many times I turn the switch on and off, nothing happens. Bhagavan said, you need to recognize this fact that you are connected to me as the supreme *consciousness* which is functioning through you. If you keep that in mind all the time, they will make sure that that connection never gets disconnected.

See, when I design buildings, most buildings have normal electricity connection. And then when there is power outage, the connection goes out. But I designed the emergency shelter. Actually medical examiner's office in downtown. Well, you can't have the power go out during emergency. That is the time when there's a disaster.

That's the time that office becomes most active. They may have all these disaster victims coming to this place. Those pathologists have to work overnight to deal with them. So you need to have a dual power system for that. We connected that building from two different grids. So even though one grid is out, the other grid is connected.

They will never be out of that electrical connection. That's where you will have this permanent connection. Bhagavan said, if you want *eternal* happiness, you need to make sure that your connection to me is always connected. And for that, you have to offer everything that you do to me. Remembering constantly that I can only do this because he's functioning through me. With that attitude, you will develop *devotion* for him.

You will be constantly attached to him. So we both have to have that dual connection. Bhagavan has to have connection with me and I have to have connection with him. That connection when developed, we call it *devotion*. It's one that *devotion* takes place. *Bhakti* mam Avijanati Yavatna Asha asmi Tattvatahara Tatotam tattvoto Gnatva visate tat Anantaram.

By *devotion* he knows me in essence. Once I become identified completely with someone or something, I know that thing or being in its essence or his essence. He forthwith enters into me the supreme. Once I completely identify myself with the supreme *self*, I enters into him. In other words, I become one with that supreme being. Sarvakarmani API sada Kurvanaha mat vyapaasrayah mat prasadat avapnothi Saswatam padam avyayam.

The process took place. I gave up identification with my *ego*. I chose the field of my actions. I started working in the field of my actions without any expectations and offered all my actions to him. Now with that connection I have identified completely with him. So now my life is doing all actions always taking refuge in him with his *grace*.

Now I have not become happy with my efforts. I have become peaceful and happy with his *grace*. This space is properly conditioned and lit up right now -- by the grace of Dominion Virginia Power. When their *grace* is taken away from me, the lights will go away and the air conditioning will go away. As long as I recognize that the lights and air conditioning are not because of me -- not because I'm paying the bills, but because of their *grace* in connecting electricity to this space -- then I will be fine.

Then I'll develop that *devotion* to Dominion Virginia Power. As soon as the bill comes, pay the bill. Bhagavan said, one who becomes one with me, with this root of actions he has become one with me and therefore he achieves that Saswatam Padam avyayam.
snippets.reflection:
These verses describe the culmination of the spiritual journey through devotion. Verse 55 declares: bhaktya mam abhijanati - through devotion one knows Me in essence, and knowing Me thus in truth, immediately enters into Me. This is not intellectual knowing but direct realization through love. The analogy of complete identification applies - just as we intimately know those we deeply love, complete devotion to the Divine yields complete knowledge of the Divine.

Verse 56 offers remarkable assurance: sarva-karmani api sada kurvano - even while always performing all actions, one who takes refuge in Me attains by My grace the eternal, imperishable abode. This is the Gita's liberating promise: you do not need to abandon action for liberation. Continue your duties, but mat-vyapashraya - take refuge in the Divine. Mat-prasadat - by grace, not solely personal effort, comes the eternal state. Verse 57 summarizes: mentally surrender all actions to Me, keep Me as your supreme goal, practice buddhi-yoga, and constantly fix your mind on Me.

The practical instruction is clear: maintain your connection to the Source through all activities. Like staying connected to the power grid while using electricity for various purposes, stay connected to the Divine while engaging with the world. Today, practice mat-chitta - keeping the Divine in your awareness through activities. Before each task, briefly remember the Source of your abilities. During activities, occasionally pause and reconnect. This is not adding a spiritual practice to your day but infusing your entire day with spiritual awareness. The promise is that this constant remembrance, combined with offering all actions, leads to the eternal abode - by grace.
snippets.shortReflection: You don't need to quit your job and move to a cave. Keep doing what you're doing, but stay connected to something bigger than the task list. Like a phone plugged in while you use it—stay plugged into what matters while you work.

snippets.title: Day 233: Nature Compels You to Act

verseTranslations: Fix but thy mind on Me, and by My grace thou shalt overcome the obstacles in thy path. But if, misled by pride, thou wilt not listen, then indeed thou shalt be lost.
If thou in thy vanity thinkest of avoiding this fight, thy will shall not be fulfilled, for Nature herself will compel thee.
O Arjuna! Thy duty binds thee. From thine own nature has it arisen, and that which in thy delusion thou desire not to do, that very thing thou shalt do. Thou art helpless.
snippets.commentary:
We are literally coming to the end of Bhagavan's advice in this chapter. So in the beginning, obviously, we have seen that the goal of life is to achieve permanent happiness. And we have heard from our scriptures that the only way one can achieve that perfect happiness is either one becomes a sannyasi or a yogi. Everyone else is in the rut of life. And therefore, if that's your goal, to achieve that permanent happiness, you have to either become a sannyasi or a yogi.

So the chapter opened with the definition of sannyasi and yogi. The one who has renounced the sense of "I am the doer" -- the sense of agency -- is the sannyasi. And who is the yogi? The one who has given up the *desire* for the fruits of actions is a yogi. So to achieve that permanent happiness, I have to either become a sannyasi or a yogi. And then the prescription came.

It is easier for us to give up the fruits of actions than giving up the sense of agency. *Ego* is so entrenched in my personality right now that for me to think I'm not doing it is more difficult. I must at least give up the expectations for desired results of my actions. I can start with that. If I have to do that, I first have to understand what is action and how it is done, what is my involvement in performing my actions. So we have this detailed analysis of what is *action*, what is an actor, and what propels that *action*.

The *knowledge* propels my actions. My knowledge about myself and this world, my relationship with this world drives me to act in this world. So we have detailed analysis of these three, the *action*, the actor, and the *knowledge*. We have seen that all of these three are driven by the texture of my mind. My mind has either a sattvic, Rajasic or tamasic tendencies that will make me either a sattvic actor, Rajasic actor, tamasic actor, that will drive me to the sattvic actions, rajasic actions or tamasic actions. So the texture of my mind is the basis for my life.

Who I am today is a reflection of my mind. With *self-introspection*, I may come to a conclusion about the makeup of my mind. Right now I'm 20% Sattvic, 60% Rajasic, and 20% Tamasic. I really don't have a choice to change that overnight. Just because I go to a doctor to get my blood work done which I do every four months and they say your cholesterol is too high, triglycerides are way out of control.

Just knowing that, I will not be able to change it right away. Neither is there any magic bullet where I can change it overnight. But I can start on a course of *action* -- a course of *action* which my doctors constantly, every four months, remind me of. I remember the first month, but for three months I take it easy. And as soon as the fourth month comes, I'm vigilant again. I have to be in that prescribed method consistently.

So the first thing is I have to accept my condition. I have to accept that I have the high cholesterol and high triglycerides and I have this propensity to get a heart attack and all that. If I deny that, if I'm in denial -- for a long time I denied my blood pressure. I go to my one doctor, my blood pressure always comes out right. I go anywhere else, my blood pressure is very high. So I go to the insurance company, they check and say, "Your blood pressure is high."

I said, "No, no, you are wrong. Let me go back to my doctor, I'll check it out." For some reason it worked -- every time I go there, my blood pressure is normal. I go anywhere else, my blood pressure is not normal. So I was in complete denial that I have high blood pressure.

Finally I had to accept that I probably do have high blood pressure. So the first step is acceptance -- accepting that I may have this condition. The conditioning which I see as myself is not in my control. It was in my control at one point of time, but it has now become the past. So I have now become who I am because of all my past experiences and actions. And I accept that now I have to work on it.

So first thing I have to do is what comes naturally to me at this time and then take it from there what my goal would be. So Bhagavan said, now if your goal is to achieve permanent happiness, you have come to this conclusion: this is the makeup of your mind. The advice is Sahajam *Karma* Kaunteya Sadosham Api Na Tyajet. Do the actions which come naturally to you, even though they are imperfect. My chosen field of *action* may not be the most popular, the most appreciated.

But that's what my nature is. I like carpentry and I want to be a carpenter. I like arts and I want to be an artist. They always have this hungry artists exhibitions because artists go hungry. But that's the chosen field comes naturally to me. The Bhagavan said, sahajam *karma* kaunteya sadosha bin natya jat.

You cannot give up the field of actions which come naturally to you. First advice, Clear guidance. Stay in the field which comes naturally to you and then go from there. So the next advice is then. Okay, Now I have figured out what my natural field of *action* is. But how should I act so that I'll get the benefit of that?

The next thing is Asaktah Jitatma -- without *attachment* and without any expectation. We have seen there are only two paths: either to become a sannyasi or a yogi. Yogi is the one who gives up Karma Phala, the *desire* for fruits of *action*. So I've found the field of my actions.

I'm ready to now launch my career in that field or my endeavors -- but without any expectation. I will do what I like to the best I can. What comes out of my actions is not in my control, because I am not the *Karma* Faladatta. *Karma* Faladatta is always the Lord, Ishvara, somebody other than me.

I need to leave it to them their duties to perform diligently. I will perform my *duty* diligently. The Bhagavan said, perform your actions without *attachment* expectations in the field which comes naturally to you. Doing so, you will develop *devotion* for me. You will align your thoughts with the one who empowers you to do these actions. So therefore he said, become one with me.

Offer everything to me. And the last few verses which you have seen. He says, bhaktiya mam abhijanati yavat na aschasmi tatvatah tatomam tattvato gnatva visatei tad anantharam. Just by acting in this manner of *offering* everything to him. As we have seen in detail the previous verses, once I decided the field of my actions, I decided that I am not really the one who empowers me to act. The *consciousness* functioning through me as my life empowers me to act.

I'll be only able to conduct Gita classes as long as I'm alive. The day I drop dead, Gita classes will be history. That's because my *consciousness* in me allows me to understand Bhagavad Gita. So the empowering authority is something other than me. That which connects the electricity in this room is the empowering authority for the electricity. We have lights, we have air conditioning.

Right now we are pretty happy. Things are working fine. But when they first rented the place, the electricity wasn't there. He thought, "I am the Almighty for this place." Calls me up and says, "Not working."

I said, I think the machine is not working. Electricity is not connecting through Dominion Virginia Power. Dominion Virginia Power is the final authority that the electricity comes here. I have a limited power to turn the switch on and off when I need that. But in that limited power, I start thinking because it is always there. I think I am in control and I can turn this thing on and off.

It is only when the power goes out I realize I am just a Nimitta Matra. Virginia Power decides whether I have electricity or not. As long as that electricity is functioning through this space, I can control this space. When Dominion Virginia Power connection is disconnected, no matter how many times I turn the switch on and off, nothing happens. Bhagavan said, you need to recognize this fact that you are connected to me as the supreme *consciousness* which is functioning through you. If you keep that in mind all the time, they will make sure that that connection never gets disconnected.

See, when I design buildings, most buildings have normal electricity connection. And then when there is power outage, the connection goes out. But I designed the emergency shelter. Actually medical examiner's office in downtown. Well, you can't have the power go out during emergency. That is the time when there's a disaster.

That's the time that office becomes most active. They may have all these disaster victims coming to this place. Those pathologists have to work overnight to deal with them. So you need to have a dual power system for that. We connected that building from two different grids. So even though one grid is out, the other grid is connected.

They will never be out of that electrical connection. That's where you will have this permanent connection. Bhagavan said, if you want *eternal* happiness, you need to make sure that your connection to me is always connected. And for that, you have to offer everything that you do to me. Remembering constantly that I can only do this because he's functioning through me. With that attitude, you will develop *devotion* for him.

You will be constantly attached to him. So we both have to have that dual connection. Bhagavan has to have connection with me and I have to have connection with him. That connection when developed, we call it *devotion*. It's one that *devotion* takes place. *Bhakti* mam Avijanati Yavatna Asha asmi Tattvatahara Tatotam tattvoto Gnatva visate tat Anantaram.

By *devotion* he knows me in essence. Once I become identified completely with someone or something, I know that thing or being in its essence or his essence. He forthwith enters into me the supreme. Once I completely identify myself with the supreme *self*, I enters into him. In other words, I become one with that supreme being. Sarvakarmani API sada Kurvanaha mat vyapaasrayah mat prasadat avapnothi Saswatam padam avyayam.

The process took place. I gave up identification with my *ego*. I chose the field of my actions. I started working in the field of my actions without any expectations and offered all my actions to him. Now with that connection I have identified completely with him. So now my life is doing all actions always taking refuge in him with his *grace*.

Now I have not become happy with my efforts. I have become peaceful and happy with his *grace*. This space is properly conditioned and lit up right now -- by the grace of Dominion Virginia Power. When their *grace* is taken away from me, the lights will go away and the air conditioning will go away. As long as I recognize that the lights and air conditioning are not because of me -- not because I'm paying the bills, but because of their *grace* in connecting electricity to this space -- then I will be fine.

Then I'll develop that *devotion* to Dominion Virginia Power. As soon as the bill comes, pay the bill. Bhagavan said, one who becomes one with me, with this root of actions he has become one with me and therefore he achieves that Saswatam Padam avyayam.
snippets.reflection:
These verses present both the promise and the warning. Verse 58: mat-chitta - with mind fixed on Me, you will overcome all obstacles by My grace. But aham-karat na shroshyasi - if through ego you will not listen, you will perish. The choice is stark: surrender and be carried across all difficulties, or cling to ego and be destroyed. Verse 59 addresses Arjuna's specific situation: if through ego you think "I will not fight," your resolution is vain - Prakriti will compel you. This applies universally: we cannot escape our nature through willful avoidance.

Verse 60 drives the point home: svabhava-jena nibaddha - bound by your own karma born of your nature, what you do not wish to do through delusion, you will do helplessly. This is not fatalism but psychological truth. Our vasanas (tendencies) are powerful forces that will express themselves. The question is not whether to act but whether to act consciously or be driven unconsciously. Arjuna cannot avoid being a warrior; his nature will assert itself. Better to fight consciously with understanding than to fight unconsciously driven by repressed instincts.

Examine where ego-resistance is preventing you from doing what needs to be done. What are you avoiding through willful stubbornness that your nature will eventually force you to face? The teaching suggests that surrender is not weakness but wisdom - recognizing that fighting against our fundamental nature is futile. Today, identify one area where you are resisting something that aligns with your dharma. Ask: Is my resistance protecting something valuable, or is it merely ego avoiding what feels threatening? Often what we resist most persistently is exactly what we need to embrace.
snippets.shortReflection: Where are you resisting what you know you need to face? Not what others think you should do, but what deep down you know is yours to handle. That resistance? It's just ego trying to stay safe. What would happen if you stopped fighting your own nature?

snippets.title: Day 234: The Lord Within Every Heart
snippets.sanskrit:

verseTranslations: God dwells in the hearts of all beings, O Arjuna! He causes them to revolve as it were on a wheel by His mystic power.
With all thy strength, fly unto Him and surrender thyself, and by His grace shalt thou attain Supreme Peace and reach the Eternal Home.
Thus have I revealed to thee the Truth, the Mystery of mysteries. Having thought it over, thou art free to act as thou wilt.
snippets.commentary:
We have discussed them before and also experienced them in our life. Something as simple as this: in this world, people have different temperaments. Not all people are alike. Each one has his or her own temperament. Depending on that temperament, he may be good at one thing or another. Everybody is not good at everything, but depending on your temperament, you may be good at something.

And also this temperament will make you like some things and dislike other things. So this temperament is your own nature or your personality. Therefore, because in this world the different people have different personalities, different temperaments, they do different things. Some are good at scholarly pursuits and some are good at doing heroic things and some are good at creating wealth and some are just happy serving others, you may find yourself to be somewhere in this spectrum. Not everybody likes same type of coffee. Some like strong, some like very mild.

Others may be somewhere in between. So you will find yourself somewhere in the spectrum of temperament. Some are very sattvic, some are very tamasic and most of us are somewhere in between. Therefore find out what your real nature is. Bhagawan said this is a fact that each one has his or her own qualities and temperaments. So depending on your temperament, now you have to find the field of activity which is appropriate for you.

So earlier in chapter three, Bhagavan said Swadharma Nidhanam Shreya Paradharma Bhayavahah -- working in your own nature is better, because another's *dharma* is frightening. If you try to do something against your nature, it will be very frightening. You will always be a fish out of water. You are a very artistic person and you want to run a business -- you will be a fish out of water.

You will not feel comfortable. So therefore find your own *Dharma* and then work in it. So in this chapter again he reminds us what is good for you. So he said that Sriyan Swadharmo Vigunaha, Paradharma, Swanushti daat. Your *Dharma* alone is good for you, even though it has faults. It may not be as pristine as others, but this is what your nature is and it is good for you.

And therefore Sahajam, *Karma*, kaunteh. So find the field of activities which come naturally to you. Do the activities which come naturally to you. You shall not incur any sin in doing so. You shall not incur any sin. Continue doing what you like, what comes naturally to you.

And do not worry about whether I'll incur any sin or I'll incur any wrong tendencies. We have learnt in the previous chapter that no matter what your tendencies are and what activities you are performing, you start with Om Tatsat, purify them. So in chapter 17 we have learned that no matter what your Saddha is, whether it is Sattvic, whether it is, whether it is Raja Sikh, whether it is Tamasic, you are acting in that manner. But rather than worrying about whether it is Sattvik, Rajasik, or Tamasik, do whatever is natural to you. But whatever you do, start with Aum. Every activity which you do, remember him, that he is almighty and all pervading.

And he is enabling me to do this activity. So start with Om and say end with Tat, that this is not for me, this is for you. There is nothing that I am doing it for myself because I am not even capable of doing anything. He is all pervading and everything I am doing, I am *offering* to him because he made me do this. So Bhagawan said, with that attitude, when you perform any actions in the field of your liking which come naturally to you, you will find your happiness. We try everything and we get frustrated.

That's because we say, one, you are not pursuing your own *Dharma* and secondly, you think you are doing it for yourself. Those two things, if you correct them -- find the field of activities which is natural to you, and then don't expect anything from it -- Then Bhagavan said that you will be relieved from these sorrows and unhappiness. In spite of all this diversity which we see in this world, there is a profound unity. Iswarahas, Sarvabhutanam, Prudeshe, Arjuna, Tisthati.

He said, this is why you should offer everything to him and remember him all the time. Even though you find yourself to be very different from others, even though you find all these people are very different from each other, there's one thing very common. They are all functioning because of that one single principle functioning through them. There are not several consciousnesses -- mine different from yours, yours different from hers, hers different from his. One *consciousness* functioning through all. Depending on the quality of the equipment, outer behavior will be different from each other.

Just as we have used these examples many many times. This room space is dependent on the conditioning. How far the walls are from each other and how far the ceiling is from the floor. But the space is the same space as it is outside. The space outside and space inside is no different same. All pervading space is in each room in this universe.

Wherever you find a space which is confined by limitations, the space is universal. The same way, Isvara Sarva Bhutanam Hrudeshe Tishtati -- the core of all being is the Ishvara himself residing there. Because of his presence only, things are functioning. But how are they functioning? Bhramayan Sarva Bhutani Yantra Rudhani Mayaya -- by his illusive power *Maya*, everyone is functioning in this world.

They are functioning because of Iswara's presence and his power of *Maya*. The elusive power Brahmayan Sarvabhoot are Yantra Rudhani. It seems like they are just mounted on a machine, helpless to act in this world. We are driven by our own likes and dislikes and vasanas almost compulsively. Whether we like it or not. We see something which is of our liking, we will be attracted towards it.

Something which is of not conducive, we will be staying away from it. Bhagavan said everybody is propelled by this *Maya* as if they are helpless. But at the core of all being, Ishvara is the cause for all beings functioning in this world. Keep that unity in mind. So this is a profound revelation. We knew that everybody is different from each other.

Everyone has their own qualities. Everyone has their liking and disliking. Everyone has their own talents. But see, what is common is the cause for all the talents and all the liking and all the disliking is that all pervading principle. The Ishvara, the Lord himself. So *Brahman*, the all pervading *self*, with his power of *Maya* becomes the almighty Creator Ishwara.

With this *Maya*, he creates this world of plurality. So I myself, with my power of dreaming, I create my own world of dream. While I'm dreaming, I'm by myself. The dream is me. The people in the dream are me. The dreamer himself is also me.

There is no other entity. Only when I wake up, I realize that there were not actually other people around. There were no different sceneries around. So this is like it is in Ishwara's mind, a great dream. So therefore he said Brahmayan Sarva Bhutani Yantra Rudhani *Maya*. By this elusive power of Ishvara, each individual in this world is functioning compulsively.

Driven by their own temperaments and qualities. So therefore he says Tamevasharanam gacha. So now the advice, having understood that people will be different: you are different from everybody else. Do not try to compare yourself with others and don't try to copy them. You find your own bearings, what is good for you, what you like.

Continue functioning, but keep the Lord in mind -- that he is Almighty. He is making me do all these things and therefore I am *offering* everything I do to Him. Tamevasharanam gacha. Take refuge in that Ishvara, that Almighty, all-pervading *consciousness*. Sarva bhavena Bharata -- in all your being, with all your thoughts, whether thinking about your professional life, your relationships, everything.

While you are thinking, put him in the center of it -- all these things are only possible because of Him. Take refuge in him that you are the ones who is enabling me to function in this world as an individual. Tat Prasada paramsanthim Sthanam prapsi Saswatam. If you take refuge in him with all your being, with all your thoughts, no matter what that is, offer it to him that I can only think this way because of you. I can only act this way because of you. Once you start assigning all credits to him, then you are relieved.

You have no responsibilities. So in the end Bhagavan said this individualized *ego* which is identifying with this body, mind and intellect and taking credit for what I'm doing, thinking that I'm the doer. If you just keep that aside, do everything that you are doing right now exactly as you are doing. Because you are doing it as per your nature. You are propelled by your nature to do it. If you try to resist your nature, it creates distortion, a kind of mental disease.

So keep doing what you are doing. Just keep in mind Tamevasharanam Gacha, Sarva Bhavya Bharata. Just take refuge in Him. Make your identification with him versus this limited body, mind and intellect. Tat prasadat paramshantin sthan praapasi Saswatam. The *grace* is when the identification is complete then I obviously become one with him, his qualities become my qualities.

I start thinking, "I now have access to his capacities." You joined a company a day before, and from the next day onwards you're part of the company -- all the resources of the company are yours. You take the brochure of the company and go to a new client and say, "I represent IBM." All of IBM's resources are your resources. But before that, a day before, when you had not joined the company yet, you didn't have that brochure from IBM.

You are just an individual. You can say, "I can do this," and that doesn't really mean much. Once you attach yourself to the resources of the Great, all his resources become your resources; all the qualifications of that company become your qualifications. Once you identify with him and take refuge in him Tat Prasad with his *grace* you will achieve that Santisthanam Propyasi Sastvatam. You will find that *eternal* peace and a firm abode. All you have to do is just take refuge in him and continue doing what you are doing as per your own nature.

Itite Gnanam Akhyatam Guhyat Guhyatram *Maya* Vimrushyat Ashe. We have discussed this thing in detail from chapter two onward. We have analyzed every point. In the end, I came down to this: just follow your own *Dharma*, your own nature. You will not incur any sin.

Do not worry about what other people are doing, do not copy them. Your welfare is in following your own *Dharma* and giving up your ego and *attachment*. And I will take care of everything else. I told you this very secret of *knowledge*. "Secret" means it was hidden from you. It was right there, but hidden from you.

Because of your likes and dislikes, your vasanas, your *ignorance*, you were not able to see this. I took those coverings away from you so that you can see the *knowledge* as it is. I told you in its entirety. Vimrushya Etat Ashesena. Reflect on it in its totality. Don't take a verse here and there from Bhagavad Gita.
snippets.reflection:
Verse 61 reveals a profound truth: ishvara sarva-bhutanam hrid-deshe - the Lord dwells in the hearts of all beings, causing them to revolve as if mounted on a machine (yantra) by the power of Maya. This image combines divine immanence with the mechanical quality of conditioned existence. The Lord is not distant but intimately present in every heart, yet Maya creates the illusion of separate, automatic beings driven by their programming. We are simultaneously divine at core and conditioned at the surface.

Verse 62 delivers the instruction: tam eva sharanam gaccha sarva-bhavena - go to Him alone for refuge with your whole being. The result: tat-prasadat param shantim sthanam prapsyasi shashvatam - by His grace you will attain supreme peace and the eternal abode. Verse 63 concludes Krishna's teaching: I have declared to you this knowledge, the most secret of all secrets. Reflect on it fully, then do as you wish (yathecchasi tatha kuru). This final freedom is remarkable - after all instruction, the choice remains with Arjuna.

The teaching honors your autonomy while pointing to the truth. Today, contemplate the reality that Ishvara dwells in your heart right now - not as a visitor but as the very core of your being. The sense of being a separate mechanism driven by forces beyond your control is Maya's creation. Beneath that programming lies the Lord. Take refuge there - not as an escape from life but as a grounding that transforms how you engage with life. And remember: after receiving all teaching, the choice remains yours. What will you choose today?
snippets.shortReflection: The divine isn't somewhere far away waiting for you to be good enough. It's in your heart right now, under all the noise and busyness. The question isn't whether it's there—it's whether you'll take refuge in it today.

verseTranslations: Only listen once more to My last word, the deepest secret of all; thou art My beloved, thou art My friend, and I speak for thy welfare.
Dedicate thyself to Me, worship Me, sacrifice all for Me, prostrate thyself before Me, and to Me thou shalt surely come. Truly do I pledge thee; thou art My own beloved.
Give up then thy earthly duties, surrender thyself to Me only. Do not be anxious; I will absolve thee from all thy sin.

These verses contain the Gita's supreme teaching. Verse 64 establishes the context: because you are dear to Me, I will speak for your welfare the most secret of all. Verse 65 gives the complete instruction: man-mana bhava mad-bhakto mad-yaji mam namaskuru - fix your mind on Me, be My devotee, worship Me, bow to Me. The promise: mam evaishyasi satyam - you shall come to Me truly, I promise you, for you are dear to Me. This is love speaking to love.

Verse 66 is the charama-shloka, the ultimate verse: sarva-dharman parityajya mam ekam sharanam vraja - abandoning all dharmas, take refuge in Me alone. Aham tva sarva-papebhyo mokshayishyami - I shall liberate you from all sins; do not grieve. This is not abandonment of ethical conduct but transcendence of all limited identifications. Every role we play comes with its dharma - parent, professional, citizen. These are necessary but partial. The instruction is to ultimately take refuge in the One beyond all roles.

This is the heart of surrender: not passive resignation but active trust in the Source of all. The promise "I shall liberate you from all sins" addresses our deepest fear - that our past mistakes have permanently damaged us. They have not. Grace is more powerful than karma. Today, practice this surrender: acknowledge the various dharmas you carry, the roles and their obligations. Then, beneath all these, find the One to whom they are all offered. Say inwardly: "I take refuge in You alone." Notice the peace that comes when the burden of being the sole doer is released. Ma shuchah - do not grieve.
snippets.shortReflection: You're carrying roles and expectations and obligations. They're real, they matter. But underneath all of them, there's something that doesn't come and go with your job title or relationships. Can you touch that, just for a moment today?

snippets.reflection:
These verses address the transmission of knowledge. Verse 67 specifies to whom this teaching should NOT be given: na atapaskaya (one without discipline), na abhaktaya (one without devotion), na ashushrusha (one unwilling to serve/listen), and one who abhyasuyati (cavils or finds fault). This is not exclusion but wisdom - teaching reaches only those prepared to receive it. Forcing spiritual knowledge on unprepared minds creates neither understanding nor transformation.

Verses 68-69 describe the supreme service: teaching this knowledge to sincere devotees is the highest form of worship, and no one is dearer to Krishna than one who shares this wisdom. This is the concept of jnana-yajna - the sacrifice of knowledge. The study group movement embodies this teaching, recognizing that teaching multiplies understanding both for teacher and student.

Consider: What knowledge have you received that is meant to be shared? Not everyone is ready - verse 67's criteria apply. But among those who show discipline, devotion, and willingness to learn, you have something to offer. Today, reflect on one insight from your spiritual journey that has genuinely helped you. Identify one person in your life who might benefit and is ready to receive. The teaching need not be formal - a conversation, a recommended reading, a shared practice. The Gita promises that sharing wisdom with ready students is the highest devotion. What will you share, and with whom?
snippets.shortReflection: What do you know now that you didn't know a year ago—something that actually changed how you live? And who in your life is ready to hear it? Not everyone wants teaching. But someone does.

verseTranslations: He who will study this spiritual discourse of ours, I assure thee, he shall thereby worship Me at the altar of Wisdom.
Yea, he who listens to it with faith and without doubt, even he, freed from evil, shall rise to the worlds which the virtuous attain through righteous deeds.
O Arjuna! Hast thou listened attentively to My words? Has thy ignorance and thy delusion gone?
snippets.commentary:
It boils down to Sreyan Swadharma Vigunaha Paradharma Swanashti da.

Your own Dharma is better for you than other dharma. And therefore he says, Sahajam *Karma* Kamateja Sadosham Abhiyana Tej. These are the two basic facts.

He pointed out to us that your welfare is in staying within your *Dharma*, whatever Dharma you have acquired through your own choice. My *dharma* as an architect -- I chose it myself. I decided to go to architecture school and therefore I became an architect.

Bhagavan said, your welfare is in your Dharma. Don't try to practice something other than what you're good at. Then there was Sahajam *Karma* Kaunteya.

Do what comes naturally to you. Because of all your experiences and vasanas and tendencies and your training, there are few things in life which comes easier for you. And others don't stay with what comes naturally to you, even though other things look more glamorous, more glorious.

But you say, even if your *Dharma*, you found it Sadosha Mapi, even there are some defects in it or not very perfect. Do actions in your own field which come naturally to you. There are the only two things he said, doing so you will overcome all your obstacles and you will never incur sin.

Working in the field which come naturally to you, keeping your own goal in mind that I'm doing it to get my ultimate happiness. But once you will never incur sin. Sin, as we have discussed, is a negative impression on my mind which creates agitations.

All we are looking for in life is peace. Give me peace of mind. Peace of mind only comes when the mind is tranquil.

Because the mind will only be tranquil if you're working according to your own *Dharma*. And then he said the final advice after completing his entire discourse: now you do whatever you think is right for you. He gave you the complete choice one more time and said, let me summarize what I told you.

Manmana Bhava mad Bhaktaha Madhya ji Mam namaskuruhu. In other words, Krishna said, if you want to summarize the entire teachings of Bhagavad Gita in half a verse, this is it. To get the happiness which you are looking for, fix your mind onto me -- me, the all-pervading almighty *self* which is also your *self*.

Focus your mind on that mad Bhaktah worship that identify with that Madhya Ji. Offer all your actions to me. Offer all your actions to the highest goal which you have when you go to the first grade.

I'm learning this and that. Because eventually I want to become a doctor. My granddaughter was telling me yesterday, I have two inventions I want to release before I became a doctor.

So there is an ultimate goal in mind. That ultimate goal is to find perfect happiness. Perfect happiness is only there if my mind is tranquil.

Bhagawan said, Madhya Ji, offer everything to me Maam namaskurohu and take refuge in me. Then he clarified say Sarva *Dharma* and parity. Aham TVA Sarva Papebiha Moksa Kshya minasucha.

Right now you think that you are incomplete. You have lots of baggage -- all your incompleteness and sins, the things which you have not done right. "I have not done this thing right in my life." Bhagawan said, no, you cannot correct yourself on your own. But if you take refuge in me, I can correct that.

Sarva Dharman Parityajya. And we have discussed this Sarva Dharman. Every role that I take, it comes with its own *Dharma*.

Every role a drama actor plays, it comes with its own requirement. Now if I start identifying with each role, then I'll get confused. I will have a nervous breakdown.

I will have a personality disorder. I don't know who I am. Am I a king or a pauper? Because I play so many different roles.

The Bhagawan says, in your life, you take on too many of these roles. All those roles come with their own *Dharma*. My Dharma as a father.

My *Dharma* as an architect. My *Dharma* as a husband. My *Dharma* as a citizen of this country.

My *Dharma* as an employer. All those Dharmas -- if I get bogged down into them and think that they will give me my happiness, then I'll be completely shattered. I do not really know which role is more important than others.

Keep working in that *dharma* when you are there. When you are an architect, act as an architect. When you are father, act as a father.

But at the end of the day, you realize that you are something other than all the roles which you play. An actor in Beverly Hills knows that he is something other than the roles he plays. So Bhagawanja Sarva *Dharma* and Paritya Jya.

At the end of the day, give up. All those dharmas are not yours. But they belong to the roles which you play.

While you're playing that role, you can't give up those dharmas. But once you're out of that role, leave those dharmas with that role and focus on who you are. Who is there One constant in all these roles which has its own *dharma*.

So Bhagawan says, ma makeam sharam Braja. Identify with that one single entity which is pervading through all the roles which you play. Ahamtva Sarva Pape bihamoksik Shami Mashu chah.

Once you identify with that, all the limitations you have in each one of those roles are of no consequence because it only belongs to the role. You may not have played the role correctly. Fine, let's move on to the next one.

One movie gets flopped, the actor doesn't get shattered. He moves on to another one, waiting for the next hit. Don't get caught up in any of those roles as that's the only thing which is mine.

And if I fail there, I have failed in it. Bhagavan said, you don't worry. Once you take refuge in your own *self*, everything will be alright.

Now that you have learnt this *knowledge*, don't just sit back and relax. That's not where your *duty* ends. You have to do your part.

Now that you were privileged enough to know what is right, you also have an obligation to teach others what is right. And I, the parent, was a son at one point of time. And I got the advice from my parents and they told me what is right and wrong.

I made my life right or wrong according to that. And now I learned after my experience what is right and wrong. I have an obligation to pass on that *knowledge* to my children.

Ya Imam paramam guhiyam mad bhakteshu abhi dashyathi bhakti mai param kutva Mama eva isyati asansaya. He said, there is one who declares this, teaches this knowledge of mine to my devotees, not to the people who are not interested in it, but those who are inspired themselves to make their life better, make their life appropriate, remove all the negatives from their life, but they still do not know how to do it. When you find those enthusiastic students, that's what you want to teach them.

Therefore I said, the one who teaches this sacred *knowledge* of mind to my Bhakta, those who are devoted to this knowledge, *Bhakti* mai param kutva maam eva Eshyati asansayaha. I consider that he is worshipping me. Bhagavan said, you don't have to come to my temple every day and put $1 in the Aarti or to do anything special.

The greatest *devotion* we can offer to our teacher is to carry the torch of his knowledge. That's why we do Pada Puja. Because the platform on which my Guru is standing that the platform which I worship, that *knowledge* is important.

Bhagawan said, one who spread this *knowledge* of mine which I gave it to you, to others, I consider him to be my devotee and therefore he will come to me without any doubt. He will become one with me or Sansayah. No other thing needed.

Bhagavan said, you just continue. You learn this *knowledge*, practice it, and then pass it on to the others. That Bhagavan said, I consider to my greatest *devotion*.

So basically it encourages all of us, whatever little we have learned from Bhagavad Gita. There is an obligation to impart the *knowledge* to someone else who is curious to know. He may not have the right frame of understanding, but he wants to know.

You have an obligation to give him that *knowledge*. Bhagawan says, Nachatasmat manushesu kaschinmi priyakrutamaha. None other than that person who carries this torch of *knowledge* is dearer to me than him.

He is the closest to me because he's carrying forward the mission that I have -- that I want to correct the misunderstanding in people. You were confused, Arjuna. I gave you this discourse so that you can now act in your life correctly.

Now you have an obligation to do that to someone else who you will find it in the same situation. And I consider that as my worship that you have appreciated what I have given you. And such a person is dearer to me.

Some other people may come and other things for me, but they are of lesser value than you carrying forward my mission. Bhavita Nachame tasmat anyaha Priyatara Bhuvi, not only now, but even in future, there won't be anyone who is dearer to me than the one who is spreading this *knowledge* to make this world better and spreading the right *knowledge*. So we have this misconception in our Hinduism -- that we obviously don't convert people, we don't encourage people to come to our fold.

In fact, we discourage people: "If someone has to be Hindu, you can't become a Hindu unless you're born Hindu." Sri Bhagawan clearly points out that that's not part of our culture. We do not want forced conversion. We don't want to tell people who have not yet understood to believe in this *knowledge*.

Give him his own time. Because forced conversion, forced imposition, never works in reality anywhere. Therefore you say, find people who are willing to understand this and give this *knowledge*.

That's your obligation. So that's a kind of missionary work. They never said that this *knowledge* should never be given out to anybody, or that it should not be given to people who are not from this class or the other.

Simply: find the right person, the right group of people who are anxious to make their lives better. Give this *knowledge* to them. I'll consider that the greatest *devotion* to me.

And he said, such a person is dear to me not only now, but this will never change. It's not that right now I'm telling you this, but in the future it may be something different. It will hold true throughout history: whoever spreads his teacher's *knowledge* is the greatest devotee, and that is the greatest Guru Dakshina one can give to his teacher.

Now, let's say you consider that you are not capable of spreading this *knowledge* -- you don't have the resources, you don't have the temperament, you don't consider yourself worthy of doing so. But if you just listen to this: Adhyeshyate Cha Imam Dharmyam Samvadam Avayoho. This dialogue of ours, this sacred dialogue which deals with who you are in reality and who you are not, how to act in this world so that you can achieve your ultimate goal.

This dialogue which we had, which is sacred, even if you just study that listening is slightly different than studying one who studies this.
snippets.reflection:
These verses address studying and listening to the Gita. Verse 70: one who studies this dharmya-samvada (sacred dialogue) worships through jnana-yajna (knowledge-sacrifice). Verse 71: even one who merely listens with shraddha (faith) and without anasuya (fault-finding) becomes liberated and reaches the auspicious worlds of the righteous. Verse 72 is Krishna's final question to Arjuna: Have you listened with one-pointed mind? Has your delusion born of ignorance been destroyed?

The distinction between studying and listening is significant. Studying is active engagement - reading, contemplating, discussing. Listening is receptive - allowing the teaching to enter without immediate analysis or judgment. Both are valid paths. The key qualifier for listening is shraddha (faith) and absence of anasuya (carping criticism). Coming to spiritual teachings looking for flaws prevents any transmission. Coming with openness allows transformation.

How do you engage with spiritual teachings? Are you a student - actively working with the material, questioning, applying? Or a listener - receptively allowing wisdom to seep in? Both have value. Today, try the approach less natural to you. If you typically analyze, simply listen without judgment. If you typically receive passively, actively wrestle with one teaching. And honestly ask yourself Krishna's question: Has your ignorance-born delusion been dispelled? If confusion remains, that is honest and workable. But if there is pretense of understanding without genuine transformation, that is the real obstacle.
snippets.shortReflection: Have your doubts actually been answered, or are you just pretending you understand? It's okay to still be confused. What's not okay is performing clarity while staying stuck in the same patterns.

snippets.title: Day 238: Delusion Destroyed, Clarity Born
